News.title: Policewoman accused of selling sex on sugar daddy website probed over alleged £10k blackmail plot against married client
News.content:
COP FOR HIRE Policewoman accused of selling sex on sugar daddy website probed over alleged £10k blackmail plot against married client







Next

A POLICEWOMAN sold ­herself for sex on the Sugar Daddy Meet UK site, The Sun on Sunday can reveal.

The officer, said to have charged £500 an hour for romps, is under investigation for allegedly then demanding £10,000 from one client to stop her telling his wife about their trysts.

It is claimed the man paid up, but the Met Police PC, who is dark-haired and in her 30s, is said to have turned up at his home anyway and informed the wife about their encounters.

A source said the man subsequently reported her to the police, and a criminal investigation was launched.





The policewoman, who cannot be named for legal reasons, was based in North West London.

She left the force last month.

Thames Valley Police are conducting the probe into allegations of demanding money with menaces.

The force and Crown Prosecution Service declined to comment but it is understood no charges have been brought at this stage.

Sources confirmed the woman advertised herself on the Sugar Daddy website.

It claims to be “committed to providing a safe and efficient platform for sugar babies & sugar daddies in the UK to explore potential sugar relationships built on mutual respect, honesty, and shared interests”.

However, there are several warnings on the Trustpilot consumers’ review site that claim the platform is “full of fake accounts and scammers”.

One source said of the female cop alleged blackmail case: “The ­allegations are shocking. She had apparently advertised herself for sex to men she met through the site.



“One man met her several times and she apparently ­discovered that he is married.

“She is supposed to have demanded that he hand over £10,000 to her or she would tell his wife all about their arrangement.

“The guy apparently paid up but she still told his wife anyway.

“It is said to have destroyed the man’s life and he reported what happened to police.’’

News.title: Furious Zelensky accuses Trump of ‘rewarding’ Putin by lifting Russia sanctions as deadly strikes hit Ukraine
News.content:
Next

LIVID Volodymyr Zelensky says Donald Trump has “rewarded” Vladimir Putin by axing sanctions.

The moves targeting Russian goods and energy were halted 48 hours before they were to come into effect.



Ukraine’s President Mr Zelensky fumed that lifting the restrictions would leave Russian despot Mr Putin feeling “joy that there is such support”.

He added: “A US sanctions blackout, easing pressure on the aggressor, financial rewards for Putin — all of this only encourages him to keep attacking.”



His remarks came after seven people were killed in a Russian blitz on Ukrainian energy infrastructure and homes in cities such as Zaporizhzhia.

Mr Trump said halting the sanctions was in the US national interest.

Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev called it a “truly historic moment”.

The US earlier agreed to buy diesel from Russia.

French president Emmanuel Macron slammed the diesel deal between the US and Russia as sending a “negative” signal.

He said: “This decision is not good for anyone.



“It sends a negative signal.

“It adds an element of division and doubt.”

News.title: Louts face £100 fines for vaping, littering and threatening behaviour on buses in new government crackdown
News.content:
Next

LOUTS who vape and drop rubbish on buses will be fined £100 in a new crackdown.

Ministers will this week announce a blitz on anti-social behaviour by transport users.



Councils will be given new powers to fine people who vape, drop rubbish or carry out threatening behaviour on buses in their area.

A Whitehall source told The Sun on Sunday: “The Government knows that anti-social behaviour is a nightmare for people who experience it.



“So they are planning a crackdown to show they are on the public’s side.”

It comes as stats show 41 per cent of Brits experienced or saw anti-social behaviour in the past year, according to the latest Crime Survey for England and Wales.



That was a rise of six per cent from a year before.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has already vowed to crack down on vape shops blighting Britain’s “hollowed-out high streets”.

Earlier this summer he said residents will get a say about what shops can open in their towns in a bid to stop them being overrun by vape outlets.

Ex-Deputy PM Angela Rayner was seen smoking a vape while on a kayak last year near Brighton.



A new vape ban will come into force across the UK in just under a fortnight.

It comes as the government is continuing its crackdown on the devices.

Come October 29, vape vending machines will no longer be allowed to operate across the UK.



The updated rules mean it will be an offence for all businesses, such as a pub, to have one of these machines on their premises.

News.title: Major red alert issued as horror floods and torrential rain devastate Spain with cars swept away in Brit hols hotspots
News.content:
Next

A MAJOR red alert has been issued as horror floods and torrential rain devastate Spain with cars swept away in Brit holiday hotspots.

Raging torrents have wreaked havoc across Barcelona and Almeria – engulfing entire streets in water and swamping homes in gushing floods.



Storm Adam rampaged along the Mediterranean coast on Saturday, leaving a trail of destruction and sparking fears of further flooding.

Residents have been trapped in stranded cars and basements flooded with water as biblical downpours lashed Barcelona and Almeria.



In one shocking video a black car drifts backwards down a gushing brown stream through a central road in El Ejido.

More horrifying clips show torrents of muddy floodwater sending basements underwater and engulfing swamped streets.



More than 100 litres per square metre drenched the worst-hit El Ejido-Norte neighbourhood in Almeria while over 75 litres per square metres poured down on Cañada Cortés and Venta Vieja.

The Andalusian authorities raised its flood risk plans to the highest emergency level as red alerts flashed along Spain’s southern coast.



Emergency services recieved more than 100 calls – mostly from people trapped inside cars caught in the deluge.

Multiple roads were shut down as rains lashed the streets and turned the city centre into a network of gushing rivers.

No one has so far been injured or killed in the sudden flash floods.

From 10am on Sunday Costa Blanca will be under a rare “danger to life” warning – and it is set to last until 10am on Monday.

State weather forecaster Aemet said: “The meteorological danger is extraordinary.



“Vulnerable people and property in exposed areas could suffer very serious or catastrophic impacts.”

Text alerts pinged across phones in Valencia on Saturday afternoon as the government urged residents to stay indoors.

Frightening rainfall of between 200mm to 700mm is forecast for just 12 hours in the region, according to Aemet.

All parks, gardens, libraries and cemeteries have been closed and football matches and concerts cancelled to prepare for the oncoming onslaught.

Some weather models suggested a low chance of a hurricane forming over the Mediterranean sea.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Residents have been urged to avoid all non-essential travel and to steer clear of dry riverbeds and from crossing flooded areas.

The horror downpours come two years after mass flash floods in Valencia killed 242 people.

News.title: Child & adult dead after pickup truck ploughs into players and fans on football field in horror ‘mass casualty’ event
News.content:
FIELD TRAGEDY Child & adult dead after pickup truck ploughs into players and fans on football field in horror ‘mass casualty’ event







Next

A CHILD and an adult have been killed after a truck ploughed into players and fans at a youth football match in Kansas.

Emergency services raced to Stryker Sports Complex for what police described as a “mass casualty” event.



The terrifying incident unfolded at around 3.25pm.

Several people were struck by the truck and have been rushed to hospital, according to Wichita Police Capt. Aaron Moses.



The extent of the injuries sustained remains unconfirmed, but police have confirmed two fatalities.

Names and ages of the victims have not been revealed.

read more FATAL SHOOTING Man shot & killed at New York subway station as suspect seen fleeing in mask

One witness told 12 News that a “black pickup truck came plowing through the youth soccer fields hitting multiple people before stopping 100-200 yards down the fields”.

Police captain Moses said that at this time it is unclear how fast the truck was going or how it got onto the field.

It is understood the driver has been detained with officials insisting there is no further danger to the public.

A Wichita Police spokesperson said: “The vehicle involved in this incident remained at the scene.



“The driver of that vehicle is currently in our custody.”

There were two juveniles understood to be inside the vehicle when the incident occurred, according to police captain Moses.

Horrified bystanders made multiple 911 calls at around 3.25pm – triggering a mass emergency response including police, firefighters and other law enforcement officials to race to the playing fields.

Witness accounts suggest the truck travelled a considerable away across the field before finally stopping.

Authorities are yet to revealed whether the tragic incident was deliberate or accidental.



It comes just weeks after a teenage driver ploughed into a crowd of rugby fans in Australia.

The horrific crash in Newcastle left 10 people injured including a five-year-old who was put in a coma and a 67-year-old man who was left fighting for his life.

A dozen ambulances and three air ambulances rushed to the scene when the 18-year-old rammed into the mass of supporters lining the streets.

Around 1,000 Newcastle Knights rugby league team fans had gathered as the teams coach set off when the incident occurred.

Knights fan Chris Clancy, 48, was among those injured, suffering a broken left collarbone, a fractured right foot, broken ribs and several small spinal fractures.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Chris told the Sydney Morning Herald he thought he was “going to die”.

He said: “No-one had time to move, it happened so fast.”

News.title: Transgender rapist claims to be victim of bullying in men’s prison after being jailed for horrific park attack
News.content:
SEX ATTACKER Transgender rapist claims to be victim of bullying in men’s prison after being jailed for horrific park attack







Next

A RAPIST who now identifies as a woman is complaining about being a “victim” and getting bullied in prison.

Alexander Secker left his rape victim traumatised in a park before switching genders, calling himself Lexi and being jailed for 6½ years.

The 37-year-old is now deputy chair of a gay rights group at Ashfield men’s prison in Bristol.

And Secker — caged in 2024 for the drunken attack in Blunsdon, Wilts — claims guards ignore transphobic bullying.





The rapist wrote in a lags’ mag: “Transphobic and homophobic attitudes are rampant.

“We’ve requested staff undergo much-needed training around LGBTQIA+ issues.”

But a prison spokesman insisted: “We don’t recognise these claims.

“HMP Ashfield is proud of its inclusive environment and has a significant transgender prisoner population who are welcomed and supported.



“We hold monthly forums for each protected characteristic, and we are not aware of any complaints relating to discrimination.”

Judge Jason Taylor KC sentenced Secker to six and a half years in a male prison as he was living as a man when the offence was committed.

The judge said: “I am sure you hatched a plan to be alone with her.

“You suggested you take her for a walk under the pretence of sobering up. You took her to a secluded spot in the woods.”

News.title: Katie Zacharia felt tap on shoulder mid-interview from top Trump aide saying ‘JD wants to chat’ before brutal firing
News.content:
Next

KATIE Zacharia felt a tap on her shoulder mid-interview – minutes before her brutal firing five days into the job.

A top White House aide told Zacharia “JD wants to chat” before whisking her out of the press office – never to return.



The White House press secretary was speaking to Wall Street Journal (WSJ) reporters when she was rudely interrupted.

Jason Miller, a senior advisor to Donald Trump, walked into the press powow to tell Zacharia: “JD wanted to chat with us real quick.”



She excused herself and left the office – but never came back, according to the WSJ journalists.

Minutes later, Trump told hordes of reporters that he questioned whether being a press secretary was the right role for Zacharia.

In a fresh humiliation he recounted a conversation in which he told her: “Is this for you Katie? Because honestly, you don’t need this.”

He added: “You don’t have to do this if you don’t want to… honestly if I were you I’d reconsider.”

Asked if he had confidence in her, Trump damningly replied: “I don’t know. We’ll see. I’m gonna let her make that decision.”

The shock exit came just three days after Zacharia made her first disastrous appearance as press secretary.



She stumbled through her scripted 14-minute debut before flubbing a question on Ukraine and accidentally announcing an unconfirmed dismissal.

Behind the scenes, Trump’s ice maiden Susie Wiles is said to have sounded the death knell and dealt the final blow.

On Thursday Zacharia was thrown into an interview with Sean Hannity on Fox News in what insiders told Politico was a “sanctioned hit”.



She was grilled over her credentials after it emerged that she had failed her bar exam and her shoddy performance in the press pit.

Nonetheless, the mum-of-four was reportedly oblivious to the plot to see her booted.

She told WSJ reporters on Friday – just minutes before she was fired – that there were “no staffing changes that are happening”.

Trying to explain away her shambolic first briefing, she said she’d only had 24 hours to prepare.

Speaking to the Wall Street Journal, she said: “The truth is that I have a hard time saying ‘no’ because I want to be a team player” before hastily adding that she was not accusing the White House of rushing her.



The frazzled former press sec also confessed that she was running on “no sleep and high adrenaline and probably too much caffeine and no food”.

One former Trump official described her as an “overwhelmed substitute teacher” while conservative commentator Candace Owens blasted her for reading everything off a script “including her own name”.

After her public dismissal, the mom of four took to Instagram to mark the end of her record-breaking tenure.

“President Trump is a kind, wonderful, gracious, thoughtful, enthusiastic, and the most hardworking man,” she wrote in the caption alongside a picture of herself and the president.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I wish more Americans appreciated him. No one will ever make America great the way he has and continues to.



“It was an honor to work for him.”

News.title: Black cab rapist John Worboys ‘delighted’ over possible move to secure hospital after personality disorder diagnosis
News.content:
Next

BLACK cab rapist John Worboys is celebrating after being told he may be leaving jail for a secure hospital, we can reveal.

Evil Worboys, 69, is on a “pathway” to a facility such as Broadmoor after experts ruled he has a personality disorder.



He has already been moved from Wakefield to the Westgate Unit at HMP Frankland, Co. Durham.

A source said: “The unit was set up to treat inmates with complex psychological issues.



“Although it holds dangerous people and killers, it is more of a hospital environment and is like a prison within a prison.

“Worboys is cock-a-hoop.



“He knows he’s on a pathway towards a potential move to a secure hospital because of his diagnosis.

“And while he hopes to be freed, he knows that life there would be much easier than in a high-security jail.”

Ex-London cabbie Worboys is serving life for attacking 16 women.

Police believe there may be more than 100 victims.



He was refused parole in May on the grounds he posed a “high risk” of reoffending.

The Ministry of Justice said it did not comment on individual prisoners.

News.title: Man City charges LIVE: Points deduction size emerges as Premier League rivals 'fuming'
News.content:
Football finance expert Kieran Maguire has claimed Manchester City must be deduced "multiple double figures of points" after breaching Premier League financial rules.

Maguire said: "The redacted report sets out year by year how much the sham contracts contributed to the artificial commercial revenue. Over the rolling three-year period, in some years we could be talking about a £350million difference. That would shatter all records for PSR compliance.

"Everton and Nottingham Forest's deductions covered a single breach in a single year, an overspend of no more than £20million. So is there a ceiling on what can be deducted? And the sanctions hearing could already have taken place. Because City are appealing and everyone has NDAs, we might not know the sanction until the appeal result. But it has to be multiple double figures of points, before you start the calculations.

"I worked out that if you add up nine years of Champions League non-participation for individual clubs at an average of £50million a time, around £20million for the Europa League, plus potential claims from players who missed bonuses, the Premier League's legal fees and a fine, we're talking in excess of a billion pounds regardless of the points deduction.

When asked about the possibility of City being kicked out of the Premier League, Maguire responded: "I think it would be a very unusual vote. We did see Bury get expelled from League Two some time ago but I think that the other clubs would have to bear in mind that Manchester City would probably take legal redress and that could prove to be very expensive if they are expelled without the verdict being held and without the appeal. So it's a risky path to tread, but the strength of feeling does vary from club to club.

"Certainly some of the other elite clubs are very unhappy with the delay in the situation because they feel it has an impact upon their ability to qualify for the Champions League. I think some of the more mid-tier clubs who don't see Manchester City as a threat, their main concern is, is this going to further increase the already sky-high legal costs that have been incurred by the Premier League and they don't want any part of it.

"So, they want a quick resolution and then they can get on with the rest of their season and focus on their own clubs."

News.title: Flying instructor, 80, who died in plane crash with boy, 16 pictured
News.content:
Flying instructor, 80, who died in plane crash with boy, 16 pictured

Ian Haggis was sadly pronounced dead at the scene of the crash near Drymen, Stirlingshire, alongside a teenage student

View Image Ian Haggis, 80, lost his life alongside a 16-year-old student (Image: Facebook)

A flying instructor who died alongside a teen student after their aircraft plummeted and crashed has been identified and pictured for the first time.

‌



‌



On Friday, emergency services swarmed a remote field near Drymen, Stirlingshire, shortly before 4.45pm to reports of a plane crash.

‌



Sadly, an 80-year-old man and a 16-year-old boy were declared dead at the scene.

‌



It has now been confirmed the flying instructor, Ian Haggis, was the victim. Known fondly as Flying Haggis, it is understood he was an experienced commercial pilot and was reportedly in charge of the Pipe Tomahawk II.

The light aircraft is understood to have departed Cumbernauld Airport in Lanarkshire at 11.46am on Friday before travelling to Glasgow Airport. Transmissions stopped at around 4.37pm.

The identity of the 16-year-old student remains unknown. It is thought he may have been taking a flying lesson, the Daily Record reports.

‌



Tributes have since been pouring in for the instructor. A close friend, Joseph Thompson, wrote on Facebook: “My good friend and instructor Ian Haggis was killed yesterday in an air accident, my heart goes to his family.”

The Air Accidents Investigation Branch (AAIB) has launched a probe. In a statement, the AAIB said: “An investigation has begun into an accident involving a light aircraft which occurred on October 16, 2026.

“A team has travelled to the accident site near Drymen to make inquiries and gather evidence as part of the process of conducting an investigation.”

‌



After leaving Cumbernauld Airport towards Glasgow, flight-tracking data suggests the aircraft headed north-east towards Newport-on-Tay in Fife before returning to Glasgow, where it remained on the ground for just over an hour.

It took off from Glasgow at 4.17pm and was heading towards the Loch Lomond and Drymen area when its transmissions stopped at 4.37pm, a few miles north-east of the village.

The aircraft, which is around 45 years old, was bought from a Liverpool company in April and is understood to be registered to Leading Edge Flight Training Ltd. The firm, which operates from Glasgow and Cumbernauld airports, offers trial flying lessons, introductory flights and advanced training.

‌



A cordon was erected near Old Drymen Road, with officers seen heading towards the hillside where the aircraft is believed to have crashed.

A tarpaulin was draped over the aircraft’s canopy at the scene.

Gavin Birch-Williams, managing director of Glasgow Airport, said: “This is a deeply tragic event and the thoughts and sympathies from all at Glasgow Airport are with the friends and families affected.”

Article continues below

Temporary airspace restrictions have been imposed over the Drymen area.

News.title: Nigel Farage's fresh crisis as aspiring Reform MP calls for 'concentration camps' in Britain
News.content:
Nigel Farage's fresh crisis as aspiring Reform MP calls for 'concentration camps' in Britain

An undercover sting by ITV shows a Reform councillor saying he wants to 'machine gun' grooming gang perpetrators, and an aspiring MP calling for 'concentration camps' in Britain

View 2 Images Nigel Farage was accused of 'sitting on his hands' (Image: Gary Oakley/PA Wire)

Nigel Farage has been plunged into yet another crisis after fresh allegations of racism and bigotry in Reform.

‌



‌



An undercover sting by ITV shows a prominent member of Reform’s Board saying “I was racist every single day” at school, a Reform councillor saying he wants to “machine gun” grooming gang perpetrators, and an aspiring MP calling for “concentration camps” in Britain.

‌



Mr Farage had vowed to kick out the “bad apples” and professionalise the party, but has now been accused of “sitting on his hands” as the allegations soar.

‌



The footage shows Reform’s Board member Gawain Towler, saying “I was racist every single day against a friend.. I was racist every single day.”

Mr Towler told ITV that as a child he held views that were wrong and he is appalled by them now.

Robert Jenrick tied in knots after being accused of 'deflecting' Reform row questions READ MORE :

View 2 Images Nigel Farage previously vowed to kick out the 'bad apples' in Reform (Image: Gareth Fuller/PA Wire)

‌



Footage also shows two Reform councillors, Adam Parkins and David Kerr from Hounslow in West London, saying the party will get more “hard line” if they get in power.

Mr Parkins said he would “quite happily do Sunday morning Rose Garden executions” for grooming gang perpetrators, while Mr Kerr, discussing how he'd reverse immigration, said “there's no way you're going to be able to even discuss a tenable solution without being called a f***ing Nazi.”

Councillor Kerr did not respond to request for comment, while Councillor Parkins said Reform policy is grooming gangs should face the toughest possible sentences under British law, and that is his view.

‌



The footage also shows aspiring Reform MP Jason Powell saying he had passed vetting checks, then saying the party should “build concentration camps” for anyone who comes to Britain across the Channel. He also said “you cannot be a Muslim and British.”

Mr Powell told ITV his views are those of British people in general and are not extremist.

Responding to the allegations, Bridget Phillipson MP, Chair of the Labour Party, said: “Bad apples don’t fall far from the tree. The sleaze, scandals and appalling revelations of racism and rank misogyny piling up by the day go right to the top of Reform UK. Nigel Farage is incapable of taking responsibility and getting his house in order because he himself shares culpability.

‌



“Farage has sat on his hands and desperately tried to deflect over and over again because he’s completely unfit to lead. The more and more the public see the true face of Nigel Farage and Reform UK, the more it becomes clear they’re completely unfit for office.”

In a statement Reform said: “Not all individuals covertly recorded by ITV are members of Reform UK. Where members, activists and councillors have clearly behaved inappropriately, investigations have commenced. In some cases, there have been suspensions and due process must be followed.

“Reform UK has improved and prioritised its vetting procedures, but from time to time, a handful of individuals who do not share our values will initially make it through vetting. This is the same for all organisations. However good the vetting, one cannot vet a future comment.

Article continues below

“There is no room for racism in Reform UK. We always respect due process of investigations and whilst these are ongoing it would not be appropriate to comment on individual cases.”

The accusations are among those set to feature in 90-minute film Undercover: A Year In Reform, Sunday 18th October at 10.20pm on ITV1, ITVX, STV & STV Player.

News.title: Bedford train crash hero doctor says 'aftermath was like a war zone'
News.content:
Bedford train crash hero doctor says 'aftermath was like a war zone'

When the train she was on near Bedford crashed, Dr Eli ignored her own injuries to help others around her. She will receive a Special Recognition award at Pride of Britain in honour of her selfless, lifesaving action

Train crash doctor who saved lives wins Pride of Britain Award

Seconds after a terrifying train crash, which killed the driver and left 162 injured, passenger Eleanor Prior could only hear an eerie silence. The GP and mum of two was sitting in the front carriage of the train, on her way to a friend’s 40th birthday in London, when it ploughed into a stationary train at around 50mph near Bedford in June.

‌



‌



The force of the impact threw Dr Eleanor, known as Eli, around eight metres down the aisle, leaving her with multiple injuries. She says: “I remember seeing smoke and it was very quiet, with everything happening in slow motion. There was smashed glass and blood everywhere. It was like a war zone.

‌



“I rang 999 and yelled, ‘Bring everything, there’s been a train crash’. That’s when the noise started, the crying and screaming.”

‌



Eli dragged herself towards the doors as everyone tried to escape the smoke-filled carriage, but she realised that she had to stay and help the wounded.

View 7 Images Dr. Eli Prior pictured at home in Bedfordshire (Image: Philip Coburn/Daily Mirror)

She was one of the first to call 999, then worked alongside emergency services to triage passengers and even refused an ambulance for herself, insisting it went to someone else.

‌



The 41-year-old, from Bedford, will win a Daily Mirror Pride of Britain Award at our star-studded celebration, which honours the nation's unsung heroes. She will receive a Special Recognition award at the event in partnership with P&O Cruises, in honour of her selfless, lifesaving action, despite her own injuries.

It was June 19th when Eli, who lives with husband Chris and daughters Annie, four, and Lottie, three, left for her evening out. Speaking for the first time, Eli says: “I was meeting three of my best friends. The ticket officer suggested I get the next train as it was busy, but I didn’t want to be late.”

Eli then chose a seat with nothing opposite, a last-minute decision she calls “a miracle” that saved her from worse injuries.

‌



View 7 Images Investigators and police officers at the scene where two East Midlands Railway trains collided near Bedford on 19 June 2026 (Image: TOLGA AKMEN/EPA/Shutterstock)

She recalls: “I was typing on my phone. The next thing I’d travelled about eight metres. I’m not sure if I lost consciousness, but I hit my head. As I came to, my phone was somehow still in my hand. It was strangely quiet. I stumbled back to the doors.

“I called 999. They kept asking what service I wanted and I was just shouting, ‘F***ing everything, bring everything!’ I called Chris and said, ‘I’ve been in a train crash’.

‌



“I remember feeling like I was going to pass out. I think I was hyperventilating. There was a girl who was shell shocked and we were just staring at each other.

“Then two men managed to force open the doors. People started getting off the train if they could, crossing the track to the field. I remember thinking I should get off. Then I turned around and saw a woman lying on the floor. I thought, ‘God, no, I can’t get off the train. Look at these people.’”

View 7 Images Dr Eli's quick thinking and bravery saved lives (Image: Philip Coburn/Daily Mirror)

‌



Chris, 40, a teacher, vividly remembers that first phone call. He says: “As soon as you hear ‘train crash’, you think, ‘That’s hugely destructive’. She was sobbing, then she had to go.

“When she next called I could hear wailing and screaming in the background. She was frantic. I thought ‘Oh my God, is she going to die? Are there dead people on the train? What is happening?’

“Then she didn’t pick up the phone for ages. Your mind is racing with the absolute worst ‘what ifs’.

‌



“I thought either she’s dead or she’s helping people. I knew she wouldn’t get off that train if someone else was hurt. When we finally spoke, she said, ‘I’ve got to stay here’. She was talking to the people around her. She’d gone into responsibility mode.”

View 7 Images Dr Rob Willmore, from Essex & Herts Air Ambulance

Train driver Shaun Burton, 60, died in the crash, which happened at around 5.15pm at Elstow, about 2.5 miles south of Bedford Station. On the train, Eli was faced with passengers who had some of the worst injuries.

‌



Eli recalls: “The woman lying on the floor whispered, ‘I can't feel my legs.’ She was in horrendous pain and struggling to breathe. I knew it was a spinal injury.

“Another woman was screaming. All the skin had come off her face and I could see her skull. Another lady had broken both legs, they were bleeding. Lots of people were vocally in pain, but I was most worried about the quiet ones. I was worried they would die.”

Passenger Melanie Ross, a retired solicitor from Wellingborough, Northants, who broke her leg, says: “It was pandemonium, people were hysterical. Straight away I saw Eli on the phone, distinctive in her green dress. She looked very shaken and had clearly been thrown out of her seat.

‌



View 7 Images Eli Prior, husband Chris Prior, and daughters Annie, four, and Lottie, three

“She stood up and shouted, ‘My name’s Eli, I’m a doctor’. Then she sprang into action. If it hadn’t been for Eli, people would have died.”

Eli says: “I find sirens really traumatic now because I remember holding people’s hands, tears rolling down my face, saying, ‘I can hear sirens. They’re coming to help us. Keep breathing, you’re fine.’”

‌



Millie Dudley, 21, a firefighter from Bedford Fire and Rescue Service, says: “As soon as I got on the train I saw Eli. She said, ‘I am a little bit injured, but I’m here to help.’ She didn’t think about herself despite going through that same thing, it was just amazing.”

It was only at this point that Eli realised her hand was injured as she couldn't tie a tourniquet. However, she stayed with the injured, administering oxygen and pain relief, and helped a woman onto a spinal board. She also spoke to relatives who were calling passengers’ phones.

View 7 Images Millie Dudley, a 21-year-old firefighter from Bedford Fire and Rescue Service, had only been in the job 18 months and was one of the first on the scene at Bedford train crash

‌



Eli says: “I was one of the last people off the train. I was trying to manage things for about three hours.

“Outside, I realised that my back was horrendously bruised. I had a suspected broken foot but managed to walk across the field and asked if my husband could just pick me up.”

Chris recalls: “She was covered in cuts and her jacket was caked in blood, most of it not hers. I just burst into tears. In the car she cried and said everything hurt. She was holding face in her hands saying how awful it was.

‌



“That’s when she realised, ‘I can’t deal with this’. She became Eli again, not the doctor.” Chris took her to Bedford Hospital and she was later discharged after X-rays and an ultrasound to check for internal bleeding.

The Rail Accident Investigation Branch reports that the train passed a red light at 76mph, braking only seconds before the collision. The stationary train had stopped after the Automatic Warning System activated its brakes.

View 7 Images The Rail Accident Investigation Branch reports that the train passed a red light at 76mph (Image: Bav Media)

‌



Eli has since had operations for her broken right (dominant) hand, which needed a plate and five screws, and treatment for her foot, knee and back, and still has no grip in her fingers, though she has recently managed to return to work.

The Fire Service and passengers reached out on social media looking for ‘the woman with the blonde hair in the green dress’ to thank her. Eli says: “My whole body hurt. It felt like I was in a train crash, literally. I’m still in a lot of pain and seeing a psychologist for the trauma.

“It now feels like there's life ‘before the train crash’ and ‘after the train crash’. I need to get rid of that feeling.”

‌



Chris adds: “I told our little girls that Mummy’s train had crashed. They said, ‘Oh it’s good that Mummy was on the train because she’s a doctor’. All I wanted was for her to get off the train, but she couldn’t. She cares deeply about people. She sees a problem, she tries to help.

“It could have been very, very different. But there’s a reason she ended up on that train and that she was able to help other people.”

Dr Rob Willmore, from Essex & Herts Air Ambulance wrote to Eli: “Thank you for everything you did that day. You were absolutely extraordinary. The kindness and bravery you showed was humbling - your calmness and humanity made a world of difference.”
