News.title: Trump's wild week as he sacks top aide after five days and alarm bells ring about midterms rigging
News.content:
Trump's wild week as he sacks top aide after five days and alarm bells ring about midterms rigging

In any normal week, Katie Zacharia's disastrous first briefing would be the top of this list - but events move fast in Trumpworld. Here's a roundup of what you need to know this week

View Image Trump with 5-day press secretary Katie Zacharia (Image: X/ @KatieZacharia)

It's just weeks until the midterm elections and Donald Trump is doing the things he does before an election.

‌



‌



He's holding rallies to dwindling numbers of people in States where his party should be winning but isn't. Oh, and he's laying the groundwork for rigging the election if it looks like he's going to lose. Meanwhile he's had to sack his new press secretary just five days into the job. And he's been accused of betraying Ukraine by relaxing even more sanctions on Russia. Here's everything that's happened this week in Trumpworld that you need to know about. Buckle up.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

‌



For more of our coverage of Trump's America: Subscribe to The Trump Update on YouTube

Subscribe to the US Dispatch - our weekly newsletter exclusively for Mirror+ readers - following all the gossip and intrigue from Trump's DC swamp

- following all the gossip and intrigue from Trump's DC swamp Follow Mikey Smith on Twitter, TikTok, Bluesky or Facebook.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Katie Zacharia lasted half a Scaramucci

In any normal week, I'd be starting this roundup with Trump blindsiding everyone - including Chief of Staff Susie Wiles - by appointing Katie Zacharia as his new Press Secretary on Monday. And then maybe a rundown of her disastrous debut hosting the White House Press Briefing, which lasted 13 minutes, five of which she spent taking questions from just three people and still managed to commit an excruciating gaffe.

‌



Even worse than her stilted, mumbling, head-down delivery of an opening monologue of the President's "wins" was the moment when she mistakenly referred to her husband as "my president". A flub that would surely have prompted an awkward conversation with said husband, who she explained was making preparations to move from California to DC to support her in her new role. Well, hopefully they didn't, you know, buy or sell property or anything. Because just four days after said disaster briefing, Trump sacked her. And not just over the briefing.

See, Katie Zacharia has, for some time, described herself in public as a lawyer and/or as an attorney. So, not unreasonably, people started asking in which state she took the bar exam - perhaps aware that she made an attempt at it in California in 2011, and failed. Asked about it outside the White House, she mumbled something about "when I was in China." Which is a weird answer to that question. She did live in China for a spell after she left college, got married and failed the California bar exam. She even worked at a law firm. But a qualified lawyer she was not. In fact, in China you have to be a citizen to take the bar exam. Katie denied having misled anyone about her credentials - though Trump's face when she was asked the question did not suggest he knew beforehand.

‌



After that, it was all somehow downhill. She appeared on Sean Hannity's Fox News show to defend herself...and what she clearly thought would be a softball interview turned into a pretty stern grilling on her past and performance from the TV host who is in Trump's ear the most. Then she went on Fox and Friends, and it was a similar kind of car crash.

So on Friday afternoon, when Trump was departing for a rally in Georgia, he told reporters he had had a chat with Zacharia and suggested, perhaps, the job was "not for her" and she'd be "transitioned" to another part of the administration. Whether this conversation actually took place is unconfirmed...but the message was clear. She was out and he was moving on.

And today's latest is that the interview with Hannity that sealed her fate...was set up by Wiles, and has been described as a "sanctioned hit." This, under any normal administration would be seen as a hack move by a Chief of Staff who wanted to throw someone under a bus. But in Trump 2.0 Wiles looks like a galaxy brain, Malcolm Tucker-level political operator.

‌



Trump betrays Ukraine

In a far more depressing turn of events, Trump's journey to Putin's way of thinking appears to be complete. Since the Russian hardman's birthday last week, when Trump made a point of calling his bestie on the phone, the US President has been in a downward spiral of unthinkable acts.

It started with the diesel deal, presumably a birthday present for Putin, which saw Trump relax sanctions to allow Russia to pump its fuel into American tractors. And last night Trump signed an executive order suspending yet more sanctions - which he signed into law just a month ago at the behest of late Senator Lindsay Graham. Trump said scrapping the sanctions was in the US "national interest". But the lurch to Putin's side and apparent betrayal of Ukraine has prompted a bipartisan backlash from US lawmakers - many of whom are facing re-election battles in less than three weeks' time.

Meanwhile, in an even darker turn of events, Starshield - the satellite internet service Ukraine relies upon for defensive intelligence and drone control - has apparently been limited, putting lives under threat. Reuters reported the limitation was deliberate, and was ordered from inside the Trump administration - though both Trump and Elon Musk - on whose Starlink service the system is built - have denied involvement.

‌



The midterms are looming - and the threats have begun

Trump has been on the campaign trail, holding rallies almost every night to try and prevent a complete blowout in the looming midterm elections. All 435 seats in the House, 34 Senate seats and 36 governors mansions are up for grabs across the country - and the Republican Party is braced to suffer heavy losses.

Statewide polls put Democrats ahead in enough states to hand them control of both the House and Senate - with even Republican strongholds like Texas looking likely to turn blue on November 3. Which means Trump has been giving lengthy, meandering speeches in states like Georgia, Texas, Kentucky and Michigan in a bid to try and energise his base. "Pretend I'm on the ballot," is his most oft-repeated refrain - but with recent polls putting his approval as low as 22%, that may do more harm than good.

And the results aren't the only thing to be watching in this set of elections. Yesterday, three Democratic senators felt they compelled to write to Attorney General Todd Blanche, to ask for a commitment that he won't seize ballots or any other election materials before the votes have been concluded and the results certified.

‌



The letter from Sens. Alex Padilla, (California), Sheldon Whitehouse (Rhode Island) and Dick Durbin (Illinois), argued any such actions would constitute unlawful election interference by the Justice Department. The letter comes against a backdrop of escalating threats by the DOJ to election officials who don’t comply with its demands.

On Thursday, the DOJ sued California election officials, alleging they didn’t act quickly enough to review names the federal government identified as “likely” noncitizens. And Trump posted on Friday night threatening to jail election officials if they don't comply. The Justice Department seized 2020 ballots from Georgia’s Fulton County earlier this year, saying it was investigating “irregularities.” Georgia’s votes in that presidential race were counted three times and affirmed Democrat Joe Biden’s win

Oh, and here's Kid Rock being racist

In Michigan, the Democrats have selected a man named Abdul El-Sayed as their candidate for the vacant Senate seat. He's known by most as a Michigan-born progressive left-leaning, very charismatic epidemiologist. To Trump's ol' buddy Kid Rock, he's a potential Islamic Terrorist. "The point I would like to make with especially El Sayed is that we need to be very careful," Rock said on Fox News. "...with these ideologies that I don't believe are compatible with western civilisation. It appears that that El Sayed is assimilated. You know what I mean? But I don't see him saying all the time like this is the greatest country and I love the opportunities it gave me. It's all this country is racist and this that and the other."

‌



El-Sayed is, once again, a native Michigander.

Rock went on: "And I would like to make the point that there's been some other people who have assimilated to this country. The Fort Hood shooter. Those men, those extremists that became pilots and and crashed into our World Trade Centers. And this is why I call him a wolf in sheep's clothing."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Article continues below

Trump has been doing some dog-whistling of his own, deliberately misnaming the Democrat as "Mohammed El Sayed". It's unclear if he was aware El Sayed's middle name was Mohamed when he repeatedly made the comments over the last week. And responding to the backlash to his taunts, Trump said in Georgia on Friday night: "I don't care. I'm the President of the United States, I can call you whatever the hell I want." He went on to say: "His name is actually Abdullahalalalala baa ba ba Muhammad El-Sayed. So his middle name is Muhammad. I was right.. almost."

Stay classy.

News.title: Meghan Markle's 'furious' phone call about Kate blunder - 'You've embarrassed me!'
News.content:
Meghan Markle's 'furious' phone call about Kate blunder - 'You've embarrassed me!'

Meghan Markle was reportedly left furious after an embarrassing blunder involving a high-end fashion designer and her sister-in-law, Kate Middleton

View 3 Images The blunder involved Meghan's sister-in-law, the Princess of Wales (Image: Getty Images)

Meghan Markle was reportedly furious after an awkward blunder involving Kate Middleton. The Duchess of Sussex is said to have fallen out with high-end fashion designer, Roland Mouret, who had sent the former actress a handful of outfits after she started dating Prince Harry. The pair had been friends for some time.

‌



Roland, 65, asked a member of his team to send a selection of items he had personally set aside to Kensington Palace and instructed the staffer to "leave them there as long as she [Meghan] wants them." He also instructed the member of staff not to "follow up on it and do not talk about it to anyone at all, here or outside."

However, after Meghan and Harry's relationship became public, the staffer who sent the clothes "decided, in an honest attempt to be efficient, to call Kate's stylist at the palace and ask for Meghan’s dresses to be returned."

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google, make us your preferred source. Free and easy to do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

3 View 3 Images Meghan had been friends with Roland for some time (Image: WireImage) 3 View 3 Images The Duchess was reportedly left 'furious' (Image: Getty Images for TIME)

‌



In an excerpt of his memoir, I Am Roland Mouret: The Butcher's Boy Who Dressed The World, serialised by The Times, he claims the Duchess was "furious." Roland wrote: "Meghan was furious and called me." He went on to claim that she said: "You don't realise what you've done, you've embarrassed me!"

The designer apologised directly to Meghan, saying that he understood she wanted things handled "privately". However, she is alleged to have responded: "You know I can never wear your clothes again."

However, Roland was left baffled by the "logic of this," adding that Meghan's decision not to wear his brand again was hers, "not the palace's, not anybody else's, I don't think anyone else cared," he said.

‌



However, just a year later, he reached out to the Duchess after spotting her wearing what he claimed was "a cheap high street copy" of one of his designs. "I messaged her: ‘I can understand if you don't wear my stuff, but if it’' to wear a cheap copy then that's ridiculous. Come back,'" he said.

Meghan responded, via text message saying: "I think I should come and see you." Meghan and the Princess of Wales have had a strained relationship in recent years. During a bombshell interview with Oprah Winfry, the Duchess claims the then Duchess of Cambridge made her cry in the days leading up to her wedding, not the other way around, as was originally claimed.

During the 2021 interview, a year after she and Prince Harry stepped down as senior working royals, Meghan claimed that she and the Princess clashed over the dresses her flower girls, including Princess Charlotte, would wear.

"It made me cry, and it really hurt my feelings," she said. Meghan said, "There wasn't a confrontation. I don't think it's fair to her to get into the details because she apologised, and I've forgiven her.

"It was a really hard week of the wedding, and she was upset about something, but she owned it, and she apologised, and she brought me flowers and a note, apologising." She went on to say that Kate was "a good person".

The Mirror approached a spokesperson for the Duchess.

News.title: How day of protests unfolded as disorder breaks out across France
News.content:
An estimated 550,000 people took part in protests across France, demanding greater investment in education and action on the rising cost of living.

The demonstrations quickly descended into violence, with cars and buildings set alight and shops ransacked.

At least 1,200 people were arrested on Saturday as riot police deployed tear gas and water cannons to disperse crowds.

The unrest follows weeks of student-led protests, with demonstrators joining forces to express growing anger over economic conditions and French President Emmanuel Macron handling of the crisis.

In a social media post, Macron denounced the violence and said that vandals and looters will be "prosecuted and punished".

BBC correspondent Adina Campbell reports from Paris.

Video editor: Zahra Fatima

Read more about the day of protests across France.

News.title: More NHS staff sacked over attacks victims' records
News.content:
Further members of staff have been sacked by an NHS trust for inappropriately accessing medical records of the Nottingham attacks victims.

Nottingham students Barnaby Webber and Grace O'Malley-Kumar, and grandfather Ian Coates, were stabbed to death on 13 June 2023 by Valdo Calocane, who was diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia in 2020.

In May, Nottingham University Hospitals (NUH) NHS Trust confirmed it had dismissed 11 members of staff and, in an update on Friday, said a total of 15 people had now been sacked as part of its investigation.

Dr Sanjoy Kumar, Grace's father, said: "I am appalled, it's time to get a handle on these failures."

He added: "Clearly, the way that the highest confidential data, which is medical data, is being looked at by voyeuristic people in the NHS is disgraceful."

Dr Manjeet Shehmar, medical director at NUH, said: "There is simply no excuse for accessing the records of a patient without a legitimate reason and I hope this sends a really clear message â we will investigate and we will take action.

"To lose a loved one in the way that the families of Ian, Grace and Barnaby have is heartbreaking enough.

"I am so sorry that they have had this further compounded by the actions of these staff members."

News.title: Swinney's emotional explanation for his commitment to independence
News.content:
This was a more emotional speech than we are used to from John Swinney.

His voice quivered as he explained that his personal commitment to the cause is for the future of his 15-year-old son, Matthew.

Then the autocue stalled and the SNP leader is heard saying under his breath "oh, come on".

A period of silence was broken by the conference crowd who came to his rescue with a standing ovation.

Without the prime minister's name being mentioned, this section of the speech seemed to be a response to Andy Burnham's emotional appeal for the union in memory of his father at the Labour conference in Liverpool.

News.title: Dubois destroys Wardley in two rounds to retain title
News.content:
Daniel Dubois underlined his status as Britain's leading heavyweight with a devastating second-round stoppage of Fabio Wardley to retain his WBO title in London.

The 29-year-old floored Wardley with a straight right inside the opening 20 seconds of their eagerly anticipated rematch at the O2 Arena and continued his relentless assault.

Wardley survived the opening round but was overwhelmed by another sustained attack in the second, prompting his corner to throw in the towel.

Dubois registers a second successive stoppage victory over Wardley, just five months after climbing off the canvas twice to dethrone his British rival in a thrilling 11-round contest in Manchester.

This time, there was no such drama for the champion, who was dominant from the opening bell as he extended his professional record to 24 wins - 23 by knockout - and three defeats.

"Fabio is a great boy, coming in for the second time, but it was my time and my era. I had my intentions, bad intentions from the beginning," Dubois said.

"My back was against the wall the first time, this time we just had to go out there and show that we mean business, which is what we did tonight."

Wardley, 31, suffered the second defeat of his 23-fight professional career.

"I have always thrown myself in with the best competitors out there, the best in the business, the biggest, hardest, meanest guys around so, there is no shame in a loss when you're testing yourself against the best," he said.

News.title: The playground murder: Trauma, loss and a love that endured
News.content:
As we spoke, beside her on the sofa was her husband, Andy Thomson.

It took me a moment to take it in when they told me that Andy had been Alan's best friend.

That through all the tragedy and trauma, this couple found solace in each other and they've been married for 34 years.

Their little grandson is the light of their lives.

"We were kids and I got what she was going through because I was so close to Alan," says Andy.

"And then obviously when Alan passed away, it just drew the two of us even closer.

"And we're 34 years together, we're still going strong and always have been. And always will be."

"No one gives you a book on how to cope with trauma when you're a teenager," Pauline says.

"We were left to cope, and we helped each other. Our life hasn't been all trauma â not at all. But it has been a part of it.

"The most important thing for us was we wanted to talk about Diane and Alan, not just the names in the newspapers.

"For people to have a better understanding of them as kids â because that's what they were, they were kids. Just normal teenagers who should still be here."

If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support can be found at the BBC's Action Line website.

News.title: Manifest: From reality TV to Wembley Arena in one turbulent year
News.content:
A few weeks after their appearance on the boat, I meet the group again at Wembley Arena, where they are preparing for their first UK concert the following night.

As the staging - complete with giant LED screens and the group's logo - is set up around them, the six members rehearse synchronised choreography alongside their back-up dancers.

The group consists of main vocalist Sueda Uluca, lead vocalist Lidya PÄ±nar, sub-vocalist Mina Solak, sub-vocalist and main rapper Zeynep Sude Oktay, lead dancer Hilal YelekÃ§i and main dancer Esin Bahat.

But Wembley is just the beginning of their ambitions.

"After Wembley, we'll manifest Coachella and other big stages," says Hilal YelekÃ§i, playing on the group's name.

manifest were formed in February last year through the Turkish reality TV talent competition Big5 TÃ¼rkiye, which saw contestants compete over several months for a place in the group.

They were mentored by established Turkish pop stars, including GÃ¼lÃ§in ErgÃ¼l, a former member of girl group Hepsi, who was also a judge on the show.

The band's rise has been rapid, and they now have more than six million monthly listeners on Spotify.

News.title: Not sure what to wear for Halloween? These outfits are set to be the most popular this year
News.content:
If you're still on the hunt for the perfect Halloween costume, then you might want to look to gargoyles, Freaky Nikki and Dolly Parton for inspiration - they are all predicted to be popular outfit choices for 2026.

"People don't necessarily want to look frightening - they want to look extraordinary," says costume designer Tamar Zaig, who runs a fancy dress hire shop in London and says she's seeing a "real appetite for escapism, glamour and a bit of dark humour" right now.

And as usual, the year's major film and TV releases, as well as news and pop culture trends, are also driving outfit choices.

So, here are some spooky ideas to try.

News.title: Why people who have never smoked are getting hooked on vapes
News.content:
When vaping first took off at Gracey Mungulu's school, she was vocal about the fact she found it as repulsive as smoking.

"I literally used to tell people like, 'Er, why are you doing that?'" she says.

But Gracey says the habit became so common among her classmates that by the age of 16 she too had taken it up, even though the first time left her coughing rather than inhaling.

"The more you see it, the more you start trying it a bit more," Gracey says, "and then eventually I just got used to it and I was just doing it all the time."

Now 21, she buys a refillable vape every day, using it whenever her hands aren't busy with her work as a hairdresser and in a school.

Gracey is among the more than one million people in the UK who say they have never smoked but now vape, according to recent Office for National Statistics (ONS) survey data â and that number has risen year-on-year.

When vaping first came to the market it was seen as a way to help smokers quit cigarettes.

Vaping nicotine, a highly addictive substance, is less harmful than cigarettes, but the long-term effects are not yet clear, according to the NHS.

News.title: UK must protect against Russian 'hybrid attacks', ex-national security adviser says
News.content:
The government must do more to protect key infrastructure against "hybrid attacks" from Russia, a former national security adviser has told the BBC.

Lord Ricketts said more money should be spent on the defence budget, as well as improving the resilience of energy, transport and air traffic control.

He warned hybrid attacks were becoming "more reckless, more dangerous" and that people could end up being killed.

It comes after MI5 chief Sir Kevin McCallum said in his annual speech earlier this week that threats from foreign states, including Russia and Iran, had quadrupled in the last decade.

Lord Ricketts told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that ministers had to warn British people about what might be coming.

"Not only is [Russian President Vladimir] Putin trying to break morale in Ukraine, he's also trying to undermine morale in European countries," he said.

He said there had been a stark warning from the head of MI5 that there could be worse to come in terms of hybrid attacks in the UK or on other Nato territory.

Responding to a question about the impact of disruption by Russia, Lord Ricketts said: "I'm not saying there's going to be industrial war with tanks rolling across the north German plain.

"But yes these hybrid attacks are getting more reckless, more dangerous...people are going to end up getting killed somewhere."

Hybrid attacks tend to use non-military methods, such as hacking, in an attempt to destabilise a country.

Moscow is suspected to be behind many such attacks in Europe since the start of the war in Ukraine, but it has always denied involvement.

As well as cyber-attacks, hybrid attacks can include attempts at sabotage and efforts to spread misinformation.

Lord Ricketts's warning comes after US President Donald Trump blocked sanctions on Russia. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said the decision "only encourages him [Putin] to keep attacking" Ukraine.

The former national security adviser, who also previously ran the Foreign Office, said the UK's focus should be on putting more effort into the coalition of the willing, rather than attempting to act as a bridge between Zelensky and Trump.

"I don't think in Trump's current mood there is any influence Britain can have in the short term," he said.

A growing number of European leaders have warned that Russia may be preparing attacks to test their commitment to supporting Ukraine.

Last month, Germany said Russia was responsible for a drone attack on an airport in Leipzig, in which an explosive failed to detonate close to Ukrainian cargo planes.

French President Emmanuel Macron warned in September that the threat of hybrid attacks by Russia against Europe and France had intensified.

News.title: Scotland 'not like Manchester', Swinney says in dig at PM Burnham
News.content:
John Swinney has taken aim at those who think Scotland "should be just like Manchester" as he vowed Scotland would soon be an independent nation.

In a closing speech at the SNP conference that did not mention Prime Minister Andy Burnham by name, Swinney issued a veiled retort to the former Greater Manchester mayor after he visited Scotland.

The first minister, speaking in Aberdeen, also announced that the country's bus network would be brought under public control by the end of the parliamentary term in 2031.

Swinney made further pledges to extend a Â£2 bus fare cap to the north east of Scotland, launch an independence campaign, fund anti-racism initiatives and tackle misogyny in schools.

News.title: Boy, 16, and 80-year-old man die in light aircraft crash near Loch Lomond
News.content:
A 16-year-old boy and an 80-year-old man have died following a light aircraft crash near Loch Lomond in Scotland.

Emergency services were called to the scene of the crash near the village of Drymen, in the Stirling Council area, at about 16:45 BST on Friday.

The boy and man were pronounced dead and their next of kin have been informed, police said.

Temporary airspace restrictions are currently in place over the area while the Air Accidents Investigation Branch (AAIB) conducts its inquiries.

An AAIB spokesperson said: "A team has travelled to the accident site near Drymen, north of Glasgow, to make inquiries and gather evidence as part of the process of conducting a safety investigation."

News.title: Man jailed for Starmer-linked arson attacks is deported
News.content:
A man who plotted to carry out arson attacks on property connected to Sir Keir Starmer has been deported, the Home Office says.

Stanislav Carpiuc, 28, was one of two men convicted over the attacks, which took place in May last year and targeted a car and two houses.

The Ukrainian-born Romanian national was sentenced to two years in prison in June. The Home Office said he had been removed from the UK, without specifying where he had been sent.

The BBC revealed the attacks were ordered on behalf of Russia, with an anonymous handler known as EL promising payment to Carpiuc's accomplice, Roman Lavrynovych.

Lavrynovych, a 22-year-old Ukrainian national, was sentenced to seven years imprisonment in June.

A Home Office spokesperson said: "This was an abhorrent attack and the conviction and imprisonment of these men should send a clear message to anyone blinded by the promise of money from strangers. You will be caught and face severe consequences.

"This individual has now been deported from the UK," it added, referring to Carpiuc.

News.title: Nurse stole £750k from 99-year-old woman for cosmetic surgery and home improvements
News.content:
A nurse who stole Â£750,000 from a vulnerable 99-year-old and spent the money on cosmetic surgery and home improvements has been struck off.

Rebecca Louise Burwood exploited the resident who was living at Bryn Yr Haul Care Home in Mold, Flintshire, where she was deputy manager, for her own personal and financial gain.

She coerced the pensioner from 2017 to 2023 and also bought a car and campervan with the stolen money, as well as obtaining ownership of the woman's home.

A Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) hearing found Burwood's fitness to practise was impaired by reason of misconduct and imposed a striking-off order, meaning she will be removed from the nursing register.

The NMC hearing was told Burwood had a longstanding relationship with the woman before she moved into the home in 2018.

The panel heard the resident had no family members and was vulnerable after a fall. She was dependent on Burwood for friendship and social contact.

It found that, between 2017 and 2023, Burwood abused a position of trust and power, becoming the resident's lasting power of attorney, while also overseeing her care.

Burwood withdrew money from the woman's bank account, accepted ownership of her house and received thousand of pounds, which was used for her own benefit, including for building work and the purchase of vehicles.

Evidence presented showed more than Â£370,000 had left the resident's account over five years, with Â£160,000 of that from making large cash withdrawals at ATMs.

She also took the resident to the solicitors and got her to transfer the ownership of her Â£400,000 house.

The hearing was told there was "evidence to show Mrs Burwood used the funds for house improvements, utility bills and council tax", and there were "allegations that Mrs Burwood used some of the funds for personal cosmetic surgery".

She convinced the resident to pay Â£20,000 for a car and Â£9,000 for a campervan, which she said was purchased so the pair could go on days out.

Burwood claimed the work on her home had been so the elderly woman could live with her in the event of another outbreak of Covid - however it had been paid for before any Covid lockdown in the UK.

News.title: Why hasn't the UK had any named storms yet?
News.content:
With November already on the horizon the UK is yet to see its first named storm of the season.

Deep Atlantic lows responsible for more turbulent conditions have been steered away by dominant areas of high pressure.

This year the headlines have been about worsening drought rather than the impact of gales.

However, could this be the calm before the storms as the Met Office predict a growing chance that late autumn and early winter will turn wetter and windier as El NiÃ±o strengthens in the Pacific.

News.title: Husband calls for PM to intervene after wife detained in Egypt
News.content:
The husband of a woman who was detained by the Egyptian authorities has called for Prime Minister Andy Burnham to get involved and help with her release.

Eman el-Shazly, from Handsworth Wood, in Birmingham, was taken from her mother's house in Cairo two months ago, allegedly in relation to her sister's online activism.

Her husband, Zeesharn Moustapha, said that their family felt "very helpless" and that their "only possible solution" was for Burnham to "make a phone call to Egypt" to end the detainment.

The BBC has approached the Egyptian consulate in London for a response. The Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office said it was in contact with authorities in Egypt.

Moustapha said he had had "no contact whatsoever" with his wife, but had heard from her mother that her health had deteriorated due to a lack of food and medical assistance.

"It's not a five-star hotel, there's 30 individuals sleeping in a cell with one toilet and one shower," he said.

He told the BBC that his wife had travelled to Egypt to look after her elderly, sick mother, who had been undertaking 18-hour round trips to take food to el-Shazly's two brothers in detention.

News.title: DIY SOS to be 'rested' next year to save money, BBC says
News.content:
The long-running home renovation TV series DIY SOS will be "rested" next year in the light of "savings challenges", the BBC has said.

It will be replaced by a spin-off show featuring highlights from past episodes. Sources denied reports in the Sun newspaper the programme would be axed as part of a plan to make savings.

Presented by Nick Knowles, DIY SOS sees a team transform the homes of families who are facing severe illness, disability, bereavement or building disasters.

It was first broadcast in 1999 and is currently airing its 35th series on BBC One and iPlayer.

The decision comes during the corporation's drive to save Â£500m over three years. It has already cancelled several well-known TV shows including Blankety Blank, Celebrity Mastermind and Live At The Apollo.

A BBC spokesperson said: "In light of the BBC's savings challenges we have taken the decision to rest DIY SOS in 2027 and commission a new spin-off show instead from producers South Shore.

"DIY SOS Rebuilt My Life will revisit successes from the show's past and expand the brand on the BBC in a more cost-effective way next year."

News.title: Fire crews battle Southern California blaze that burned 6 homes, led to the evacuation of 16,000
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Fire crews in Southern California worked Saturday to contain a wind-driven blaze that charred hills and burned at least six large coastal homes, prompting the evacuation of thousands of people.

Hundreds of firefighters worked through the night on a blaze burning on the hills that straddle the coastal cities of San Juan Capistrano and San Clemente, in Orange County. On a scenic hill popular with hikers, only an American flag remained among the scorched terrain.

The fast-moving Norte Fire sparked Friday in San Clemente amid hot, strong Santa Ana winds that drove it into San Juan Capistrano, prompting the evacuation of about 16,000 residents.

It was one of several fires in the region hit by dry, warm gusts known as Santa Anas, which blow from the interior and toward the coast. The strongest winds hit the area Friday afternoon. But conditions that increase the fire risk were expected to last through Saturday night, with a heat advisory in effect until 8 p.m. Saturday on the Orange County and San Diego County coast, the National Weather Service said.

The blaze was just under a square mile (2 square kilometers) and 5% contained Saturday, when firefighters were still dousing water on smoldering debris from a home that burned.

The fire has damaged or destroyed at least six homes — some of them hillside homes with sweeping ocean views, officials said.

Some evacuation orders were lifted Saturday, but authorities said the large majority remained in effect and urged people to stay away from the area.

“We do have an active fire line, we do have wind, and we have a heat advisory in effect so there is still a risk so, we please ask everybody to please cooperate and heed our advice and stay out of those areas,” said Greg Balta, a spokesperson with the Orange County Fire Authority.

News.title: Top 10 heavyweight fighters in boxing as Dubois destroys Wardley before Fury vs Joshua
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Heavyweight boxing continues to be a compelling draw in the sport with Daniel Dubois stamping his mark on the division by destroying Fabio Wardley before Tyson Fury finally meets Anthony Joshua in the highly-anticipated bout between the two generational British fighters.

That fight, to bring an end to 2026, should set up a fascinating 2027 with a number of contenders, including newly-crowned champions Agit Kabayel and Filip Hrgovic. While super talent Moses Itauma will hope to regroup after a shock first defeat of his career.

Then there is the king of the division: Oleksandr Usyk, patiently waiting for one final payday and an attraction to showcase his exceptional skill on the way out of what has been a legendary career.

Honourable mentions should go out to Murat Gassiev, who holds the WBA regular belt, while Efe Ajagba, Justis Huni, Frank Sanchez, Bakhodir Jalolov and Deontay Wilder remain live contenders.

Here, Independent Sport glosses over the contenders and ranks the fighters on both credentials and their present ability in the ring, as the division takes shape and hurtles towards another unification bout in 2027.

10. Rico Verhoeven (1-1-0)

A controversial selection, perhaps, the great Dutch kickboxer is ranked in the top 10 by the WBC and top 15 by the WBA after his impressive display to get on top of Oleksandr Usyk in Cairo, only to be ground down and stopped late, even if there was some debate over the premature nature of the stoppage. A fight with Deontay Wilder has been floated, on the undercard of Fury v Joshua, which would offer insight into Verhoeven’s ability to mix it with lesser competition in the sport. A rematch with the Ukrainian legend is surely a priority, yet Verhoeven against any of the fighters on this list would be compelling from a competition standpoint, which legitimises his presence in this list.

open image in gallery Rico Verhoeven and Oleksandr Usyk touch gloves ( Getty )

9. Joseph Parker (36-4-0)

After reports that Parker’s positive test for cocaine before his defeat to Fabio Wardley in October last year was caused by a nutritionist, Parker appears to be in the clear to fight again. And while he was exhausted and overpowered by the heavy-handed Wardley last time out, he held his own and showed his exceptional skill to box and move, piling up the rounds and moving to the brink of victory before that dramatic 11th round conclusion. If back and healthy, Parker will be a live opponent for anybody on this list.

8. Moses Itauma (14-1-0)

The aforementioned Parker, rusty after a long lay-off, could make for a fine test for Itauma off the back of his stunning upset defeat to Filip Hrgovic. The promise and potential remain immense, but lessons must be learned, despite dominating the Croatian until his unfortunate and abrupt demise in the ninth round in August. A straight rematch appears too risky for a 21-year-old, but there’s no way back now and a big name to headline will be required next in a highly-anticipated comeback.

7. Anthony Joshua (30-4-0)

Finally set to mix it with great rival Tyson Fury in a fight that might be decided by who has more left in the tank. Joshua’s immense power could point to great hope, with the cliche that it is always the last asset to go for a fighter. The turmoil of that first round against Kristian Prenga casts doubt on ‘AJ’ and his stature in the division, yet his prowess and heart, let’s not forget from his gripping contest with Daniel Dubois in 2024, show how dangerous he remains.

open image in gallery Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will be fighting in the early hours of the morning ( PA Wire )

Enjoy 185+ fights a year on DAZN, the Global Home of Boxing Never miss a fight from top promoters. Watch on your devices anywhere, anytime. Buy Now . If you sign up to this service we will earn commission. This revenue helps to fund journalism across The Independent.

Enjoy 185+ fights a year on DAZN, the Global Home of Boxing Never miss a fight from top promoters. Watch on your devices anywhere, anytime. Buy Now . If you sign up to this service we will earn commission. This revenue helps to fund journalism across The Independent.

6. Filip Hrgovic (21-1-0)

Rocketing up these rankings after a stunning win as a massive underdog to Itauma to snatch the IBF world title, Hrgovic is eager to snatch a world title in the coming months. Since a bloody loss to Dubois in 2024, Hrgovic dispatched Joe Joyce, David Adeleye and Dave Allen, with the patient, yet ruthless defeat of Itauma showing he is ready for another big test in the near future as the belt holder.

5. Fabio Wardley (20-2-1)

Following an unlikely and mesmeric rise to the top of heavyweight, Wardley now finds himself at risk of drifting into the wilderness. He was striving to bounce back from the first defeat of his career against Dubois, a fight he could have won in the early stages, when the pair locked horns again in London. However, the 31-year-old was this time obliterated in short order by the WBO champion, making that back-to-back defeats for a man who came into 2026 undefeated. Wardley is now potentially charged with navigating a title eliminator before he can return to the top table, and his ranking is hurt as a result.

open image in gallery Fabio Wardley is at risk of drifting into the wilderness after a second consecutive defeat to Daniel Dubois ( Reuters )

4. Agit Kabayel (27-0-0)

The WBC champion, undefeated, might consider himself unlucky not to be a little higher on this list, considering he dealt with Arslanbek Makhmudov in better fashion than Tyson Fury and then put away Frank Sanchez and the past-his-prime Zhilei Zhang before a soft win over Damian Knyba to pick up the interim belt before being elevated. Nelson Hysa might not convince the doubters yet, but Kabayel deserves a big unification fight in 2027, perhaps with Dubois after his destruction of Wardley?

3. Tyson Fury (36-2-1)

Finally in the ring with Joshua to conclude 2026, Fury will hope to shake off the rust displayed against Makhmudov and then again with the glorified sparring session with Mariusz Wach to tune up for ‘AJ’. The pedigree still warrants respect and there is less vulnerability than Joshua to ensure he holds a lofty ranking here. Fury is adamant he will fight Usyk once more, but he’ll need to look dominant in Cardiff to convince fans a third fight sets pulses racing.

2. Daniel Dubois (24-3-0)

An outstanding resume all of a sudden, despite two losses to Usyk. Stopped Hrgovic, who has since made that win look even better after stunning Itauma, then destroyed Joshua at Wembley before recovering from a second Usyk defeat to claim the WBO title with a crushing 11th round come-from-behind victory over Wardley. Now, after an even more dominant display in the Wardley rematch, he’s put the division in an awkward position: does anybody want to see a third fight with Usyk? Does Usyk deserve one or two more showcase fights? If so, then Dubois is essentially the No 1 fighter in the division that remains active and open to all challengers.

open image in gallery Daniel Dubois suffered two stoppage losses to Oleksandr Usyk ( Getty )

1. Oleksandr Usyk (25-0-0)

Usyk remains the king of the heavyweights, but for how much longer? Verhoeven perhaps showed the cracks or the inevitable signs of Father Time gradually imposing itself on the legendary Ukrainian. A rematch against the Dutch kickboxer? A trilogy with Fury? There doesn’t appear to be an obvious fight for Usyk left, even if he will gladly pick up one last payday.

News.title: Zack Polanski’s poll approval ratings hit new low amid ‘Zionism is racism’ row
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Zack Polanski has fallen to his lowest poll rating as Green leader following a dispute over his party’s "Zionism is racism" policy position.

An Ipsos survey conducted in October revealed that 52 per cent of the public hold an unfavourable view of the Green leader. This represents a six-point rise since September and marks the first time over half the population has held a negative opinion.

Only 16 per cent of respondents held a positive view of Mr Polanski, leaving his overall rating at minus 36, which is the lowest of any national party leader.

Opposition to Mr Polanski is predominantly focused within older age demographics, according to the findings.

However, he has also shed support among under-35s, falling from a net score of plus 16 in April to plus two.

His standing with 2024 Labour voters has similarly collapsed, dropping from a net favourability score of plus seven in April to minus 24 in October.

open image in gallery An Ipsos survey conducted in October revealed that 52 per cent of the public hold an unfavourable view of the Green Party leader Zack Polanski ( PA Wire )

Keiran Pedley, UK director of politics at Ipsos, said the public had noticed that it had been a “bruising month” for Mr Polanski.

He has faced both internal and external criticism of his leadership after the Green Party conference in Brighton backed a motion describing Zionism as “racism” in a vote Mr Polanski did not take part in.

The decision has seen the leader of the Jewish Greens, Vivien Lichtenstein, call for Mr Polanski to resign and say she is considering leaving the party.

Labour has also issued an ultimatum to local Green groups it is currently in coalition with, telling them to disown the motion or lose the party’s support.

Just days after the conference decision, Mr Polanski suffered a further setback when he was defeated at the Holborn and St Pancras by-election.

open image in gallery Camden Council leader Sagal Abdi-Wali won with 12,292 votes, 45 per cent, while Polanski came second with 8,928 at 33 per cent Holborn and St Pancras by-election ( PA )

The Ipsos poll, conducted in the immediate wake of that by-election, found Andy Burnham remained the only senior UK politician with an overall positive favourability score.

The Prime Minister enjoys a net favourability score of plus eight, while Kemi Badenoch’s score is minus 12 and Sir Ed Davey’s is minus 15.

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage’s overall score is minus 31, with some 56 per cent of people saying they have an unfavourable view of him.

Mr Pedley added: “Andy Burnham appears to be in the ascendancy for the battle for hearts and minds on the left, with 2024 Green voters almost as positive towards him as the leader of the Green Party itself.”

The Ipsos poll surveyed 2,257 British adults online between 9 and 13 October.

News.title: Two dead including child after man drives car onto Wichita soccer field during game: police
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A child and at least one adult are dead after a man drove a vehicle through a soccer game at the Stryker Sports Complex in Wichita, Kansas, Saturday afternoon, police said.

Multiple people were injured and taken to local hospitals before police arrested the driver at the scene, authorities said.

Emergency dispatchers in Sedgwick County began receiving 911 calls around 3:25 p.m. reporting that a vehicle had entered the field at 2999 Greenwich Road. Two juvenile passengers were also inside the vehicle during the crash.

Multiple law enforcement and emergency medical crews responded to the scene, including the Wichita Fire Department, Sedgwick County EMS, Sedgwick County Sheriff’s Office, Kansas Highway Patrol, and the Bel Air Police Department.

The Wichita Police Department confirmed on social media that officers were investigating a "mass casualty incident" and that there was no remaining threat to the public.

open image in gallery Speaking at a news briefing shortly after the incident, Captain Aaron Moses, executive officer with the Wichita Police Department, provided preliminary details with Battalion Chief Jose Okades of the Wichita Fire Department ( Wichita Police Department )

Speaking at a news briefing shortly after the incident, Captain Aaron Moses, executive officer with the Wichita Police Department, outlined the status of the investigation.

“We have two fatalities confirmed here at the scene, and multiple other casualties with individuals transported to area hospitals,” Moses said. “The vehicle involved in this incident remained at the scene. The driver of that vehicle is currently in our custody.”

More follows

News.title: Daniel Dubois destroys Fabio Wardley in blistering fashion to fulfil rematch vow
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Daniel Dubois left no doubt in the mind as he knocked out Fabio Wardley inside two rounds, fulfilling his vow to make quick work of his British heavyweight rival in their rematch.

Having been the one to succumb to an early knockdown in the first matchup, Dubois came out of the blocks in blistering fashion and sent Wardley to the canvas inside 17 seconds.

Wardley, weathering a first-round firestorm, attempted to respond with a huge right cross of his own up against the ropes which narrowly missed.

But Dubois continued to pummel his opponent and threatened to put him away as the round came to a close, Wardley’s trainer Ben Davison holding the towel seemingly ready to pull his man out before the Ipswich man was saved by the bell.

open image in gallery Daniel Dubois unloaded on Fabio Wardley to seal a quick victory in their rematch ( PA )

The punishment continued as the second round began, rocking Wardley with a sharp one-two before he was forced into a corner once again, with Dubois’s attacks overwhelming his British rival.

This time Davison did throw in the towel, something he was criticised for not doing in the first fight, to seal Wardley’s fate and ensure Dubois retained his world title.

"Shout out to everybody, shoutout to my dad, my whole team. Fabio is a great warrior, but it was my time, my era,” Dubois said.

"I had bad intentions from the beginning. Our back was against the wall first time. We just had to go out there and show we meant business tonight."

open image in gallery Dubois celebrates with his team after finishing Wardley ( Getty )

open image in gallery Dubois retained his WBO world heavyweight title ( Reuters )

Wardley is now left to bounce back from two consecutive losses having entered the year undefeated.

Enjoy 185+ fights a year on DAZN, the Global Home of Boxing Never miss a fight from top promoters. Watch on your devices anywhere, anytime. Buy Now . If you sign up to this service we will earn commission. This revenue helps to fund journalism across The Independent.

Enjoy 185+ fights a year on DAZN, the Global Home of Boxing Never miss a fight from top promoters. Watch on your devices anywhere, anytime. Buy Now . If you sign up to this service we will earn commission. This revenue helps to fund journalism across The Independent.

He said: "It's never fun to lose. It is what it is, I've always thrown myself in with the biggest, toughest, meanest guys around, there's no shame in testing yourself against the best.

"Daniel is testament to coming again and I'll come again. You come with a game plan, try to adjust things and it didn't work tonight. It's credit to Daniel of how well he prepared."

Wardley came into the mammoth heavyweight rematch off the back of a brutal defeat in the British pair’s first meeting back in May, when he failed to take advantage of two early knockdowns before Dubois showed immense heart, turning the tide and eventually stopping Wardley in the 11th round.

The 31-year-old Ipswich man was left battered and bloodied by the time the referee eventually waved off the clash at Manchester’s Co-op Live, his nose smashed in and right eye near-completely shut.

Wardley, however, told promoter Frank Warren of his desire to rematch Dubois immediately following the first bout, revealing this request was made in his dressing room before leaving the arena.

Wardley was insistent that he was in a better position to make adjustments from the first bout compared to Dubois, saying that the room for growth was “exponentially in my favour”, despite being the older man by two years.

Dubois was the heavier man on the night by a slender margin of five pounds, though both fighters took to the scale at career-heaviest weights at Friday’s ceremonial weigh-in in London’s Old Spitalfields Market.

And despite Wardley’s confidence, Dubois put on an emphatic display to finish him in short order, taking a step towards his goal of becoming undisputed champion at heavyweight.

open image in gallery Wardley’s corner threw in the towel in the second round ( Reuters )

Dubois has already fought and failed in the pursuit of undisputed gold, knocked out by Oleksandr Usyk under the Wembley arch in July 2025, his previous fight before facing Wardley earlier this year.

He now looks set to target another heavyweight champion after Usyk vacated his titles earlier this year, and squared off with IBF holder Filip Hrgovic - who stunted British 21-year-old Moses Itauma’s stunning rise in August - in the ring after his second triumph over Wardley.

Dubois, however, expressed his desire to complete a trilogy with Usyk, telling a post-fight press conference that he would be “coming out on top” in a third fight.
