News.title: Drivers warned of frisky deer that pose ‘possible danger to life’ on the roads
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Drivers across the United States are being warned to watch out for deer entering their annual mating season, which officials say poses a serious collision risk and a possible danger to life on the roads.

National insurance figures show drivers face a 1 in 145 chance of colliding with an animal, according to an analysis by State Farm. The insurer estimated that more than 1.6 million animal collision claims were filed nationwide between July 2025 and June 2026, with deer topping the list of struck wildlife.

Drivers face the highest risk during the peak mating and hunting months of November, October and December.

West Virginia, Montana and Wisconsin rank as the top states for animal crashes, prompting officials across the country to issue regional warnings. In New Jersey, the Department of Environmental Protection noted that the “fall rut” runs from mid-to-late October through mid-December.

“Collisions with deer pose a very serious safety threat and can cause significant damage to vehicles and possible loss of life,” said Dave Golden, assistant commissioner for NJDEP Fish & Wildlife, in an agency release. “It’s especially important that drivers be extra vigilant to this threat and take time to know steps that can be taken to reduce the risk of collision.”

US drivers are being warned that deer mating season poses a serious collision risk and potential danger to life on the roads — officials urge drivers not to swerve if a crash is unavoidable, warning that veering off-road increases the risk of a fatal accident ( AFP via Getty Images )

State authorities also said that daily commutes frequently overlapped with peak animal activity around dawn and dusk. During the fall rut, deer are more likely to be present near and on roadways as bucks attempt to court does.

The safety hazard is expected to intensify when daylight saving time ends on November 1, shifting heavy traffic periods into darker hours.

The problem has grown worse as suburban development spreads into natural habitats. In New Jersey, around 100,000 deer now roam the state, according to Gothamist.

Nearby New York sees a similar toll, with state transport officials estimating between 60,000 and 70,000 deer crashes every year.

To reduce risk, officials advise motorists to slow down, watch for crossing signs and use high beams in the dark. If a collision is unavoidable, state guidelines urge drivers not to swerve, as counter-maneuvers make fatal crashes far more likely when vehicles hit oncoming traffic or roadside structures.

News.title: Hundreds arrested as protesters clash with police across France over rising living costs
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Clashes have broken out between police and protesters in cities across France as tens of thousands of people angered by rising costs and declining public services took to the streets – in some of the country's most violent protests of recent times.

More than 1,200 people have been arrested across the country, while in Lyon, protesters torched the tourist office. In Marseille, the mayor said the town hall had been vandalised and that additional police were being sent to the city following talks with the government.

The protesters said most people were protesting peacefully and put much of the violence down to troublemakers who had set out to cause damage and clash with the police.

The Interior Ministry said, however, that violence was increasing, and that there had been "confrontations with law enforcement, looting or attempted looting of shops, attacks on and damage to public buildings”.

open image in gallery A car burns amid clashes between protesters and the French police during a demonstration ( Reuters )

It blamed the unrest on ⁠what it described as the "ultra-left". French President Emmanuel Macron said there is “no place for violence" in France, and vowed those responsible would be "prosecuted and punished".

In some parts of Paris, police fired tear gas rounds as they retreated in the face of mostly young protesters, many of whom were dressed in black and wore hoodies, masks and goggles to protect against tear gas. Windows of many shops and restaurants in the capital were smashed, and cars and ​bins were set on fire. In the Les Halles area, a rapid-response riot police force has been deployed.

The roof of a town hall in the central French city of Limoges collapsed after it was set on fire earlier on Saturday, with dramatic footage showing the moment the historic building’s roof caved in as it was engulfed in flames.

"The roof has collapsed onto the lower floors, except in the west wing, and two-thirds of the facade have already disappeared," state representative Maurice Barate said according to Le Parisian.

Masked protesters stormed the town hall in Marseille on Saturday morning after ramming the doors with security barriers and shouting: “It's the Revolution, we're taking the Bastille.” In Lyon, demonstrators set fire to the tourism office and smashed its windows, before trying to prevent firefighters from tackling the blaze.

"The movement is marked by a very strong mobilisation of far-left elements, whose sole intent is to incite disorder," The Interior Ministry said, adding that demonstrations have involved "targeted acts of violence" from "hooded individuals". Security forces have responded "swiftly and decisively", the ministry said. Tear gas has been fired at protesters in multiple locations.

In an update on X, Paris police said: "We do not back down in the face of rioters and those who come to attack the law enforcement forces." They accused "hostile individuals" of targeting police, adding that officers are facing them "with courage and professionalism".

open image in gallery A protester holds a placard amid tear gas smoke as clashes erupt at Place de la Republique ( AFP/Getty )

A large police presence was visible in central Paris, especially near landmarks such as the Avenue des Champs-Elysees and the Arc de Triomphe, which were excluded from the routes of the two official demonstrations.

In Avignon, individuals entered the courtyard of the government Vaucluse prefecture, while protesters in Pau, Montpellier, Toulouse and Valence vandalised businesses, the interior ministry said.

Protesters in Grenoble damaged the city hall and launched an attack on a BNP Paribas bank, smashing the windows and trying to break through the doors.

Protesters in hi-vis vests blocked streets, an echo of the unrest that dogged President Macron's previous term. The protests began last ‌month at high schools in Paris' poor northern suburbs, where anger over teacher absences and shabby facilities quickly morphed into a nationwide movement against inequality, weak public spending and falling standards.

"We are fighting because the cost of living is too harsh, because the price of fuel is too high, because high school pupils are being violently attacked and hurt all over the country just for trying to protest and ask for more teachers and decent learning conditions," said a 19-year-old protester in Paris who gave her name as Lola.

open image in gallery A protester marches with a placard (L) reading "fashion but not fascist" ( AFP/Getty )

In protests partly inspired by those in France, several hundred mostly young people also protested in Brussels on Saturday, and some clashed with police. Belgian student groups have said they are protesting against rising education costs and reforms they fear will make higher education less accessible. Albania also faced more protests on Saturday, with police firing what appeared to be rubber bullets at protesters during a fifth day of mass student demonstrations calling for Prime Minister Edi Rama to step down.

The police have drawn criticism for their response due to a grisly list of injuries among demonstrators in recent weeks, including one teenager who had his hand blown off after picking up a stun grenade.

Prime minister Sebastien Lecornu said more than 900 police had also been injured.

The internal police watchdog is investigating at least two dozen cases of alleged police violence.

open image in gallery Tear gas smoke rises at Place de la Republique ( AFP/Getty )

France suspended the use of stun grenades for the student demonstrations, but Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said they could be used on Saturday.

"If there were to be clashes, all types of intermediate weapons can be used," he told Telematin TV on Friday.

Mr Macron is entering the final stretch of his presidency, leaving behind a polarised electorate and a badly fragmented political landscape.

A long struggle to reduce rising public debt has not impressed investors, who are ditching French bonds, driving borrowing costs to their highest levels in more than two decades.

Mr Lecornu said on Thursday that authorities feared unrest during the protests. The government accused the hard-left France Unbowed of inflaming the protests, an accusation it denies.

open image in gallery Protesters stand next to a burning car amid clashes during a demonstration at the Place de la Republique in Paris ( Reuters )

Calls on social media for members of past protest movements to join the fray appear to have worked, suggesting the protests could grow significantly.

The Yellow Vests, which is helping lead Saturday’ protests in France, said there were more 1,756 mobilisations taking place, including 811 demonstrations.

It includes protests at petrol stations, refineries, oil depots, and ports, as the nationwide movement revolts against rising fuel prices.

The Yellow Vest movement started in 2018 as a protest against taxes on diesel before expanding into an outpouring of anger at high living costs and income inequality.

However, things have been largely quiet since Mr Macron agreed to billions of euros in tax cuts. Yannick Maillou, a teacher from La Crèche in western France, joined the Yellow Vests in 2018 and remains involved in the movement.

He said there were several nearby meeting points for protesters on Saturday, with unions also calling for participation.

News.title: Ruthless Daniel Dubois dispatches Fabio Wardley in just two rounds
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley.

When Wardley dragged himself out of the ring at Manchester’s Co-Op LIVE Arena, the physical damage was obvious, but the psychological sting was far deeper. Wardley had Dubois severely hurt early on, flooring the Londoner twice and teetering on the verge of a career-defining stoppage. Instead, he let the knockout slip away, allowed Dubois to find his rhythm, and was ultimately broken down and halted in the 11th round - surrendering his WBO heavyweight belt in a dramatic comeback victory.

Now, just five months after that gruelling night, the two heavyweights meet again at London’s O2 Arena in an immediate rematch that carries potentially massive implications for the entire division.

For Wardley (20-1-1, 19 KOs), the decision to trigger his rematch clause was instant. Dismissing concerns over the severe punishment he absorbed down the stretch, the Ipswich man is motivated entirely by redemption and the belief that his early success proved Dubois is beatable.

Dubois (23-3, 22 KOs), however, views things very differently. Entering as The Ring’s No. 1 heavyweight contender and a proven two-time world champion, Dubois has brushed off Wardley’s power, claiming his rival “punches like a baby” and insists Wardley threw away his one and only chance at glory in Manchester.

With Oleksandr Usyk approaching the final chapter of his career and the Anthony Joshua vs. Tyson Fury blockbuster looming just eight weeks away, this London clash is far more than a personal grudge match. The winner won’t just walk away with the WBO strap; they will stake an undeniable claim as the torch-bearer for the heavyweight division’s next era if they can land another title fight in short order.

News.title: Newcastle jeers tell Matthias Jaissle his ‘vertical’ football is not working
News.content:
Newcastle United look like a poor team playing badly. The evidence is increasingly damning after Matthias Jaissle’s side were loudly booed off at the end of this limp defeat.

This has all the makings of a long, hard season. Anger is already rising to the surface, even though Jaissle claimed Newcastle deserved more from a game they “controlled” in the first half and “dominated” in the second. Those comments jarred with what we had just seen.

After four years of enjoying an upward trajectory under Eddie Howe, the team faded last season, sold their best players in the summer, lost the manager and there is no evidence yet they have replaced anything with better.

This was supposed to be a reaction to the embarrassing 4-1 thrashing at Coventry City, but it led to another loss and, in the first half at least, another abject display. Aston Villa were always the more fluent and more threatening. They should have won by more than just Johan Manzambi’s first-half header.

News.title: Liverpool’s £400m front line clicks but win at Brentford turns on red card
News.content:
Only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

Admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

But as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

News.title: Steely Chelsea triumph despite losing Martinez to head injury
News.content:
This was the afternoon when Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea went from swashbuckling to stoic, thrilling to tenacious.

For all Alonso’s attacking vigour at the start of his reign, there can have been no more symbolically satisfying victory under the new coach than this resolute win at Everton – the most vivid example of an increasingly impressive transformation.

This was what Alonso described as “winning in a different way”. A triumph amid the adversity of losing goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez to what appears to be a serious injury after a head collision with Jarrad Branthwaite is just one facet of why the joyous visiting supporters might consider this an early turning point.

Where recently they wilted, on Saturday they thrived in securing a first Premier League clean sheet for nine months.

Much more of this and the adjectives which were splattered across Chelsea during the golden years of José Mourinho – solid, robust and dogged – will be part of the Stamford Bridge lexicon once more.

“Just one day,” Alonso warned, both acclaiming the importance of the win while wisely preaching caution. “It will be key when we manage 10 clean sheets, even though this one feels good. We need to repeat it again and again, but the mentality was very good. Sometimes it is not to play nice, it is to play good – to win second balls, and to be efficient. We needed one of these: a clean sheet and a win.”

Asked about Martinez’s condition, Alonso said: “It was a concussion, but beyond that I do not know. I have only seen one clip of the incident, so we need to wait.

“What we know is that he left the stadium conscious and is now in hospital undergoing precautionary tests.

“We need to wait. Hopefully it will not be too serious, but at the moment we just have to wait.”

News.title: Wallabies humiliated in ‘unacceptable’ thrashing by New Zealand
News.content:
New Zealand blew Australia off the field in an extraordinary first-half display in Sydney as they claimed a 13th successive win against the Wallabies and completed a 2-0 Bledisloe Cup clean sweep.

The annual series had already gone New Zealand’s way for a 24th successive year at Eden Park last weekend, but Australia did enough in a highly competitive first half in Auckland to suggest they could give the All Blacks a game on their home turf. And in a breathless opening six minutes in Sydney, it looked as if they might.

The ball-in-play time during that opening spell was incredible as both teams committed to fast, attacking rugby, offloading from everywhere. Like two heavyweights going toe-to-toe in the opening round of a boxing contest, throwing haymakers to see who would get knocked out first.

Ryan Lonergan produced an excellent turnover for the Wallabies to trigger an Australia counter, and the irrepressible Peter Lakai responded with one for the visitors, as the ball travelled from one end of the pitch to the other in one long unbroken spell.

But after New Zealand wing Josh Moorby finally crossed the whitewash, it was Australia who found themselves out on their feet, punch drunk.

News.title: England’s Rugby League World Cup hopes in tatters after Tonga defeat
News.content:
McDermott was full of credit. “They’re a big team, a strong team,” he said. “They’ve got some tremendous players in there, and I thought we stuck toe-to-toe with them for nearly all the game.

“They scored some tries through kicks, which are always hard to defend, and then towards the back-end of the game we made some errors chasing the scoreboard.”

It should be factored in that this was McDermott’s first match in charge and strides have clearly been made since England were woeful in losing the Ashes 3-0 last year.

“I thought we opened up Tonga in that first 20,” McDermott added. “Whether we went through the middle or the edge, we found ourselves in a good ball position, but we had some scrappy finishes to the good ball sets. It was too erratic. We wanted to put a load of fatigue into Tonga, but credit to them. I thought they were terrific defensively.”

Having been beaten by Samoa in the World Cup four years ago, England must face up to the burgeoning conviction that they are no longer among the top three countries in international rugby league. There was the palpable sense of the old order being changed in a stadium packed with the red shirts of Tonga.

As Williams said in the build-up, this is a “mad” format, with only the top two from the combined six-team group of Pool B and C going through to the semi-finals, but now it is very simple as far as England are concerned. They must beat France and Papua New Guinea in their remaining two matches, and do so heavily, then pray that Tonga can beat Samoa in the last match of the pool stage. However, Samoa thumped France 78-4 on Friday, so even that potential avenue appears blocked. McDermott has no other option but to look ahead.

“We know what’s in front of us now, we’ve got to win the next two games and improve on the things we need to improve on,” he said. “But I’ve seen enough tonight that is telling me we’re heading in the right direction.

“It would be tremendously disrespectful to either France or PNG to suggest we’re going to rack up points. I can start looking at points difference and start working out our strategies, but the road will lead us back to winning those two games, and winning them in a strong way.”

Team details

England Radley, Pearce-Paul, Nsemba (King 62), Thompson (Harvard 29, Currie 69), O’Neill (Litten 58); Brimson (Nsemba 79), Young, Savala, Farnworth, Eckersley, Williams, Smith, King (Walters 33, Thompson 76).

Tonga Frizell (Vaimauga 28, Taumalolo 64), Wong (Olakau’atu 41), Olakau’atu (Fonua-Blake 38, Utoikamanu 66), Taumalolo (Halasima 31), Foketi; Hopoate, Watene-Zelezniak, Koula, Toia, Fifita, Fainu (Lolohea 17), Katoa, Fonua-Blake (Utoikamanu 21, Wong 52).

Referee Gerard Sutton (Australia).

England’s Rugby League World Cup challenge could well be over, just 80 minutes after it started.

Brian McDermott’s hopes of qualifying for the semi-finals were all but shattered in his side’s first pool match in a brutal encounter in which Pacific Island physicality and passion ultimately earned Tonga a famous victory.

England displayed huge attacking courage with their offload strategy – in all, they made 26 – but their adventurous intent could not find the finishing touch and was not enough to topple a ferocious opposition defence in Perth. Despite excellent performances from captain George Williams and Dom Young, they were ultimately blown off HBF Park.

On their seventh attempt, this was Tonga’s first win over England and although this intense contest was for, so long, much closer than the scoreboard finally showed, there can be no doubting the excellence of Kristian Woolf’s team and the ruthlessness they displayed in the last quarter in which they never stopped tackling refused to stop coming.

News.title: ‘The boats don’t stop’: The deadly coastline that has become a trafficking superhighway
News.content:
The dangers were illustrated earlier this month, when a boat carrying more than 300 migrants sank near Obock on its way to Yemen. At least 139 people drowned, including 15 children. There were 700 drownings or people lost at sea on the route in 2025.

“The boats don’t stop, day or night,” the local coastguard chief told the Telegraph as he looked out at the waterway, walkie-talkie in hand, one day earlier this month.

The chief, who declined to be named, pointed to skiffs and fishing boats moored in a lagoon outside his outpost, that he had confiscated from smugglers and traffickers.

The world has become familiar with the 18-mile-wide Bab el-Mandeb strait as one of the globe’s most congested and strategically important maritime choke points.

Sitting to the south of the Suez Canal, the East-West artery flowing through the strait carries approximately 12 to 15 percent of global maritime trade.

What is less well known is that there is also a migration superhighway running across the strait, linking Africa via Djibouti to Yemen and the Gulf beyond.

Many tens of thousands of people cross the waterway each year and while Yemeni refugees fleeing the Houthi offensive have made headlines in recent weeks, the majority of those braving the waterway are heading the other way.

This maritime migrant route out of Africa has recently been busier than all the crossings across the Mediterranean into Europe, according to the International Organisation for Migration (IOM).

The IOM estimates there were nearly 64,000 crossings across the Bab el-Mandeb in the first four months of 2026, compared with a total of just over 23,000 across the Western, Eastern and central routes of the Med.

The vast majority heading east are Ethiopians so desperate to find work in the Gulf that they are prepared to trek through war-torn Yemen, which has been tipped into a humanitarian crisis by its civil war.

The IOM recorded some 202,000 migrant trips into Djibouti from Ethiopia in 2025 and by early October, the figure for 2026 had already hit 177,000.

The reignited war in Ethiopia’s Tigray region is expected to increase the numbers wanting to leave, yet the exodus is also being held up by escalating fighting along Yemen’s coast between Houthis and the government.

Fewer are now able to get across the strait, leaving them stranded on the western side, or forced to take more dangerous routes.

News.title: Asia’s vaccine self-sufficiency drive gets $650m boost
News.content:
An “innovative” partnership to boost vaccine security across Southeast Asia will inject up to $650 million into regional manufacturing, in a bid to reduce reliance on imported shots.

The five-year initiative, announced at the annual meetings of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund in Bangkok on Friday, will see major lenders, non-profits, and the private sector come together to invest in the region’s vaccine industry.

Currently Southeast Asia’s production base remains limited and exposed. The majority of shots are imported, and any capacity the region does have is highly concentrated – one analysis this year estimates 60 to 90 per cent sits with a single vaccine manufacturer.

Even before Covid-19 hit, this vulnerability was recognised. The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean), a regional bloc of 11 countries, endorsed a vaccine security and self-reliance initiative in 2019, driven by Thailand’s National Vaccine Institute (NVI).

These concerns have mounted since the pandemic, but up until now investment as well as political will has been lacking. The partnership announced on Friday, led by NVI, hopes to remedy this, and develop a model that can be copied worldwide.

​​“If we can do it here in Asia, then that really provides a model for the world,” said Aurélia Nguyen, deputy CEO of the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (Cepi), a a vaccine research non-profit. “We can build it out in Africa, in Latin America, and that really gives us the resilience that we want the next time we have a major epidemic.”

Cepi has committed up to $20 million of “catalytic funding” for the programme, which is backed by the World Bank as well as organisations like the Singapore-based AVPN investment network.

In all, the package of loans and grants will include at least $174m in public financing, and up to $460m in private capital mobilisation for regional vaccine manufacturing. Further details, including recipients, have not yet been announced.

But Paschal Donohoe, the managing director and chief knowledge officer of the World Bank Group, told a panel in the Thai capital that “we believe this has the ability over time to mobilise up to $650m of finance”.

He added that the group would use public loans and grants alongside investments by its private-sector arm, the IFC, while its guarantee arm, MIGA, would help cover investors against risk.

“It’s really important because each element of the World Bank Group is involved in it,” Donohoe said. “We’re not just talking the talk, but walking the walk.”

Speaking to the Telegraph after the event, Nguyen added: “Innovative models and partnerships like this, where we’re each bringing a piece to de-risk scientific technology, [allow us] to leverage larger quantities of capital.

“But I think what’s also helpful in this model is, beyond the financing, [we] have a sort of coordinating umbrella through Asean,” she said. “So you can be smart and [avoid] duplicating investments, which brings commercial sustainability and resilience for health systems.”

Nakorn Premsri, the director of NVI, added that the investment model will help “build a more sustainable and resilient regional vaccine ecosystem, to meet both routine needs and the demands of health emergencies”.

Sports.title: When can Emiliano Martinez make Chelsea comeback after Everton head injury?
Sports.content:
When can Emiliano Martinez make Chelsea comeback after Everton head injury?

Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez saw a severe head injury force him off against Everton with concussion protocols likely needing to be followed

View 2 Images Chelsea's Emiliano Martinez could be out for a few games after suffering a head injury (Image: (Photo by Richard Martin-Roberts - CameraSport via Getty Images))

Emiliano Martinez could feature in Chelsea's Premier League clash against Tottenham next Saturday but that seems unlikely if he has suffered a concussion. The 34-year-old took a heavy blow to the head from Jarrad Branthwaite and was subsequently stretchered off in the Blues' 2-0 win over Everton.

‌



‌



Mike Penders replaced Martinez in the Chelsea goal and helped see out the clean sheet. Despite the strong display, Martinez's health was the priority with Xabi Alonso able to offer a positive update after the game.

‌



He said: "What we know is that he left the stadium conscious. Right now he's in the hospital doing precautionary tests. So we need to wait, and, for sure, hopefully it won't be too bad, but we need to wait at the moment."

‌



The best-case scenario would be that Martinez has not suffered a concussion, but the 10-minute delay while he received treatment and speed of the collision suggests he has.

Xabi Alonso issues Emi Martinez injury update as Chelsea star taken to hospital READ MORE :

Chelsea's Emi Martinez forced off on stretcher after huge collision and lengthy delay READ MORE :

At elite-level football, a return to action can be managed on day 7 - which would be next Saturday - and that is when Spurs visit Stamford Bridge.

However, Martinez would have not trained throughout the week and it is all dependent on if he comes through a six-stage 'return to play' procedure unscathed. The initial phase involves a 48-hour rest period with minimal physical and 'cognitive' activities, such as working and screen time.

‌



According to the FA's guidelines, this should be followed by "a staged and graduated return to full daily activities". Light football training is permitted during this stage but nothing should be undertaken to "worsen existing symptoms more than mildly or produce new symptoms".

View 2 Images Emiliano Martinez made some good saves before being forced off

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



The four subsequent stages consist of football-specific exercise, non-contact training, full-contact training, and ultimately a complete return to match action.

Players diagnosed with a concussion very rarely feature in the next fixture, with Nico Gonzalez having suffered such an injury this season and sitting out Newcastle United's following match.

Chelsea host London rivals Tottenham at Stamford Bridge in their next Premier League encounter, with the match scheduled to take place under the lights next Saturday.

‌



While some uncertainty remains surrounding Alonso, he will definitely be without club captain Reece James for that fixture after the full-back underwent knee surgery earlier this week, an operation expected to sideline him for a few months.

Alonso has, however, been boosted by the return of Moises Caicedo, with the midfield maestro proving instrumental in their 2-0 victory at Everton. Martinez also produced a string of fine stops prior to his early exit, with Mike Penders stepping in to help secure the three points.

It was a Pedro Neto double that earned Chelsea the win, with the Portuguese winger dedicating his brace to both of the club's goalkeepers.

Article continues below

He said: "In his [ Emiliano Martinez's ] honour. We needed that. We did a very good game. Emi deserved this. Mike [Penders] deserved this as well. We are really happy."

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola provides double Liverpool injury update after pair forced off vs Brentford
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola provides double Liverpool injury update after pair forced off vs Brentford

Liverpool were 2-1 winners away to Brentford on Saturday, but their win was blemished by injuries to Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong either side of half-time

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola provided updates on Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremy Frimpong (Image: This Is Anfield)

Andoni Iraola has confirmed that Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong will be out for 'some time' after both Liverpool players came off injured against Brentford. Iraola's side won 2-1 courtesy of goals from Victor Munoz and Alexander Isak, completing a second-half comeback.

‌



‌



But Liverpool left the Gtech Community Stadium with concern. Szoboszlai's return from a hamstring injury lasted just half an hour while Frimpong only managed seven minutes after coming on as a substitute.

‌



Post-match, Iraola shed light on their setbacks. "I think we have a very delicate situation," the Reds manager explained. "We were coming from playing Champions League away two days ago, we arrived [home] late at night and probably with not a proper recovery.

‌



"You are in doubt between the players that have already started two games and are very tired, or the players that are recovering from injuries but you're probably not 100 per cent certain.

"They were different cases. Dom felt the same injury, it's not a new injury and was probably not healed enough, so we will need more time with him.

"Jeremie's was new, I think he finished cramping the other day [against LASK]. I put him on because playing against 10, going forward I thought he could give us more than Ronald [Araujo].

"After, I value a lot and he was very good, Victor playing as a right-back. But it will mean we will lose Dom and Jeremie for some time, yes."

‌



How should Liverpool line up against Villarreal? Let us know your XI in the comments section.

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola will be without the duo for 'some time' (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Barring the injuries, Iraola was largely a happy man. Liverpool leapfrogged Brentford and moved up to fifth in the Premier League table before they return to Champions League action by hosting Villarreal on Tuesday.

Article continues below

"I think we played really well until the 2-1," Iraola told Sky Sports. "After that we started to protect something, I think we didn't manage the last minutes well.

"I think some of the players were seeing quite clear chances to finish the game that we haven't been able to finish. We lacked some composure on the ball. Sometimes it was just about keeping the ball more and not going for the goal with the first chance."

Sports.title: Viktor Gyokeres eyeing Arsenal January exit after Gunners' transfer pursuit
Sports.content:
Viktor Gyokeres eyeing Arsenal January exit after Gunners' transfer pursuit

Viktor Gyokeres has struggled to find his footing in Mikel Arteta's Arsenal set-up over the past 12 months, with his future at the Emirates Stadium now under serious doubt as January transfer talk intensifies

View 2 Images Viktor Gyokeres could be looking for a move away from Arsenal (Image: David Price, Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Viktor Gyokeres is reportedly keen to leave Arsenal due to a lack of first-team opportunities. The Swedish frontman was the subject of intense speculation in north London last summer, with the Gunners eventually wrapping up a £63.5million agreement with Sporting CP for the 28-year-old following a lengthy and protracted transfer saga.

‌



‌



Yet Gyokeres has found it difficult to establish himself in Mikel Arteta's system over the past 12 months, with his long-term future at the Emirates Stadium now under serious scrutiny. This season, Gyokeres has been restricted to a mere 56 Premier League minutes in total, and has unsurprisingly failed to register a single goal or assist despite his endeavours.

‌



Arsenal also devoted considerable energy towards landing Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez during the summer window, only to come away empty-handed owing to the La Liga outfit's firm refusal to sell combined with the Argentine forward's preference to join Barcelona instead.

‌



With the Madrid club making clear they have no intention of selling their prized asset to their Catalan rivals, and with Alvarez's relationship with the Atletico faithful somewhat strained following his Camp Nou ambitions this summer, Arsenal could be well-positioned to make a renewed push for the striker come January.

That would also all but cement Gyokeres' standing at his current club, with Alvarez likely to spearhead Arteta's attack upon his arrival given the substantial fee Atleti would demand for his services.

Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



According to TEAMtalk, Atletico Madrid also remains a possible destination for Gyokeres should he depart Arsenal. The La Liga outfit expressed an interest in the striker during their meetings with Andrea Berta over the summer, with discussions over a potential deal for Alvarez also regularly featuring in those conversations.

However, a number of other clubs across the Premier League, Italy and Germany are also keeping tabs on Gyokeres, meaning Arsenal could face a hectic period when the transfer window swings open again at the start of 2027.

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez remains a target for Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Despite shining in the Nations League with Sweden, netting four goals in four appearances throughout the recent international break, Arteta continues to place his trust in Kai Havertz as a false-nine rather than handing Gyokeres the opportunity to lead the line.

That's also despite Gyokeres' track record for thriving on English soil. The striker racked up 43 goals and 17 assists for Coventry City between 2021 and 2023 before securing his move to Sporting.

Article continues below

There, he enjoyed a further 97 goals and 28 assists in 102 games before landing in North London last summer.

Whether the Gunners boss deviates from his current approach or gives Gyokeres the chance he deserves on paper when Arsenal make the trip to the City Ground to face Nottingham Forest on Sunday, 18th October, remains to be seen.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso knows minimum Chelsea requirement after ending nine-month wait
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso knows minimum Chelsea requirement after ending nine-month wait

Xabi Alonso saw Chelsea win and with a clean sheet - their first in exactly nine months - with the Spaniard knowing the expectations upon him despite his regime being in its infancy

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso has arrived at Chelsea with serious pedigree

Jordan Pickford went the length of the pitch to show his concern for his fellow goalkeeper, while Jarrad Branthwaite stood by Emiliano Martinez for most of the ten minutes it took to safely move the Chelsea man onto a stretcher.

‌



‌



The only real concern after this match was that Martinez recovers fully after being taken from the field with his neck and head needing support. He managed to give a thumbs-up to Branthwaite, which was slightly promising.

‌



The second-half collision had been purely accidental, albeit one that took place in the context of a quite ill-tempered occasion. And for Chelsea to come through this feisty meeting with a win and a clean sheet will certainly give Xabi Alonso huge encouragement.

‌



Never mind that it is Alonso’s first campaign as a Premier League manager, anything less than a Chelsea title challenge will represent failure.

It might well drag on and on but you can safely take Manchester City out of the equation, and Liverpool and Manchester United have shown little to suggest they can pose a serious threat to Arsenal.

‌

The champions themselves have been efficient without being mightily impressive. With no European football to distract and fatigue them - and a squad that gives Alonso myriad options - there really is no excuse for Chelsea should they repeat last season’s mediocre efforts.

One of the things that has already improved under Alonso is the team’s discipline, after a category-leading eight red cards last season.

‌



That discipline was sorely tested by an Everton side that does not shirk the physical battle. In large parts, this was indeed a distinctly fractious contest and Chelsea were fortunate to get to half-time with a full quota, Paul Tierney deciding against an obvious second yellow card for Morgan Rogers when he endangered James Garner just before half-time.

Garner’s undramatic reaction helped his England team-mate. And Garner probably regretted his sportsmanship when a Rogers reverse-pass began the move that led to Pedro Neto’s opener.

It was a nice assist from Jarrel Hato but Pickford’s involvement is, from an Everton and the England keeper’s point of view, best forgotten.

‌



View 2 Images Pedro Neto scored both goals at Everton

It is fair to say Pickford - under pressure from James Trafford for his place in the national team - has not had the most convincing opening to his club season. And when Pickford errs, it can be more significant than is standard in the Premier League. That is because a David Moyes team is normally less than prolific.

Everton scored 47 times last season and now have eight from seven this season. When Everton finished fourth under Moyes in 2004-05, they scored 45 goals in amassing 61 points. They had a negative goal difference.

Article continues below

Moyes is never going to be the great entertainer. But he is the great organiser. With organisation, comes strength.

And after the serious injury to Martinez, Everton’s strength threatened an equaliser but Chelsea showed an unfamiliar defensive resilience before Neto wrapped up matters with his second. Alonso’s first - and sole - concern will, of course, be for Martinez. But when and if he allows himself a reflection on the football, this was most definitely a statement of intent.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola's bold Liverpool change pays off as nine-man Brentford cause their own undoing
Sports.content:
Liverpool came from behind to beat nine-man Brentford 2-1, with a change from Andoni Iraola sparking their turnaround. The Reds came away from the Gtech Community Stadium with all three points thanks to second-half goals from Victor Munoz and Alexander Isak.

But the stage was set by a dramatic first half that saw two decisions overturned by VAR and a deserved lead for Brentford. Keane Lewis-Potter fired the Bees in front shortly after Liverpool thought they'd been given a penalty.

But Keith Andrews' side - who went into Saturday unbeaten - were reduced to 10 when Yehor Yarmolyuk was deemed to have headbutted Jeremy Jacquet. Munoz and Isak eventually punished Brentford, although it wasn't straightforward for the visitors - even after another Brentford red card.

Make sure you don't miss the best Liverpool coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Liverpool dealt Szoboszlai blow

When team news was confirmed, Liverpool fans were delighted to see the return to Dominik Szoboszlai. The Hungarian had missed his side's last two games but was back in the starting XI.

Unfortunately for Szoboszlai, he only lasted 32 minutes. The 25-year-old went down off the ball in what appeared to be an aggravation of his prior injury.

All eyes will be on Iraola's post-match comments and whether Szoboszlai will be fit to face Villarreal in the Champions League on Tuesday. And talk about bad things coming in threes...

‌



Where will Liverpool finish this season? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 5 Images Dominik Szoboszlai's return from injury was short-lived (Image: Glyn KIRK/AFP via Getty Images)

VAR dominates first half

It was all going wrong for Liverpool as half-time neared. Shortly after Szoboszlai's substitution, the Reds were given a penalty by John Brooks, as Dango Ouattara went sliding in on Alexis Mac Allister, and quickly had it taken away.

Replays showed that the only contact Brentford winger Ouattara made was with the ball, prompting Brooks to overturn his decision on the recommendation of video assistant referee Darren England. But VAR wasn't done getting involved - more that shortly.

‌



Brentford made the most of their reprieve, as Keane Lewis-Potter's header put the hosts 1-0 up. The goal came about after Mac Allister had lost possession inside his own half, allowing the hosts to pounce.

View 5 Images Keane Lewis-Potter broke the deadlock (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

The ball ended up at the feet of Igor Thiago, whose cross was perfectly converted by Lewis-Potter. Then finally something went right for Liverpool.

At a corner, Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet was having it out with Yehor Yarmolyuk, and the Brentford midfielder lost his cool with a headbutt akin to Rodrigo Bentancur's against Manchester United last weekend. England spotted in the incident and Brooks had no choice but to show Yarmolyuk a red card.

‌



No penalty was awarded because the ball wasn't in play at the time of the incident. Liverpool still had it all to do, but facing 10 men gave them a huge advantage.

View 5 Images Yehor Yarmolyuk was sent off for a headbutt (Image: Julian Finney/Getty Images)

Iraola's bold change pays off

For a spell early in the second period, Brentford held their own with 10 men, testing Liverpool before their onslaught came about somewhat inadvertently. Jeremie Frimpong, brought on as a half-time substitute, had to come off just seven minutes after his introduction due to injury.

Would Iraola turn to Joe Gomez or opt for something bolder?

‌



The answer was the latter. Rio Ngumoha entered the fray, offering more of an attacking threat.

Ngumoha's introduction forced Victor Munoz to right-back, but it didn't put the Spaniard off bombing forward. Munoz would equalise with a brilliant solo goal, cutting inside and producing a cool finish from inside the 18-yard box.

View 5 Images Andoni Iraola made a game-changing attacking substitution (Image: Glyn KIRK/AFP via Getty Images)

Iraola's men kept up the pressure and would be rewarded when Mac Allister picked out Bradley Barcola, who was free at the far post. His header wasn't ideal but Alexander Isak showed superb centre forward play to take the ball away from his man and slot past Caoimhin Kelleher.

‌



Although Ngumoha wasn't involved in either of the goals, the winger's presence changed the dynamic for Liverpool. Gomez did eventually come on to help the Reds over the line, a task made easier by Vitaly Janelt's second yellow card for a foul on Barcola in stoppage time.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso issues Emi Martinez injury update as Chelsea star taken to hospital
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso issues Emi Martinez injury update as Chelsea star taken to hospital

Emi Martinez was forced off in Chelsea's win at Everton following a nasty collision, and Xabi Alonso has confirmed that his goalkeeper was taken to hospital

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso was quizzed on Emi Martinez's condition (Image: TNT Sports)

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso has confirmed that Emi Martinez was conscious when he left the Hill Dickinson Stadium and his visit to hospital is "precautionary".

‌



‌



The Spaniard was unable to give any more information with the Blues boss being quizzed shortly after his side's win at Everton as he awaits a full report on their goalkeeper.

‌



Martinez needed to be stretchered off midway through the second half after a major collision with Jarrad Branthwaite. The Everton defender, after receiving treatment, was able to jump back to his feet and continued.

‌



The Argentine, though, was still being tended to by medical staff. The stretcher was bought out, with Martinez being assisted off as the Hill Dickinson Stadium applauded him. The pause would result in 11 minutes of added time.

Alonso said: “As far as I know, he left the stadium conscious. Now he is in the hospital doing precautionary tests. Let’s see, but this is what I know so far.”

Chelsea would secure their first clean sheet in nine months on Merseyside. Martinez needed to be alert to deny Jack Grealish in the first half whilst the Blues' shut out was completed by Mike Prenders, who came on and spent the final 25 minutes on the pitch.

Matchwinner Neto said after his two goals secured the three points: "We are really pleased. Shame for Emi [Martinez] but we wish you all the best. This win is for him."

‌



He also added: "We need a clean sheet to be honest. I think we did a very good game. Emi deserved this, Mike [Penders] did as well."

View 2 Images The Chelsea goalkeeper had to be taken off on a stretcher

The ex-Aston Villa No.1 will now be sidelined for at least two weeks as per the concussion protocols. It means he will miss the clash with Tottenham next week and is a doubt for the Carabao Cup tie at Anfield against Liverpool as well as the game against Manchester United on October 31.

Article continues below

In recent years, the Football Association (FA) have implemented strict head injury procedures and Martinez will now have to go through the process.

Sports.title: FIFA quietly dish out two punishments to World Cup winners Spain
Sports.content:
FIFA quietly dish out two punishments to World Cup winners Spain

Spain handed double FIFA punishment following Islamophobic chanting during Egypt friendly

View Image Spain coach Luis de la Fuente

FIFA have fined Spain $20,000 (£15,000) and ordered a partial stadium closure following Islamophobic chanting during their friendly against Egypt in March. The chants were heard during the first half and again at the start of the second period.

‌



‌



A section of supporters were reportedly heard singing: "Bote, bote, bote, musulman el que no bote," which translates as "Jump, jump, jump, whoever doesn’t jump is a Muslim."

‌



An anti-discrimination message was subsequently displayed inside the stadium condemning 'Islamophobic and xenophobic' chanting. FIFA launched disciplinary proceedings against the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) following the incident, with Spain manager Luis de la Fuente among those to condemn the behaviour.

‌



Real Madrid demand La Liga chief Javier Tebas quits after Nazi comparison READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"I am repulsed by and absolutely reject any form of xenophobia or racism - it's completely intolerable," De la Fuente said. "I don't know exactly what the protocol is, but I think it was the right decision to display the message on the scoreboard and make the announcement.

"Those [chanting] are a disgrace and the majority [inside the stadium] whistled them. There's nothing else to say. They are not representative of football.

‌



"They take advantage of football, as they do in other areas of life. They need to be removed from society, the further away, the better."

The RFEF also reiterated its stance against discrimination, writing on social media: "The RFEF stands against racism in football and condemns any act of violence inside stadiums."

Sports.title: Chelsea's Emi Martinez forced off on stretcher after huge collision and lengthy delay
Sports.content:
Chelsea's Emi Martinez forced off on stretcher after huge collision and lengthy delay

The goalkeeper has been stretchered off during Chelsea's Premier League clash with Everton following a clash of heads with Jarrad Branthwaite

View Image Emi Martinez had to be stretchered off following a collision

Emiliano Martinez was stretchered off during Chelsea's clash with Everton following a nasty collision with defender Jarrad Branthwaite. The incident occurred around the hour mark, with play halted for a lengthy period as medical staff attended to both players.

‌



‌



The incident followed a free-kick for the hosts, with Martinez and Branthwaite both challenging for the ball before colliding heads. Both players received medical attention on the pitch, but Martinez was ultimately stretchered off.

‌



The Argentine was seen awake and moving as he was carried off at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, while Branthwaite was able to continue playing. Providing an update on TNT Sports, commentator Darren Fletcher confirmed Martinez was being taken to hospital.

‌



Reece James suffers yet another injury blow as Chelsea captain undergoes surgery READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"Only news we can bring you and bring you today is that he's been taken away to hospital which is the best place possible," he said. "Emi Martinez on his way to hospital in Liverpool."

Mike Penders, 21, came on to replace Martinez, making his Premier League debut in the process.

‌



The Football Association has guidelines in place for managing concussion, outlining the symptoms to look out for and the recommended recovery process.

Its guidance states: "The first symptoms of concussion typically appear immediately or within minutes of injury but may be delayed and appear over 24-48 hours following a head injury. Over the next several days, additional symptoms may become apparent.

"After the initial 24-48 hour period of relative rest, a staged and graduated return to full daily activities (education/work) and football training is allowed but at a rate that does not worsen existing symptoms, more than mildly, or produce new symptoms.

‌

Sports.title: Rangers miss chance to go top as Jones earns Dundee a point
Sports.content:
Callum Jones scored a second-half equaliser as Rangers were held to a 2-2 draw by Dundee and missed the chance to go top of the Scottish Premiership.

Dundee opened the scoring when Rangers failed to deal with a routine long ball, with Bradley Fink capitalising to round the goalkeeper and slide home.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bradley Fink's composed finish gave Dundee the lead against Rangers.

The lead did not last long, though, as Badredine Bouanani cut inside and curled in a stunning equaliser to open his account for Rangers.

Nico Raskin scored the goal of the game when his shot from outside the area went in off the underside of the crossbar.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nicolas Raskin produced an outrageous strike to put Rangers back in front against Dundee.

But Jones then caught Dan Neil dwelling on the ball and nicked it off the Rangers captain to slot home the Dundee equaliser.

Rangers remain second and move one point behind Celtic, who host Hearts live on Sky Sports on Sunday from 2.30pm.

The key moments from Dens Park

8: BLOCKED! Kim has a shot blocked with the goal gaping. Rangers cry for handball but nothing doing.

14: SHOT! Forrest drives from midfield and shoots from the outside of the area, but Pandur gathers comfortably.

23: SHOT! Hay has a speculative shot and again it's saved comfortably by Pandur.

28: SAVE! Hamilton whips a free kick across and Astley heads towards goal from outside of the area tipped behind by Pandur.

29: OFF THE BAR! Hay leaps to meet the corner and it rattles the bar.

36: CLOSE! Hamilton takes an early shot after Dundee win the ball back and it goes just wide.

37: GOAL! Fink rounds the goalkeeper and scores!

42: GOAL! Bouanani curls into the top corner for his first goal for Rangers!

56: SAVE! Gassama shoots from the edge of the area, and it's saved one-handed by the 'keeper

60: GOAL! Nico Raskin scores a screamer off the bar from outside of the area.

69: GOAL! Neil dwells on the ball and is dispossessed by Jones who slots past the goalkeeper to get Dundee level!

74: CLOSE! Ball falls to Neil in the six-yard box but Dundee somehow scramble the ball clear!

McInnes: We shouldn't need three goals to win

Rangers boss Derek McInnes:

"I thought Dundee's press was good, as expected, and we wanted to try and draw the centre-backs out at times and try and hit spaces and feed our wide players and try and get 1v1.

"It never quite materialised.

"We shouldn't need to come away from home and need to score three goals to win a game.

"Two goals should have been enough tonight. We had a few chances when it went to two each.

"Dundee are a good team, but I think we gifted an opportunity there not to take all three points.

"We're disappointed not to come away with three points."

Pressley: We showed grit and determination

Image: Callum Jones scores for Dundee to make it 2-2

Dundee boss Steven Pressley:

"I think it was a game of two halves.

"I thought we were outstanding in the first half, really aggressive, controlled a lot of the game.

"We were really strong on second balls, had one or two moments where we should have capitalised and restricted Rangers to very little.

"We obviously expected a reaction from Rangers and they gave that reaction. They put us under a lot of pressure in the second half.

"We showed grit and determination.

"The game was getting away from us but we never gave up, we kept going and going and (Callum) Jones got his reward for a really strong performance today."

Boyd: Dundee asked questions of Rangers

Sky Sports' Kris Boyd:

"Dundee are a good team. They're not there [in the table] by fluke or luck.

"They've got a style of play, Steven Pressley has got a group of players willing to run themselves into the ground for him and that's hard to get.

"They put in a shift and even when they're asked to dig in and suffer like they did for the first 20/25 minutes of that second half.

"They then got a second wind and came back at Rangers and asked questions of them.

"A draw was a fair result. It took wonder strikes to get Rangers two goals.

"There was a lack of creativity at the top end of the pitch and it's something they're going to have to improve."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Dubois smashes through Wardley to win world title rematch in two rounds
Sports.content:
Daniel Dubois smashed Fabio Wardley to defeat in the second round of their world championship rematch at London’s O2 Arena.

Dubois retained the WBO heavyweight title he won from Wardley in May in crushing style, picking up just where he left off in their first fight.

Dubois and Wardley were renewing hostilities only five months after a frenetic and ultimately brutal contest.

Then London's Dubois had needed to rise twice from early knockdowns to punch out a savage 11-round victory over Wardley, hurting the Ipswich fighter even though Wardley was stopped on his feet.

Image: Dubois finishes Wardley in a corner.

Wardley, determined to win back his world title as soon as he could, exercised the rematch clause in his contract and forced this second fight to take place.

But Dubois snuffed out his hopes with brutal speed.

A smashing Dubois right cross saw Wardley drop, ever so briefly, to a knee in the opening seconds of the first round. He bounced up immediately, inviting the right uppercut that followed.

The referee administered a count, and that proved to be just a momentary reprieve. Dubois set about him with shuddering force for the rest of the round.

Wardley was pained, being driven to the ropes by an unrelenting Dubois.

The champion continued his onslaught in the second round. He hammered Wardey into a corner, jolting his head on his neck with a salvo of stunning punches, until Wardley's trainer Ben Davison threw in the towel and the referee rushed in to end it.

On the undercard Bakhodir Jalolov, a two-time Olympic super-heavyweight gold medallist, showcased just what makes him so formidable as he hammered out a 10 round unanimous decision victory over Solomon Dacres.

Image: Bakhodir Jalolov dominates Solomon Dacres (Photos: Leigh Dawney/Queensberry)

But he also displayed what can make him so frustrating to watch. The towering southpaw controlled virtually the whole bout and struck Dacres over early in the fifth round.

The knockdown was superb, Jalolov using his right to take Dacres' left glove away from his guard, opening up a path for the Uzbek's booming left cross - a shot that sent Dacres to the canvas and bloodied his nose.

But Jalolov didn't capitalise and continued to work in single shots, albeit excellent single shots, as he dominated without turning up the pressure, winning 99-91 and 99-90 twice.

20-year-old Irish heavyweight prospect Adam Olaniyan made short work of journeyman Dan Garber.

Image: Adam Olaniyan takes out Dan Garber

In his fifth pro fight, Olaniyan maintained his 100 percent finish rate stopping Garber in the second round.

Busy without rushing his work, Olaniyan's right cranked Garber's back into a corner post at the end of the first round.

He picked up from there for the second, trapping Garber on the ropes and putting him down with another heavy cross.

Garber's corner threw in the towel, then threw in a second. But the referee kicked them out the ring and Garber tried to fight on. He was though promptly crumpled a second time. After rising unsteadily the referee waved it off at 1-15.

Sports.title: Champions Cup: Munster beat Racing on day of Foley tributes as Saracens, Bath lose
Sports.content:
Brian Gleeson was among the try scorers as Munster beat Racing 92 in Cork on a day of emotion and tributes a decade on from the death of Anthony Foley

A decade to the day since the rugby world learned of head coach Anthony Foley’s death at the age of 42, Munster marked the poignant anniversary with a stirring 33-25 Champions Cup victory over Racing 92.

The night of Friday October 16, 2016 saw Foley pass away in his sleep the night before Munster were due to face Racing in Paris, with their fixture 10 years on staged at Páirc Uí Chaoimh in Cork.

Munster crossed for five tries in a hard-fought contest, with No 8 Brian Gleeson, wearing 24 as Foley's retired No 8 was once again taken out of circulation, joined on the scoresheet by wing Shay McCarthy, lock Tadhg Beirne, replacement Fineen Wycherley and scrum-half Craig Casey.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Racing responded with three tries of their own through wing Wilfried Hulleu, replacement scrum-half Maxime Machenaud and full-back Geronimo Prisciantelli, denying Munster a bonus-point victory. Under the tournament's new rules, teams must score at least three more tries than their opponents to secure the full five points.

The match came a day after the shocking death of Lions second row Hyron Andrews in France ahead of a Champions Cup fixture in La Rochelle. Emotional tributes were paid to both Andrews and Foley before kick-off.

Glasgow, Leinster post big opening away-day victories | Saracens lose at Connacht

Elsewhere, Glasgow Warriors extended their unbeaten start to the new season by pulling away to claim an impressive 47-27 win at Sale Sharks.

The game looked in the balance until late tries from Rory Darge, Ollie Smith and debutant Otavio Tuipulotu helped Glasgow pull away and wrap up a precious bonus-point win.

Leinster made a flying start to their campaign with an emphatic 48-23 victory away to Clermont Auvergne. Tadhg Furlong, Dan Sheehan (two), Sam Prendergast, Jack Conan and Tommy O'Brien all crossed the line, while a penalty try completed a dominant seven-try display.

Connacht pulled off a stunning 45-36 victory over Saracens in Galway, scoring tries through Cian Prendergast (two), Cathal Forde, Shamus Hurley-Langton, Ciaran Frawley (two) and Caolin Blade.

Lions face La Rochelle a day after death of team-mate Andrews

Players stood in silence, with some visibly emotional, as La Rochelle and the Johannesburg-based Lions paid tribute to South African lock Hyron Andrews before Saturday's Champions Cup clash. The 31-year-old died in France on Friday, on the eve of the fixture.
