Sports.title: Kiltie double helps Kilmarnock beat fellow-strugglers Motherwell
Sports.content:
Greg Kiltie scored twice to lift Kilmarnock off the bottom of the Scottish Premiership with a 3-2 victory over Motherwell.

Kiltie struck first and last as Neil McCann's side inflicted a fifth consecutive defeat on the Steelmen, who join Killie in the bottom three, one point off bottom-placed Hibernian.

Motherwell had a dominant spell after recovering from Kiltie's second-minute opener and goals from Alex Lowry and Seb Palmer-Houlden turned the game on its head.

But Tyreece John-Jules soon equalised and Motherwell were cut open before Kiltie knocked home a 69th-minute winner.

Given their run, Motherwell fans would have feared the worst when their team gifted Kilmarnock a goal with little over 60 seconds on the clock.

Goalkeeper Alex Paulsen misplaced a short pass into central midfield and Kiltie ultimately converted after some desperate defending.

Worse almost followed several moments later when Well centre-back Martin Moorman lost possession midway inside his own half, but Joe Hugill dragged his shot wide.

But the visitors levelled in the 17th minute when Lukas Fadinger sent Emmanual Longelo down the left wing. Calum Ferrie made a great stop after Palmer-Houlden got on the end of the left-back's low cross but Lowry kept his composure to fire the rebound into the bottom corner.

Motherwell took control as Killie struggled to keep possession inside their own half. Maswanshise hit the post from 25 yards and scuffed a decent chance wide, and Ibrahim Said forced a good save from Ferrie.

Neil McCann brought on Jamie Brandon for on-loan Hearts right-back MJ Kamson-Kamara in the 33rd minute in a bid to deal with the twin threat of Longelo and Said. He was forced into another change two minutes later when the injured Bailey Rice went off for Aaron Tshibola.

The hosts improved towards the end of the half. Paulsen got down well to stop a John-Jules drive after Motherwell failed to deal with a long ball and the unmarked Tom Lowery volleyed well over.

Killie were grateful for a VAR intervention after referee Calum Scott sent George Stanger off for a high boot on Lowry. The punishment was downgraded to a yellow card after a trip to the monitor.

Motherwell were soon in front in the 56th minute after a low cross from Said. Palmer-Houlden was denied at close range by Ferrie but the ball ricocheted in off the centre-forward.

The visitors' lead only lasted two minutes. Two Motherwell defenders were barged off the ball as Brandon headed the ball back into the box after a half-cleared corner and John-Jules produced an emphatic finish.

Brandon delivered another assist when his crossfield pass played in Kiltie, who again slotted into the far corner.

Paulsen made saves from substitute Ieuan Owen and Hugill to keep Motherwell in it.

Alfred Johansson's side struggled to create chances though, and Ferrie saved from Johnny Koutroumbis deep in stoppage time when the substitute found himself in a good position.

Johansson bemoans 'low-level' defending

Motherwell manager Alfred Johansson:

"I'm very, very disappointed and frustrated with how we end this game. It's extremely difficult to accept the fact that we lost this game.

"Obviously we make it difficult for ourselves right at the start as well, but that can happen in football, you make a mistake and get punished in that way.

"But we reacted fantastically and the rest of the first half is very, very good. We're pressing together, we're aggressive, we catch them on the break, we create chances.

"They start going long into the strikers with one touch and we just don't defend those long balls well enough.

"I don't think we're winning enough second balls and also, prior to the second goal, for instance, we have the ball under control, but we give it away way too easy.

"We have chances to score more than two goals but we can't rely on scoring three goals away from home. We need to be much more solid. It's just way too low a level, how we defend."

McCann: We showed spirit and character

Kilmarnock boss Neil McCann:

"I talk about the spirit that I've got in that dressing room now.

"I talk about the character, with a group of boys that have taken a wee bit of time to come together, and I thought second half we were absolutely brilliant.

"We had a couple of wee things that we tinkered with, in terms of where we wanted to get at Motherwell.

But, tactics aside, that was just about them saying, 'no, we're going to get ourselves back in that game, and we look to go and try and win it'."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Hits & Misses: Liverpool clicking and Chelsea get serious
Sports.content:
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Brentford and Liverpool.

Liverpool spent close to £400m on Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola. Against Brentford, there was evidence that expensively-assembled attack might finally be clicking.

Isak was on the fringes of the game for long periods, limited to only 16 touches by the dogged hosts. But his brilliantly-taken goal, controlled and rifled home with dizzying speed in the second half, was a reminder of just how deadly he can be at his best.

It took him to five goals for the season. Only Erling Haaland has scored more in the Premier League. He is putting a difficult first season behind him and Andoni Iraola will be encouraged that it was Barcola who provided the assist.

The France international came into the game off the back of scoring a hat-trick against LASK in midweek and while he couldn't find the net against Brentford, missing a golden opportunity in the first half and hitting the bar in the second, Iraola liked what he saw.

"I love that he's having so many chances and being in those situations," said the Liverpool boss.

Then there was Wirtz, who provided the assist for Victor Munoz with a perfectly-weighted through-ball.

It was one of nine chances created - the joint-most by any Liverpool player in a single game since Opta started taking records in 2003/04.

Nick Wright

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Everton and Chelsea.

Chelsea have the best front three in the Premier League but attack being the best form of defence for Xabi Alonso was never going to be sustainable. No team had conceded more goals than Chelsea's 13 after six Premier League matches.

But, in Saturday's 2-0 victory at Everton, they showed a different side to their game. Remarkably, this was not only Alonso's first clean sheet in the league since his appointment but also Chelsea's first clean sheet in the league for nine months.

Defensively, Chelsea have been a liability for some time. Alonso must fix that if his team are to take the leap and challenge again. The win at Everton was a step in the right direction. In the manager's words, Chelsea produced a "serious" and "mature" performance.

These are the characteristics that will differentiate Chelsea from most of the chasing pack in a Premier League season where seriousness is sorely lacking among some of the so-called 'Big Six'. Alonso, clearly, is a serious manager.

Zinny Boswell

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Manchester City and Ipswich Town.

Lauding Erling Haaland's goalscoring prowess is clearly not a hot take. It's barely even news. But he is outdoing even his own outlandish standards so far this season.

Twelve goals across all competitions; four just this week, including two in Man City's most recent victory over Ipswich.

Haaland is a symbol of City's immense wealth in a myriad of ways. He's a wealth of talent, leadership and obviously goals.

But he also represents the riches of a club transformed beyond recognition since its Abu Dhabi takeover. The very thing under intense investigation by the Premier League.

Haaland too hot to handle Erling Haaland has now netted 100 non-penalty goals in the Premier League, reaching this milestone in fewer appearances than any other player (139).

Haaland is indeed a complete luxury. A high-end sports car with all the optional extras. Everything about him is premium. There is every chance he will go on to be the most ruthless striker the Premier League has ever seen.

And yet, many will still come to view this era of Manchester City through a different lens - no matter the outcome of the club's ongoing appeal process. Too much has already been aired.

It's a shame Haaland's immense gift cannot be celebrated for what it is in its truest form. Perhaps in the future it will be again. Because he really is a different breed of scorer.

Laura Hunter

In patches, Newcastle's performance against Aston Villa epitomised the heavy-metal, high-pressing football that defines Mattihas Jaissle's school of Red Bull philosophy. When executed well, it's high-octane and overwhelming for an opponent.

But Newcastle's approach at times seemed to be all-out chaos, planned or otherwise. The Premier League is defined by its physicality, but two yellow cards at the same time for Joelinton and Sven Botman tackles is not something we see often. The latter should also have been sent off.

The Magpies were continuously exposed by Aston Villa's transition and counter, especially in the first half, and the chaos only continued when Dan Burn came on late on as a No 9. You are only using a centre-back up front when you are desperate for a goal or rotating because you have too many. This fell into the former camp.

Amid all this, Newcastle had just one shot on target in the whole game and set a new record for goals conceded in consecutive matches at home in all competitions (16). There were bright moments, but no sense of real cohesion.

The stats this season show that whatever Jaissle is attempting is not working. A change in system coupled with a new, young squad is only exacerbating things and if the German wants to continue the gung-ho approach, it needs to be harnessed in a far better and more productive way.

Charlotte Marsh

A headline taken from Sky Sports commentator Gary Weaver, who so eloquently epitomised Aston Villa's last few seasons.

It took them seven matches to win a game last term and while it did not take as long this time around, questions were being asked about whether Unai Emery's glorious revolution at Aston Villa was finally beginning to falter.

A summer exodus coupled with an intense season in which they won the Europa League - had it all come to a head?

No such luck.

Emery is a demanding manager. He's known to hold hours-long meetings and high-intensity training sessions to get the best out of his players. That takes time to adapt to, as Tyrone Mings noted in his post-match interview with Sky Sports.

Rebuilding a team is never easy but Emery is starting to find the solutions, as he always does. Aston Villa are now unbeaten in five games and have kept back-to-back clean sheets.

The clocks go back next Sunday - as Weaver predicted, right on time for Aston Villa to start their charge up the Premier League table.

Charlotte Marsh

An ominous stat was provided by Opta during the build-up to Brentford's clash with Liverpool at the Gtech.

"Since their promotion to the top flight in 2021, the Bees have dropped more points from winning positions than any other side in the Premier League (102)."

A surprise, perhaps, given the Bees have taken to the top flight so well and finished in the top half in three of their first five seasons. And one that poses the question: what could have been?

For Brentford fans, that will not bear thinking about.

But that figure increased to 105 on Saturday, as they took the lead against the Reds before falling to a 2-1 defeat in a game they ended with nine men on the pitch.

Without the first of those reds - shown to Yehor Yarmoliuk before half-time, it might have been different. The reality? It's 11 points dropped for the season now, more than any other team in the division.

It has become a horrible habit - and one that needs kicking in to touch by Keith Andrews' men if those European ambitions are to materialise.

Dan Long

Could this be the turning point in Alvaro Arbeloa's Fulham reign?

It is certainly a start. With reports suggesting the Spaniard had two games to save his job, he needed a response and his players delivered one.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Fulham and Hull City.

Fulham played with an intensity and attacking fluency that had been missing during their winless start to the Premier League season.

They registered 10 first-half shots, moved the ball quickly and repeatedly exposed a Hull side who struggled to impose themselves. Alex Iwobi's goal was deserved, but the hosts could easily have won by a greater margin.

There were encouraging signs of an identity taking shape, with the performance even prompting thoughts of 'Arbeloa-ball' at Craven Cottage.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alvaro Arbeloa feels the support from the Fulham owners and believes Joshua King has everything and can become a top, top player.

Yet one result cannot erase the concerns of the opening weeks, and Fulham made the closing stages unnecessarily nervy before Ryan Sessegnon's stoppage-time red card.

The win lifts them out of the relegation zone and gives Arbeloa breathing space.

Whether it proves a turning point depends on what follows. For now, he has bought himself time and shown what his Fulham side can be.

William Bitibiri

Sports.title: Kartal hails mentality after 'dream come true' run to Wuhan Open final
Sports.content:
Britain's Sonay Kartal says making her maiden WTA 1000 final at the Wuhan Open is a "dream come true," adding that the mental side of sport is "one of my strongest assets."

Kartal became only the second British woman, after Johanna Konta (Beijing 2016, Miami 2017, Rome 2019), to reach a WTA 1000 final with a stunning 7-6 (11-9) 7-6 (7-5) victory over Jelena Ostapenko.

The 24-year-old, playing in only her third tournament since returning from a back injury, saved multiple set points to punish Ostapenko, despite the Latvian hitting an astonishing 50 winners in the match.

Kartal will take on Maja Chwalinska in Sunday's final, live on Sky Sports Tennis from 11.30am, after the French Open finalist upset fellow Pole and former world No 1 Iga Swiatek 7-5 6-1.

"Today was a dream come true," Kartal told media.

"I've been shooting to get this far in one of these events for a very long time and to be able to do it this fast after so long out, is special.

"I think for me to have had in my box today all the people that got me feeling fit and ready to go and injury-free, it's a special moment for me and a special moment for the rest of my team."

Currently 170th in the WTA rankings, Kartal - the lowest-ranked player to reach the final in Wuhan - will break inside the top 50 and become the new British No 1

Since the format's introduction in 1990, Kartal has become just the second player to defeat five former finalists en route to a WTA-1000 final, after Naomi Osaka in Montreal in 2005.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kartal described reaching her first ever WTA 1000 final as a huge milestone after beating Jelena Ostapenko to make the Wuhan Open last two

'I've been underdog in every match here'

Her victory over Ostapenko extended a remarkable series of wins against former Olympic champion Belinda Bencic, ex-Wimbledon finalist Jasmine Paolini, and world No 6 Elina Svitolina.

"I think in every match, I've kind of been the underdog in this event," she added. "So I think the only pressure is kind of the pressure that I'm putting on myself.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Wuhan Open quarter-final between Elina Svitolina and Kartal

"Regardless of how long I spent out, I still expect to offer a good performance and I'm very proud of what I've managed to achieve this week.

"There's a lot of first-time things that I've managed to do. So with each match, I've grown in confidence, and the atmosphere today was amazing.

"It's a special feeling to walk out onto that court. The battle was a true battle, it's what I expected. And I'm very proud of just how I handled the occasion and everything that was going on in the match."

'The mental side of sport one of my strongest assets'

After reaching the fourth round of Indian Wells in March, Kartal missed three of this year's four Grand Slams, including Wimbledon after six months out with a stress fracture in her back, returning last month at the Billie Jean King Cup Finals.

Previously ranked as high as No 44 in the world, she showed positive signs by reaching the third round in Beijing earlier this month, but scarcely could have expected such a level of success so soon.

"I think mentally, it is one of my biggest assets on the tennis court. I think I managed to stay very calm in a lot of situations that can probably get a little heated and you can get frustrated with.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kartal discussed her back injury after reaching the semi-finals of the Wuhan Open and whether she will get a celebratory tattoo if she wins

"I just really try and use that to my advantage. I can maybe see her getting a bit upset and emotional on the other side, so I know at that point it's time for me to just knuckle down and not let her distract me.

"But yeah, I've been lucky mentally, I think a lot of players have to work on it, but for me, it's just something that's always been ingrained in me.

"I think also having no pressure this week has obviously helped, and with each win, you just gain more confidence. I think this week there's been an accumulation of a lot of good things that have helped me keep my composure."

Fleming: Kartal playing the tennis of her life

Sky Sports Tennis' Colin Fleming on Sonay Kartal:

"Her ability to stay in the present got her through. She kept cool to ultimately outlast Ostapenko, who hit 50 winners past her and still couldn't win a set.

"Just a brilliant achievement and the run doesn't stop here. She's playing the tennis of her life and she's got every chance of getting her hands on the title.

"It's just so impressive the way she takes it all in her stride. Fascinating to hear her say this was a win for her mentality because it did carry her across the line in both sets when Ostapenko was losing it really.

"Kartal was there, composed, and ready to take her chances when it came. Every reason for me to think she's going to play a good match in the final. I'm not saying she's going to win but that's exciting to know.

"I have full confidence she's going to handle that occasion, play her tennis, which has been exceptional this week, and assuming she does that she'll give herself every chance."

Watch Sonay Kartal versus Maja Chwalinska in the Wuhan Open final live on Sky Sports Tennis from 11.30am on Sunday. Stream tennis with no contract on NOW and through the Sky Sports App.

Sports.title: Cameron equaliser earns a point for Dundee United at St Johnstone
Sports.content:
Lyall Cameron's 79th-minute strike earned Dundee United a deserved 1-1 draw at St Johnstone.

United trailed at half-time to a Josh Fowler goal, the striker's sixth of the Scottish Premiership campaign.

The league's top scorer did not make it out for the second half due to illness and Simo Valakari's side were unable to repeat the trick of last Sunday in Aberdeen when they successfully defended a 1-0 lead.

Jim Goodwin simply had too many creative and attacking options to throw at their hosts.

Despite a decent defensive stand from the hosts, Cameron struck the second goal of his impressive loan spell from Rangers.

The clubs are locked on 12 points in the top half of the table after encouraging starts to the campaign.

The visitors had been dominant for the opening 20 minutes, cutting through Saints at will. Cheick Diabate, on return from suspension, helped them out with jittery early moments.

Jesse Randall was a danger down United's favoured right flank and Dan Finlayson spared Diabate by charging down the winger's netbound shot. Idjessi Metsoko met a Joshua Rawlins cross six yards out but headed weakly into Toby Steward's arms.

On the opposite flank, Michael Forbes sent Daniel Bennie darting down the inside left channel. Diabate's swiped clearance off the QPR loanee's low delivery came within inches of his own net.

Saints settled thereafter and forced Jack Walton into action on 17 minutes. Sam Stanton's shot on the spin was forced away by the United keeper at full stretch.

Four minutes later, the hosts were in front.

Image: St Johnstone's Josh Fowler opened the scoring against Dundee United

United lost track of Fowler as Enes Alic's teasing cross from the left hit the six-yard box. This was perfect preying territory for an on-form scorer and Fowler pounced to prod home.

United failed to recapture their early momentum. Saints keeper Steward coped comfortably in the 40th minute with Dylan Tait's long-range effort.

Ruari Paton came on for Fowler at the break and teed up Taylor Steven. The Scotland Under-21 cap was wayward with his effort.

Paton saw his own shot spilled by Walton who recovered to block from Stanton's follow-up. But that was about all Saints had to offer by way of attacking threat.

It was all United who grew in threat with Zac Sapsford and Lachlan Rose up top. The excellent Finlayson helped Saints defend their penalty box well.

However, they were worn down 11 minutes from time. Randall delivered a low ball into the box and Sapsford's shrewd dummy helped it reach Cameron.

The midfielder was nudged by Liam Smith and a penalty could have been awarded. However, Cameron kept his balance and cool to tuck home high past Steward.

Steward pulled off a great stop after 90 minutes from Sapsford to preserve a point for Saints.

Goodwin: Players rose to challenge

Dundee United boss Jim Goodwin:

"When you're a goal behind at half-time, you're questioning the character.

"You want to see if the players have what it takes to get themselves back into the game.

"I felt the goal was coming and, if we did get that equaliser, that we would potentially go on and win the game.

"Some of our build-up was a little bit too laboured at times; a little bit too slow.

"We asked the players: Could we speed things up a little bit and play forward earlier? And don't allow St Johnstone to get their shape back behind the ball.

"In the second half, I thought we completely dominated the game."

Valakari: Fair result - I enjoyed it!

St Johnstone boss Simo Valakari:

"It was a fair result. Both teams made it difficult for each other and were going for the winner at the end. I enjoyed the game.

"Josh (Fowler0 was ill overnight. He decided he could start but after about 35 minutes it looked like he might need to be taken off.

"I couldn't waste a window to make changes, so he was able to push for us to get to half-time.

"Now he needs to recover. It says a lot about Josh that he can still score a goal like that and make the runs he did when feeling ill. I had it earlier in the week, so I know what it's like!

"Getting a chance to score a goal is good medicine for a striker! That's why we love him and he is scoring goals - he has this desire that never goes away."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Manzambi maintains Aston Villa progress with win to seal dismal week for Newcastle
Sports.content:
There is a reason why Aston Villa were so desperate to hijack Johan Manzambi’s proposed summer move from Freiburg to Newcastle. The tall, quick, tricky, clever and perfectly balanced 21-year-old Switzerland attacking midfielder looked worth every penny of the record £50m plus fee Villa ended up paying and he duly delighted in showing Tynesiders what they missed.

For Newcastle and their disconsolate manager, Matthias Jaissle, there was a cruel irony that Manzambi ended up heading the winner on a day when the Premier League’s CEO, Richard Masters, was in the directors’ box to watch arguably the two teams most affected by the spending rules imposed during his tenure.

Those regulations have turned Unai Emery into a master of reinvention at Aston Villa but, in the league at least, the Spaniard’s latest rebuild has been slow to click cleanly into place. On the evidence of their fourth win in five games in all competitions, that just might be changing.

While Villa kicked off having won only once in the league this season, Newcastle sought redemption after last Monday night’s chastening 4-1 defeat at Coventry.

Emery, who changed his mind about taking charge of Newcastle before Eddie Howe took the job, said: “It was a tough match but it was very important to win after our poor start. But we set a high standard.”

Jaissle, whose team are level on points with Villa but faces an appreciably tougher reconstruction project, was left to reflect on his “frustration” and blamed his young team’s decision making. But Newcastle’s manager was also sanguine. “Big names left the club in the summer so for sure, we knew it would be challenging,” he said. “That’s not an excuse, we have to learn fast.”

View image in fullscreen Johan Manzambi strikes a pose after scoring the winner. Photograph: Paul Ellis/AFP/Getty Images

There has always been a certain edge between these teams and Jarred Gillett issued two first-half yellow cards in quick succession. First Joelinton lunged in, two-footed, on Manzambi and then Sven Botman was guilty of another reckless challenge, two-footed and over the ball, on the dangerous Nicolas Jackson.

A video assistant referee check ensued but, after lengthy deliberation, it was decided the original decision was correct and Botman’s yellow did not require upgrading to a red. The Newcastle centre-half was probably a little fortunate. “It was so high it nearly broke my leg,” said Jackson. “But I’m OK; it’s part of football.”

Joelinton, meanwhile, has now been booked in each of the two games he has been involved in since returning from injury as a substitute at Coventry. Plus ça change.

The elegantly impressive Manzambi, seemingly electrically powered, exerted the best sort of revenge on the Brazilian when he gave Emery’s side the lead. That goal arrived in the 36th minute and involved an unmarked Manzambi – a creator brilliant at drifting into space – ghosting away from Malick Thiaw before meeting João Gomes’s splendid cross with a tremendous header.

Newcastle suddenly looked extremely vulnerable but they were reprieved when Emiliano Buendía’s shot rebounded off the inside of a post and deflected off Lukas Hornicek’s back before eventually being cleared by Lewis Hall. Once again, Hall was Jaissle’s best player.

View image in fullscreen Unai Emery secured his 100th Premier League victory but it was another game to forget for Matthias Jaissle. Photograph: Ian MacNicol/Getty Images

It was all too easy to see why Newcastle have now gone 13 Premier League home games without a clean sheet, equalling an unwanted record set in 1998-99.

Jaissle’s frustration surfaced itself as he exchanged words with Emery after an altercation involving Alysson and Hornicek and subsequently looked suitably downcast as his side were booed off at half-time.

Those home fans were not relishing the sight of Villa’s forward repeatedly accelerating behind the sometimes dangerously high home backline.

Quick Guide Newcastle 0-1 Aston Villa key facts Show • Newcastle United are now without a home clean sheet in each of their last 16 games in all competitions; it's the longest run in their history. • Yoane Wissa’s seven shots on goal with none on target is the most by a player in a Premier League game since Newcastle teammate Harvey Barnes against Brentford in April 2025 (also 7). • Unai Emery (pictured) has earned his 100th Premier League win as a manager, doing so in his 197th game in the competition (D44 L53), only eight managers have done so in fewer games in the competition’s history. Opta Photograph: Ed Sykes/REUTERS Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Zion Suzuki had been rather underemployed but a goalkeeper briefly courted by Newcastle in the summer opened the second half by making a superlative flying save to keep Botman’s high velocity strike out. It was Newcastle’s sole shot on target.

The Villa substitute Ross Barkley almost showed Jaissle’s players how to do it when he would have scored with his first touch had Hornicek not dived smartly to turn his blistering shot around a post.

Although Newcastle’s manager sent Dan Burn on for the closing minutes – as a striker – nothing was going to come between Emery and his 100th Premier League win.

Sports.title: Haaland helps Maresca achieve record start as Manchester City defeat Ipswich
Sports.content:
There have been few winners in Manchester City’s guilty verdict, except highly paid lawyers and the inflatable fruit industry. The fans have suffered, being forced to question everything they have been told, while being labelled “cheats”, but they were able to forget the cacophony of noise around the club as Enzo Maresca became the first Premier League manager to win his first seven games.

Ipswich were the latest victims, but they put up a fight in City’s first home Premier League game since being found to have breached financial rules. Defiance has fortified most of the City fanbase, who were able to see local boy Phil Foden instigate the triumph with a kiss of the badge, before an emblem of their wealth, Erling Haaland, secured the points to move six clear, albeit with a few scares between, courtesy of Daizen Maeda and Zian Flemming.

“I didn’t expect to win seven out of seven, but we are working well,” Maresca said. “This is the most important thing.”

Victory came at a cost as Haaland and Antoine Semenyo limped off at full-time, in addition to Mateo Kovacic, Matheus Nunes and Nico O’Reilly suffering injuries, although Maresca was left unsure of the severity as City prepare to host AEK Athens on Tuesday.

If City have felt like it has been their backs against the wall for the past few weeks, it was Ipswich’s turn. Gary O’Neil put 11 men behind the ball whenever the hosts ventured over the halfway line as City enjoyed 90% possession in the opening quarter-hour, but without truly threatening as they struggled to find space in the lowest of blocks, expertly organised and fully disciplined.

Maresca had made six changes to refresh the side and it took time to understand one another’s rhythm, with Ayyoub Bouaddi creating it from defensive midfield in another mature performance from the teenager making his first Premier League start.

View image in fullscreen Enzo Maresca has guided Manchester City a record seven-match winning start in the Premier League. Photograph: Michael Steele/Getty Images

It was inevitable what was coming as there was irrefutable evidence that City were dominant. As at Anfield, Jérémy Doku was a key instigator, showing mesmeric skill on the left of the area before finding Foden to sweep home for his first goal since mid-December.

“I know him from years ago, for me he’s one of the best Premier League players,” Maresca said. “Since day one, it’s my duty to help him to be again one of the best players. I’m very happy for his goal and hopefully it can be just the beginning of many goals and many good performances.”

There was an element of pantomime around the ground from the booing of the Premier League anthem, the singalongs and inflatables. It was fitting Marc Guéhi did not know Maeda was behind him, allowing the Ipswich man to latch on to a sublime curved through ball from Abdoul Ouattara and equalise two minutes after the opener.

Quick Guide Manchester City 3-2 Ipswich key facts Show • With Manchester City maintaining their 100% record, Enzo Maresca is the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a team. • Manchester City are the third team to win their opening seven games of a Premier League season, after Liverpool in 2019-20 (first 8) and Chelsea in 2005-06 (first 9). • Erling Haaland (pictured) has now scored 100 non-penalty goals in the Premier League, reaching this milestone in fewer appearances than any other player (139). The previous fewest was 150 appearances, by Alan Shearer in 1996. Opta Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

After a missed chance, Haaland showed it is possible to get a better result second time around, making the most of Kovacic becoming an auxiliary winger. The header lacked power, but Christian Walton could not keep it out, palming the ball from one hand to the other and into the net before Haaland was serenaded with the clap of bananas.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

City found themselves stuck in a lull, unable to prise open Ipswich, instead having to bide their time. It was a test of patience and a sweeping move upfield concluded with a precision pass from Iliman Ndiaye and an aggressive finish from Haaland, who was later denied a hat-trick by the video assistant referee.

View image in fullscreen Manchester City fans have gone back to more innocent times with their inflatable bananas. Photograph: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty Images

Farai Hallam reviewed footage of Guéhi taking out Abdul Fatawu in the area and Flemming did the rest in the 90th minute, as reward for an impressive team performance, leaving O’Neil upset Ipswich departed with nothing.

“They’re an incredible group,” he said. “Players giving everything. It’s a privilege to stand there and represent them because they’re an incredible group.”

City were left to complain about a Premier League official’s decision when 12 minutes was added on, with few knowing why, but this result will not be questioned.

Maresca called on his team to make their own noise while a cacophony swirls around them, but on-pitch success will not speak louder while what is happening off it is unresolved. The fans sang about relegation and trips to Stockport, embracing a dark situation with humour to match.

Sports.title: Isak completes Liverpool’s comeback win as Brentford finish with nine
Sports.content:
If Liverpool’s spluttering forwards end up remembering this as the day when their luck turned then they will owe a big debt of gratitude to Yehor Yarmolyuk. This was a game with a very clear before and after.

Andoni Iraola will hope surviving one of the toughest tests the Premier League has to offer is a sign his methods are starting to work, but Liverpool’s manager will not forget it was a very different contest after Yarmolyuk’s red card for a butt on Jérémy Jacquet left Brentford trying to defend a 1-0 lead with 10 men for the entire second half.

Brentford, who later lost Vitaly Janelt to a second yellow card, could not hold out. They raged at John Brooks’s officiating after their unbeaten start ended, but they had only themselves to blame after tumbling out of the top four. Brentford pressed the self-destruct button when they had Liverpool on the ropes. Yarmolyuk was never going to get away it in the video assistant referee era and Liverpool made the midfielder pay.

Iraola was delighted with how an attack worth close to £400m made the numerical advantage count after half-time. Most important was a telling contribution from Florian Wirtz. The £100m signing has struggled with the responsibility of playing as Liverpool’s No 10 since joining from Bayer Leverkusen, but this time he was decisive. The clever pass to release Victor Muñoz for a sharp equaliser was his second assist of the season and was followed by Bradley Barcola creating a goal for the first time since his move for an initial £106m from Paris Saint-Germain, the French winger’s header teeing up Alexander Isak to complete the turnaround in the 70th minute and lift Liverpool into fifth place.

The challenge is to push on. Isak’s Liverpool career has been stop-start since his £125m move from Newcastle, injuries holding the forward back. The Spaniard was critical of some sloppy finishing from Barcola, but was readier to dish out the praise for Wirtz’s intelligence in tight spaces in the second half. It feels significant that both of Wirtz’s assists have come for Muñoz.

“A good battle today,” Iraola said before switching focus to Barcola and Wirtz. “Both had a lot of influence. Bradley and Flo, they are players that against 10 men are lovely to have.”

There was not much between the sides before Yarmolyuk’s rush of blood to the head. Isak returned after missing last week’s defeat to Manchester City and Liverpool shaded the early openings. Barcola almost punished an error from Janelt, only to miss a chance to build on his midweek hat-trick against LASK. Isak nodded over from a good position.

Brentford responded with a series of fast breaks and Liverpool had to be strong. They looked readier for the threat posed by Brentford than when they folded in this fixture under Arne Slot 12 months ago. Jacquet, quietly impressive in central defence, made a crucial tackle to deny Igor Thiago. The initial problem for Liverpool was more their expensive attack was yet to gel.

Michael Kayode was keeping Barcola in check and Keane Lewis-Potter was edging his battle with Muñoz. Wirtz was timid and Liverpool’s worries grew when they lost Dominik Szoboszlai to injury.

With Ryan Gravenberch suspended, Liverpool were light on midfield options. Trey Nyoni replaced Szoboszali and the 19-year-old’s introduction was followed by a whirlwind spell. Iraola was unhappy when Liverpool had a penalty overturned as replays showed Dango Outtara got a clear touch on the ball before colliding with Alexis Mac Allister.

View image in fullscreen Yehor Yarmolyuk leaves the pitch after being shown the red card. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

Brentford were pumped up after the VAR intervention and soon made Liverpool rue a failure to clear their lines. The ball came back too easily, Mac Allister backed off Thiago, who crossed for Lewis-Potter to run in from left-back and head into the top corner.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“We were edging it,” Keith Andrews said. Brentford’s manager wants his team “to play on the edge”, but felt too many decisions went Liverpool’s way. However, he had no complaints about the first red. He said Liverpool were “cute and clever” during the incident, but promised that Yarmolyuk would learn from his mistake.

They were into six added minutes at the end of the first half when the midfielder clashed with Jacquet before a Liverpool corner. It was more of a jut than a proper blow, but it was enough to justify the sending off. Brooks checked the pitchside monitor and his decision was not a surprise.

Liverpool took a while to adjust in the second half. They encountered further complications when injury forced Jeremie Frimpong off seven minutes after replacing Ronald Araújo at right-back. Mac Allister let fly from distance, but Caoimhín Kelleher saved and Rio Ngumoha, on for Frimpong, crossed for Virgil van Dijk to volley wide.

Quick Guide Brentford 1-2 Liverpool key facts Show • Florian Wirtz is the first player to create nine or more chances from open play in a Premier League game since Sadio Mané against Burnley in January 2021 (9), also for Liverpool, and first in an away match since Samir Nasri for Manchester City v Spurs in August 2011 (10). Victor Muñoz (pictured centre, with Wirtz and Trey Nyoni) scored from one of them. • Liverpool’s Alexander Isak has scored in all five of his Premier League appearances against Brentford (5 goals); only Erling Haaland v Crystal Palace (6) has a better 100% rate in the competition. • Brentford received two red cards in the same league game for the first time since April 2013 against Sheffield United in League One. Opta Photograph: Peter Cziborra/REUTERS Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Brentford began to wobble and they were caught on the counterattack in the 62nd minute. Wirtz dropped back and played a clever pass inside Lewis-Potter. Muñoz raced clear, cut back and drilled a low shot into the far corner with his left foot.

The change in mood was dramatic. Barcola sliced a volley just wide, but the winner was coming. Mac Allister took a pass from Wirtz and crossed. Barcola headed down and Isak finished from close range.

Iraola was not happy with Liverpool’s play once they led. Brentford threatened an equaliser through Thiago and Liverpool were too rushed. There are flaws to iron out, but this was a positive week for Iraola.

Sports.title: Pressure on Arbeloa lifted after Alex Iwobi sinks Hull for Fulham’s first win
Sports.content:
It was not until his post-match lap of the pitch that Álvaro Arbeloa allowed himself a smile. After an uncomfortable week when his future was being called into question, the former Real Madrid manager has a Premier League win under his belt at the seventh attempt, lifting his side off the foot of the table. But it is not a win without caveats.

Alex Iwobi’s goal in the first half should have been one of many, with the Nigeria winger among those guilty of missing gilt-edge chances. Gonzalo García, who has not scored in the league since the opening weekend of the season, headed against the crossbar from close range in the second half.

Fulham ended with 10 men after Ryan Sessegnon’s red card in stoppage time, but it did not matter against a toothless Hull side, who are now winless in five.

With Fulham also a goal up against Ipswich last Saturday and Manchester United here before the international break before dropping vital points, you could forgive Arbeloa for the stern expression he wore as his team continued to pass up opportunities.

“I saw this movie before,” he said. “I didn’t have the feeling we were in danger, but in football you never know. In one second, any team can score.

“It is so important to get the chances [converted] because you want to play the last minutes with a little more calm. It’s better to win 2-0 than 1-0, even in a game like that where we were a much better team.”

This was a sentiment shared by Hull, whose lack of quality at either end of the pitch was another caveat. “That was the worst performance since I’m here,” said their head coach, Sergej Jakirovic, who is in danger of a promising start fizzling out. “You see in every challenge, they were stronger. Every challenge, they ate us alive.”

View image in fullscreen Referee Chris Kavanagh shows a red card to Ryan Sessegnon (left) of Fulham after his foul on Robinio Vaz. Photograph: Ryan Pierse/Getty Images

This was the type of performance Fulham would have expected when it appointed Arbeloa as Marco Silva’s successor in the summer. It was a move designed to bring a more entertaining style to Craven Cottage after four years of Premier League stability in midtable – the Spaniard brought five members of staff with him from Real Madrid and three players.

There was plenty of creativity on show against Hull, especially from the wingers Iwobi and Oscar Bobb. They started fast, with Iwobi sending a curling shot on to the roof of the net from the left and Bobb a constant threat on the right.

It was from an attack down the right that Fulham produced their winner. Hull’s left wing-back, Brooke Norton-Cuffy, held off Josh King, but failed to clear and Sander Berge poked the ball into Iwobi’s path. His first-time shot should not have troubled the goalkeeper, Konstantinos Tzolakis, but it squirmed under his rolling dive at the near post after coming through a crowd of bodies.

View image in fullscreen Fulham’s Alex Iwobi (centre) scores the only goal of the game. Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PA

Jakirovic needed to find answers at half-time and he replaced the centre-back Lucas Herrington, who had been booked for one of his fouls on the elusive King, with the midfielder Tim Iroegbunam. After a bright breakthrough season in the first team, the 19-year-old King is expected to push on. He was allowed to roam against Hull’s low block and after neatly combining with Shea Charles should have doubled their lead, but his low shot was too close to Tzolakis.

A smart turn from King away from Semi Ajayi preceded a chance that Iwobi, with time and the whole goal to aim at, should have buried, but he telegraphed his low effort for Tzolakis to read and smother. García was unmarked at the back post when he headed Iwobi’s cross against the bar, but Hull provided such little threat that what could have been a nervy ending, especially after Sessegnon’s stoppage-time dismissal for leaving his studs on Robinio Vaz’s achilles, was anything but.

With the pressure now relieved a little and his ideas evidently translating to his players, will the often stoney-faced Arbeloa feel more relaxed at training? “I always try to smile,” he said. “Even when you are losing, it’s even more important that you try to smile.”

Sports.title: Boos for Arsenal as draw with Birmingham extends winless WSL run
Sports.content:
An equaliser from Olivia Smith averted defeat for Arsenal, but a home draw with Birmingham did little to calm fears for Renée Slegers’s future as Gunners coach. Boos accompanied the final whistle at the Emirates Stadium, as the result left Arsenal on six points from six matches and without a win in five Women’s Super League matches, the club’s longest winless run in WSL history. They are eighth in the table, nine points behind the leaders, Manchester City, who have played one game fewer.

Birmingham opened the scoring at the start of the second half when Océane Hurtré coolly tapped in after her run from the halfway line went unchecked. Alessia Russo had hit the woodwork in the first half with a diving header, among a slew of Arsenal chances as Sophie Baggaley was kept the busier of the goalkeepers.

“I don’t think we created enough in the first half,” said Slegers. “Second half is different. There was one player we needed to stop and that was Hurtré. But she came through in a fast break and a counter, we don’t defend that well enough.”

After Smith’s spectacular strike, in the 66th minute, curled from outside the area, Arsenal would not find the winning goal that might ease pressure on Slegers. Baggaley’s goalkeeping and slack finishing meant Birmingham secured their point. “We are in a scenario we’ve had too many times season,” said Slegers.

Next week for Arsenal is a north London derby with Tottenham, who kick off at Chelsea in fourth on Sunday. Slegers said: “The next game is always the next opportunity. [It’s good] we always keep going and we rise after setbacks.

“We just need to put ourselves in better positions earlier so that’s not necessary every time because it takes energy from the team having to play those scenarios. But yes, the team has been brilliant. The urgency, the willingness, the desire in the second half was really good.”

Despite those boos at the final whistle, Smith said of the home fans: “They always bring out great support, [we’re] so happy to have them here. Again, disappointed not to get the result, must be frustrating for them, but they stay with us and support us.”

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Rangers miss chance to go top after pulsating draw with Dundee
Sports.content:
Rangers passed up the chance to go top of the Premiership in a pulsating 2-2 draw against Dundee at Dens Park. The home side took a deserved lead in the 38th minute through the striker Bradley Fink but the returning Gers attacker Badredine Bouanani fired in a stunning equaliser three minutes later with his first goal for the club.

Derek McInnes’s side came out re-energised for the second half and took the lead on the hour with the midfielder Nico Raskin’s long-range drive but in the 68th minute the midfielder Callum Jones took advantage of Gers slackness to level. Dundee were well worth a point, with Rangers moving one point behind Celtic, who can increase their lead at home to Hearts on Sunday.

Greg Kiltie scored twice to lift Kilmarnock off the bottom with a 3-2 home victory over Motherwell. Kiltie struck first and last as Neil McCann’s side inflicted a fifth consecutive defeat on the Steelmen, who join Killie in the bottom three, one point above bottom-placed Hibernian.

Motherwell had a dominant spell after recovering from Kiltie’s second-minute opener and goals from Alex Lowry and Seb Palmer-Houlden turned the game on its head. But Tyreece John-Jules soon equalised and Motherwell were cut open before Kiltie knocked home a 69th-minute winner.

View image in fullscreen Greg Kiltie celebrates scoring his second goal against Motherwell, which proved to be Kilmarnock’s winner. Photograph: Mark Runnacles/Shutterstock

Motherwell’s manager, Alfred Johansson, bemoaned his side’s defending, saying: “I’m very, very disappointed and frustrated with how we end this game. It’s extremely difficult to accept the fact that we lost this game. We have chances to score more than two goals but we can’t rely on scoring three goals away from home. We need to be much more solid. It’s just way too low a level, how we defend.”

Falkirk secured an entertaining 2-1 win at Hibernian. Their only other league victory this term was at home to Hearts in September.

In a game that went from end to end, Jacob Murrell put Falkirk 2-0 ahead inside 37 minutes, before Hibs struck back with an Owen Elding goal. The home side dominated the second half, but could not bag an equaliser.

Aberdeen returned to winning ways as a 3-1 victory over St Mirren moved them above their opponents, who have now lost five straight matches. Brad Lyons gave the hosts the lead in spectacular fashion after two minutes, but the Buddies went on to dominate the first half and levelled through Eseosa Sule. In a much-improved second-half display strikes from Kevin Nisbet and Ayoub Mouloua gave the Dons three points. Aberdeen are seventh.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Lyall Cameron’s 79th-minute strike earned Dundee United a 1-1 draw at St Johnstone. United trailed at half-time to a Josh Fowler goal, the striker’s sixth of the Premiership campaign. The league’s top scorer did not make it out for the second half due to illness and Simo Valakari’s side were unable to repeat the trick of last Sunday in Aberdeen when they successfully defended a 1-0 lead.

Jim Goodwin had too many creative and attacking options to throw at their hosts and despite a decent defensive stand from the hosts, Cameron struck the second goal of his impressive loan spell from Rangers. The clubs are locked together on 12 points in the top half of the table after encouraging starts to the campaign, with the Saints in fifth on goal difference.

Sports.title: Neto double at Everton leads Chelsea to victory marred by Martínez head injury
Sports.content:
Chelsea have returned from the international break with a spirit, authority and resilience that augurs well for Xabi Alonso. Their troubles at Everton, not a happy hunting ground in recent years, were confined to the seven minutes Emi Martínez needed treatment for a head injury as Pedro Neto’s double delivered a deserved victory in the Merseyside sunshine.

The Argentina goalkeeper was taken to hospital for tests after an accidental collision with Jarrad Branthwaite left him with suspected concussion. “When he left the stadium he was conscious,” Alonso said. “Hopefully it is not too bad but we need to wait.” A first Premier League clean sheet since January, and a second successive win since losing at Brentford before the Nations League break, were otherwise secured with a minimum of fuss in a commanding second-half performance.

“It’s one day,” the Chelsea manager replied when asked whether victory, built on a feisty first-half display and mature second, provided evidence of the mentality he craves at Stamford Bridge. “We need to repeat it again and again and again to know for sure but the mentality was very good. Sometimes it’s not about playing nice but playing good football, winning many second balls and being efficient. We need a game like this. The feeling at Brentford was that it was not enough. Today has been better but it’s just one. When it’s 10 clean sheets …”

There were goalkeeping problems at both ends of the field, with Jordan Pickford unconvincing for the second week in a row for Everton. David Moyes’s side edged the first half and could have legitimate complaints about Morgan Rogers avoiding a second yellow card moments before the break. But from Pickford’s weak attempt to stop Neto’s opener to Thierno Barry missing their one big chance of the contest, there were self-inflicted wounds in Everton’s first defeat of the season.

“It wasn’t that we played that badly overall,” said Moyes. “We just didn’t create enough which meant if we did anything wrong defensively it would count against us.” So it proved.

There was more needle than quality in the first half and Rogers, already booked, was extremely fortunate to avoid a second yellow card from the referee, Paul Tierney, when leaping into a challenge with James Garner. The Chelsea forward caught the ball and the man. The tackle could be considered just as reckless as the one that brought an earlier booking for Harrison Armstrong.

Barry wasted Everton’s best chance when heading a Jack Grealish cross straight at Martínez from close range. Another big miss from Barry was one of several recurring themes that undermined Everton’s afternoon.

View image in fullscreen Pedro Neto shows his delight after giving Chelsea the lead. Photograph: Molly Darlington/Getty Images

Chelsea began to contain the hosts and turn the tide as the interval approached. They were inches away from taking the lead in spectacular fashion. Moisés Caicedo pulled away to the back post for a Jordan Henderson corner that arrived exactly where the training ground routine required. His thunderous volley flew past Pickford but smacked the crossbar, leaving it shaking for several seconds.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Neto forced a decent save from the Everton keeper from distance in first-half stoppage time and beat him from much closer range 44 seconds after the restart. As in the draw at Hull last weekend, Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Pickford were found wanting defensively. Rogers was somewhat inevitably involved when releasing Jorrel Hato, Alonso’s one enforced change from the 5-1 defeat of Bournemouth, away from Maitland-Niles down the Chelsea left. Hato’s cross took a fortunate touch off James Tarkowski en route to Neto, whose shot beat Pickford’s weak attempt to save low to his left.

Goalkeeping worries took on a far more serious complexion when Branthwaite collided with Martínez as they challenged for a Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall free-kick. The Chelsea keeper required lengthy treatment before being carried away with his neck in a brace and to the uncomfortable sound of Evertonian boos. Thankfully he gave a thumbs up to Branthwaite when the concerned Everton defender waited to wish him well.

Martínez’s replacement, Mike Penders on his Premier League debut, was not seriously tested as the Everton threat petered out and Chelsea maintained control of the second half. Victory was sealed in the final minute of normal time when Henderson’s free-kick struck the head of Barry, rebounded off the Everton substitute Tyrique George and Vitalii Mykolenko, before dropping to Neto. The Chelsea winger rolled a confident finish past Pickford’s despairing dive into the bottom corner.

Sports.title: Championship roundup: West Ham go second; Norwich beaten again
Sports.content:
Nuno Espírito Santo was delighted West Ham finished a “demanding week” by toppling Championship leaders Swansea.

Divine Mukasa’s first-half strike in front of a record Swansea.com Stadium crowd of 20,973 gave the Hammers a 1-0 win and took them into second place and within a point of the league leaders. It was their second success in four days after a 6-0 romp at Lincoln, and ended a week that began with a 1-1 home draw against QPR following Jarrod Bowen’s last-gasp penalty miss.

“We wanted not only to keep the momentum, but to build on it,” said Nuno. “It was a very demanding week in terms of the opponents we had to face, but it finished really well due to the hard work of the boys. The commitment, the unity and the way they played was really good against a very good Swansea side. It was a very intense.”

Kim Hellberg defended his decision to rest Will Lankshear against Cardiff after the division’s top scorer came off the bench to rescue a point for Middlesbrough. Lankshear, who took his tally to 10 for the season in all competitions midweek, was rested him for the visit of the Bluebirds. That selection backfired as Cardiff stunned Boro with two first-half goals from Jack Moylan and Ollie Tanner. Lankshear was then introduced at half-time and inspired a fightback, levelling for Boro with his 11th goal of the campaign after Tommy Conway had halved the deficit.

View image in fullscreen Will Lankshear’s goal saved a point for Middlesbrough. Photograph: Richard Sellers/PA

“You need to manage your players in this league and look into numbers,” said Hellberg. “We have a lot of players that have no pre-season. Will is one of those who came late and has been doing a lot of good things. He’s been absolutely brilliant and sometimes you need to also protect him.”

Liam Millar scored twice as Birmingham beat QPR 3-0 at St Andrew’s. Millar swung the game Birmingham’s way in the 27th minute and then doubled their advantage just after the break. On both occasions he was assisted by Tomoki Iwata while Demarai Gray added the gloss in the first minute of stoppage time by hammering a pull-back by fellow substitute Luis Vázquez into the top corner.

Quick Guide League One roundup: Bradford go top; Plymouth lose Show Bradford moved top of League One with their first home win under Michael Duff, as Plymouth slipped up against Huddersfield. The Bantams, who appointed Duff as manager earlier this month following the departure of Graham Alexander, claimed a 2-0 home win over Stevenage thanks to goals inside the last 11 minutes from Antoni Sarcevic and substitute Will Swan. That proved enough to put them a point clear at the top, with previous front-runners Plymouth going down 2-0 at home to Huddersfield and dropping to fourth in the process. The Terriers climbed above their opponents into third after strikes from Derensili Sanches Fernandez and Bojan Radulovic. Stockport climbed to second, edging out Bromley 1-0 with Kyle Wootton on target, while Robbie Savage’s first home league game in charge of Peterborough ended in a 2-2 draw with Burton. It looked as if Gbemi Arubi’s 89th-minute wonderstrike had earned Albion their first win in three, but Matt Garbett responded with a 96th minute leveller to snatch his side a point. Savage started his time at London Road with a 3-1 win at Leicester last Saturday. Aaron Collins scored the winner as MK Dons beat Luton 2-1 to claim a first league victory of the season. Alex Gilbey fired the Dons ahead with a fine strike before Jordan Clark equalised for the visitors. But Collins’s penalty won the match to condemn Luton to a third defeat in their past four games. Under-pressure Leicester manager Russell Martin celebrated a badly needed win, seeing off visiting Doncaster 2-1 – with Warren O’Hara’s 84th-minute own-goal causing some late tension. Cambridge kept pace with the promotion hopefuls after Shayne Lavery grabbed the winner in added time to leave Barnsley with a 2-1 win, while Sheffield Wednesday eased to a 5-0 win over AFC Wimbledon – Davis Keillor-Dunn with a double. Bottom club Wigan registered a first league win since 2 September, Scott Hogan with the only goal against Reading. Notts County lost 2-0 at Wycombe and Leyton Orient beat Blackpool 2-0. Luke Graham scored his first goal for Stoke as they won 1-0 at Pride Park to pile more pressure on struggling Derby. The Scotland defender headed in a free-kick early in the second half and that was enough to settle a scrappy contest. Derby, who are missing a number of key players, battled away and nearly snatched a point when David Ozoh’s shot was superbly saved by goalkeeper Viktor Johansson.

West Brom completed a stunning comeback after conceding two early goals as they beat Blackburn 3-2. Andri Gudjohnsen had Rovers two up before the break, before Barney Stewart pulled a goal back for Albion. Isaac Price’s penalty levelled it up before the substitute Felix Horn Myhre netted a dramatic winner for the home side a minute from time.

James Bree, Lewis Dobbin and Léo Scienza all squandered chances as Southampton dropped points at home for the first time this season with a 0-0 draw against Bolton. The trio all wasted tap-ins, while Saints were also left bereft by a penalty not being given for a Rúben Rodrigues handball.

View image in fullscreen Luca Kjerrumgaard enjoys his crucial opener for Watford against Charlton. Photograph: Ben Peters/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock

Watford lifted the pressure on Alessio Dionisi and quelled their supporters’ rebellion against the owner, Gino Pozzo, with a deserved 2-0 win against a sluggish Charlton. After shipping nine goals in defeats by Burnley and Cardiff, Watford had slumped into the bottom three and the fans had turned their anger on Pozzo. But goals from Luca Kjerrumgaard and the substitute Jordan Zemura extended Charlton’s worrying run to eight games without a win as they were booed off at Vicarage Road.

Dionisi said later his team was “not yet strong enough for the Championship but it’s possible to improve. I’ve been a coach for 14 years and I know when my team stays near my idea. This result is important and tonight I will drink a glass of red wine.”

Portsmouth piled on the misery for struggling Norwich as they made it back-to-back Championships victories with a 1-0 win at Carrow Road. Pompey followed up their midweek victory against Sheffield United with a hard-fought success in East Anglia, with a 51st-minute penalty from striker Marezi settling the issue.

It was a sixth successive league defeat for the hosts and there were calls for the sporting director Ben Knapper to go from frustrated supporters at the final whistle.

Norwich’s head coach, Philippe Clement, had no complaints with his side’s effort – but felt they sometimes failed to see the bigger picture on the pitch.

“I am very disappointed, very frustrated,” he said. “I saw a lot of passion out there, a lot of effort, but not enough overview. It’s about getting the balance right between their hearts and their brains. I understand the frustration of our fans and all I can say is that I will work even harder than I did last season to turn it around.”

View image in fullscreen Portsmouth’s Marezi celebrates on another bleak day for Norwich. Photograph: Stephen Pond/Getty Images

Jake Cooper’s scrambled equaliser rescued a point for Millwall as they came from two goals down to draw 2-2 with Lincoln. The visitors looked on course to put Wednesday’s 6-0 home thrashing against West Ham behind them in style when goals from Andrei Coubiș and Rob Street put them in a strong position after 33 minutes at the Den. But Millwall were able to prevent back-to-back home defeats with a much-improved second-half performance, and the visitors were hanging on for a share of the spoils after having Deji Elerewe sent off soon after Cooper’s leveller. Kyrell Lisbie had scored Millwall’s first.

Quick Guide League Two roundup: Salford make it five in a row Show League Two pacesetters Salford made it five wins in a row in the fourth tier as Macaulay Langstaff scored twice in a 2-1 success over bottom side Crawley. Barnet and Crewe remain close by just a point further back. Barnet came from behind to beat Tranmere 2-1, Kabongo Tshimanga scoring both, and Crewe defeated Rochdale 3-2. York were held to a 1-1 draw at Newport after going down to 10 men but Shrewsbury held on 1-0 against Bristol Rovers despite two red cards in the last 10 minutes. Ian Holloway’s Swindon are now eight games without a win in all competitions after a 1-1 draw with Walsall, Oldham eased to a 4-1 result against Cheltenham and Port Vale edged Chesterfield 1-0. Ten-man Grimsby went down 2-0 to Northampton, Accrington took a 3-1 win over Gillingham, strugglers Rotherham lost 2-0 at Fleetwood and there was a goalless draw between Colchester and Exeter. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Oliver Arblaster’s early strike and a strong defensive display saw Sheffield United take all three points from a 1-0 victory over Bristol City at Ashton Gate. The visitors took a fifth-minute lead when a headed clearance fell to Arblaster, who connected with a sweet right-footed volley from just outside the box which gave the City goalkeeper Sam Tickle no chance. It proved enough to settle a contest high on endeavour but low on entertainment from which the Blades emerged worthy winners.

Wrexham eased the pressure on Phil Parkinson with a 4-1 win over rock-bottom Preston. Joe Worrall scored his first goal in more than two years and, after Alfie Devine briefly brought Preston level, the former Lilywhites midfielder Ben Whiteman struck next to score his first goal in Wrexham colours. Sam Smith gave the hosts breathing space just before the hour and Kieffer Moore killed it off moments later.

In a week that had seen former Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard linked with the manager’s job, Wrexham’s third league win of the season was a vital one as they moved up to 14th. But Preston remain stuck on four points from 11 games, with Graham Alexander having lost his first three games in charge.

Sports.title: Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley 2: Dynamite STOPS opponent in second round to retain world heavyweight title
Sports.content:
Breedlove: Ben Davison is hopeless. All Brit fighters should get over to America and be school by the trainers there.

Sports.title: Aston Villa had better players and a better plan than lumbering Newcastle - this was a harsh indication of the Magpies' current situation, writes CRAIG HOPE
Sports.content:
On the day Newcastle United revealed a slower version of their Blaydon Races anthem, the team on the pitch responded with a performance every bit as lumbering. When the match ball burst in stoppage-time, it was a signpost for the deflating mood that would soon descend on St James’ Park. At least, that was, after the home masses had let their feelings be known with a chorus of boos. It was just as well that this game also marked the unveiling of the club’s new pour-your-own beer pumps, for the locals needed something to numb the pain of a second defeat in a week. On this evidence, there will be plenty more. The sight of head coach Matthias Jaissle breaking the glass on the emergency option and throwing Dan Burn up front in the closing stages told of Newcastle’s desperation, as well as the absence of a workable Plan A. Come full-time, there had been just one shot on target — and that was from a defender. The club have spent £175million trying to replace Alexander Isak, and Burn is where they have ended up. Unai Emery’s Villa, by contrast, had a plan. They also had better players, including match-winner Johan Manzambi. Remarkably, the visitors are still below Newcastle in the table, not that they will be for too much longer. Villa are unbeaten in five in all competitions and this was Emery’s 100th win in the Premier League. ‘I hope there are 100 more,’ said the Spaniard. ‘This was very tough and for us it was very important after our poor start [to the season] that we needed to try to come back feeling confident, feeling comfortable in how we are building our structure.’ Aston Villa had better players than Newcastle, including match-winner Johan Manzambi, as they beat the Magpies 1-0 The midfielder, who nearly joined Newcastle in the summer, was the game’s star man and scorer of its only goal Matthias Jaissle's side are heading towards the bottom three after a second defeat in a week Much of that structure centres on the athleticism and ingenuity of Manzambi. Newcastle missing out on the signing of the Switzerland World Cup star was a sliding-doors moment in their summer, and it was among the reasons why Eddie Howe headed for the one marked ‘exit’. Had Manzambi and Victor Munoz — the Spaniard who defected to Liverpool — signed, Howe would likely have still been in charge. Sliding doors and, now, a team sliding towards the bottom three. That is the reality of their current plight. ‘Johan has skills and intelligence,’ said Emery. ‘His physicality is also very important to help us defensively. He decided he wanted to be with us [and not Newcastle]. We have Champions League. He has had a very good impact with his qualities.’ It is easy to see why Manzambi was so desired by Newcastle, who thought he was ready to join. The midfielder, 21, was the game’s star man and scorer of its only goal. Not that he had to be so great to convert a free header from six yards — for that he had the pinpoint cross of Joao Gomes to thank and, more so, the failure of defenders Sven Botman and Lewis Miley to react to his presence in the goalmouth. The moments that followed exposed the fragility of Newcastle’s confidence. Manzambi netted in the 36th minute and the hosts were fortunate not to enter the break at 2-0 down or worse. They lost shape, energy and ideas. It was like watching a boxer lose his legs after the first punch. Emiliano Buendia hit the post after a back-to-front offensive that was devastatingly simple in its execution — pass, pass, chance. It infuriated Jaissle, who yelled at Joe Willock for not stopping the move at source on the edge of Villa’s own area. The midfielder protested his innocence, in a manner to suggest he believed the job of closing Gomes belonged to someone else. That is never a good sign and was reminiscent of his team-mates’ abdication of responsibility for the goal moments earlier. MATCH FACTS Newcastle (4-2-3-1): Hornicek; Miley, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Joelinton (Burn 90), Gonzalez; Fernandez-Pardo (Toure 56), Willock (Osula 56), Barnes; Wissa Subs not used: Pope, Schar, Dedic, A Murphy, Steur, Bamba Booked: Thiaw, Botman, Gonzalez, Joelinton, Wissa, Osula Manager: Matthias Jaissle Aston Villa (4-2-3-1): Suzuki; Cash, Lindelof, Mings, Wan-Bissaka (Torres 77); Kamara, Gomes (Barkley 72); Alysson (McGinn 46), Manzambi (Mbiaye 72), Buendia (Goretzka 72); Jackson Subs not used: Bizot, Harwood-Bellis, Bogarde, Madjo Booked: Alysson, Gomes Goal: Manzambi 36 Manager: Unai Emery Jaissle had demanded his team come out swinging in response to Monday’s 4-1 defeat at Coventry, and they did, albeit with a little too much fight. The ferocity of Botman’s tackle on Nicolas Jackson needed 60 seconds of attention from Stockley Park, who eventually deemed the on-field yellow sufficient. It was a borderline red. Jackson later said: ‘I know the referee said yellow card but it was so high and hopefully maybe next time a red card. I nearly broke my leg. The most important thing is that we won, so I’m OK.’ Joelinton was also booked during the same passage for a typically robust challenge on Manzambi, requiring Villa’s medical team to divide their attention. Still, here was proof of a team ready to scrap for each other, and that resolve did at least extend until the very end, when they threatened to nick what would have been a barely-deserved equaliser amid the chaos of Burn. What was missing throughout, however, was quality and control. Marquee signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo remains without a goal and was hooked on 57 minutes after another subdued outing. The others in attack repeatedly ran down blind alleys. These two clubs have long been kindred spirits in their attempts to storm the Premier League’s elite. But whenever they have lowered the drawbridge, the following season has invariably seen them thrown back in the moat. Newcastle, you suspect, are set to sink even deeper this season.

Sports.title: Revealed: Marcus Rashford has been undergoing regular treatment all season in bid to beat injury that has affected performances for Man United
Sports.content:
Revealed: Marcus Rashford has been undergoing regular treatment all season in bid to beat injury that has affected performances for Man United

Marcus Rashford is having running repairs to be available for Manchester United this season as the England star continues to struggle with the hip injury that has dogged him since the World Cup.

Rashford has started six of United's nine games this season having returned to Old Trafford in the summer following loan spells at Barcelona and Aston Villa.

The 28-year-old has yet to score or make an assist, and failed to convert a volley in front of goal during Tuesday's Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid.

However, sources say that Rashford has been undergoing regular treatment all season to be available for head coach Michael Carrick, and it is inevitable that the problem has impacted his performances.

It remains to be seen if Rashford – who withdrew from England's recent Nations League games – starts against Leeds at Elland Road on Sunday with Matheus Cunha able to revert to the left flank after Amad Diallo's return from injury on the right freed up Bryan Mbeumo to play through the middle.

'Marcus has done a lot of good things,' said Carrick. 'He obviously had a slight injury where he pulled out with England, and he's had to manage that a little bit.

Marcus Rashford has started six of Man United's nine games so far this season despite a hip injury

'He's not quite getting that little bit of a break, putting himself in good positions and having some opportunities. He had one the other night maybe that he felt he probably could have done better with, but he's in there to make a difference.

'He keeps doing the right things, and you get the rewards in the end. So as long as he keeps doing that, he'll be okay.'

Bruno Fernandes has also been carrying an injury that forced him to sit out one of Portugal's games during the international break and appears to have affected his recent performances for United, although Carrick said that was not the reason his captain came off in the 80th minute in Madrid.

'He's been carrying some sort of issue, but he's pretty much over that now, to be honest, and he'll be back to his best,' added the United boss.

'A lot of players do carry them and it goes under the radar. People just think everyone's 100 per cent fully fit and it's probably not very often the case.

'We've got to share the load in all sorts of different ways: that's working, quality-wise, performing, being available.

'It's not an individual thing. When it's all good, it's not always just Bruno. Certainly if it's not so good, it's not all Bruno. He's a fantastic footballer, and he has a big impact on our group.

'Just because he may not be hitting the headlines or the highlights like he did last year doesn't mean that he can't, and that he won't, and I'm sure he'll do that pretty quickly.'

Sports.title: Michael Carrick responds to Nicky Butt's 'management's not for me' claim before landing the Man United job - as defiant boss insists he does not fear the sack ahead of crunch Leeds clash
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick has laughed off former Manchester United midfielder Nicky Butt's claim this week that the Old Trafford boss had told him he was no longer interested in football management before landing the job. Butt told The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast sponsored by Midnite this week, that Carrick had revealed in a private conversation before replacing Ruben Amorim: 'no it's not for me, it's too much, my head's all over the show, I'd only do it for the big job. The big job is Man United.' Carrick returned to Old Trafford in January as Ruben Amorim's replacement seven months after he was sacked from his first managerial job at Middlesbrough, and led United to a third-placed finish in the Premier League. Carrick insists though, ahead of this weekend's trip to Leeds: 'I definitely wouldn't be here if that was the case, would I?' At this stage, it's the best job and the best role I could possibly have. 'I feel a real privilege of being in this position and a real responsibility, but equally a drive of wanting to make a difference and having success here. 'I'm loving it. I love the situation when actually you get some sort of struggle and you've got to find a way out of it. I actually enjoy that because that's part of what drives you to have success. Michael Carrick was given the permanent role as Manchester United manager in the summer but has experienced a challenging start to the new season Nicky Butt took to his podcast to suggest that Michael Carrick had no desire to go into management before landing the United job 'If you're not ready for that and you can't do anything that's difficult, then you're never going to be great. So we've got to work our way through it, and I'm enjoying it as we go.' Carrick will take United to Elland Road – the scene of Amorim's last stand as head coach in January – adamant that he does not fear for his job. United face old foes Leeds with Carrick under increasing pressure after a run of four defeats and two wins in nine games this season. His predecessor Amorim was sacked over a post-match meltdown at Elland Road in which he took aim at director of football Jason Wilcox but Carrick isn't worried about his future. He said: 'I don't think about: 'How am I going to get through this? How am I going to survive this? What do I need to do to look after myself?'. 'It's not important. I really don't take it about me. It's about this football club and winning football matches. 'I don't think (Leeds) is the last game I need right now. I'm really looking forward to the game. I generally feel the drive for myself to want to push this club forward more than anything. 'There's always negativity if you want to look for it or want to feel it. But I don't go looking for it, and I don't want to feel it. 'I understand the reality. I accept where we are, but I don't feel that. I'm totally focused on what's best for this football club and what it's going to take to win games: get the boys playing how we know we're capable of, and we still don't think we're that far away. 'We can turn a few things in our favour, and we can move forward pretty quickly.'
