Sports.title: Daniel Dubois Crushes Fabio Wardley In Second Round
Sports.content:
Daniel Dubois (24-3, 23 KOs) overwhelmed Fabio Wardley (20-2-1) in two rounds to retain his WBO heavyweight title, dropping the challenger almost immediately and never allowing him to recover.

Referee Steve Gray halted the fight at 2:21 of round two after Wardley’s corner threw in the towel on Saturday at London’s O2 Arena.

Their first fight required Dubois to recover from two knockdowns before stopping Wardley in the eleventh. This time, the champion inflicted the early damage, landing a jab followed by a right hand that put Wardley down inside the opening 15 seconds.

Wardley answered the count, but his legs looked unsteady. Dubois stayed composed rather than smothering his punches, giving himself room to land more heavy right hands and combinations. Wardley tried to answer, yet he could not make the champion back off.

The punishment continued through the opening round, with Wardley pinned against the ropes at times. Ben Davison’s corner had the towel ready but allowed him to continue. Reaching the bell gave Wardley a break, although it did little to change the direction of the fight.

Wardley came out for the second trying to swing his way back into the contest. That approach left him exposed against a champion who was finding the target without needing to force his attacks.

After a quieter spell and a clinch, Dubois connected with another sharp one-two, landing the right hand cleanly on Wardley’s chin. Wardley missed with a big shot, and Dubois followed with a flurry. The towel came in before the challenger could take any more punishment.

The difference from their first meeting was how quickly Dubois established control. Wardley never had the early success that made their previous fight competitive, and the opening knockdown left him struggling simply to survive.

Dubois needed no comeback this time. He hurt Wardley early, kept his punching organized and finished the rematch with a decisive title defense.

Sports.title: Daniel Dubois vs. Fabio Wardley Rematch Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Daniel Dubois (24-3, 23 KOs) stopped Fabio Wardley (20-2-1) in the second round to retain his WBO heavyweight title. Dubois dropped Wardley within the opening 15 seconds with a jab followed by a right hand.

Wardley beat the count but struggled to regain his legs as Dubois punished him with heavy punches throughout the first round. Dubois landed another sharp right hand in the second and followed with a flurry that prompted Ben Davison’s corner to throw in the towel. The champion settled the rematch far quicker than their first fight, which ended with Dubois stopping Wardley in the eleventh round.

Louie O’Doherty (12-0-1, 3 KOs) retained his British and Commonwealth lightweight titles with a majority draw against Michael Gomez Jr. (23-2-1, 8 KOs), surviving a difficult twelve-round fight in which the challenger’s cleaner work made a strong case for victory.

Two judges scored the contest 114-114, while the third favored Gomez 115-114 on Saturday at London’s O2 Arena. None of the three scored the fight for O’Doherty, but the two level cards were enough to keep both belts with the unbeaten champion.

Gomez applied pressure early and found success with right hands, uppercuts, and punches to the body. His attacks gave O’Doherty more to deal with than simply matching his opponent’s output. The challenger was landing scoring shots while making the champion work to create room.

O’Doherty used his jab, movement, and volume to keep rounds competitive. His stronger moments came later, helping him recover ground after Gomez’s effective early work. The question was whether that late improvement deserved enough rounds to offset what the challenger had already done.

That is where the draw becomes difficult to accept for those who favored Gomez. A busy round from O’Doherty did not automatically outweigh the more accurate punches coming back. His jab and movement deserved credit when they produced clean scoring, but activity alone should not have been enough.

Equally, boxing is scored round by round. Gomez could have won his best rounds clearly and still finished level if O’Doherty edged enough of the closer ones. Without the individual round cards, it is impossible to identify exactly where the judges differed.

The result nevertheless left Gomez with a reasonable complaint. He challenged an unbeaten champion, landed effectively under pressure and received the only winning scorecard, yet left without either title.

O’Doherty kept his belts, but a rematch would give both fighters the chance to settle a result that left neither with a victory.

Unbeaten heavyweight Adam Olaniyan (5-0, 5 KOs) stopped Dan Garber at 1:15 of the second round of their scheduled four-round bout. Olaniyan put the veteran down twice in the second to secure another early finish.

The first knockdown prompted a towel to be thrown into the ring, but referee Amy Pu allowed the contest to continue. Pu kicked the towel out of the way as Garber got back up. That gave Olaniyan another opportunity to attack an opponent whose corner had already tried to end the fight.

Garber went down for a second time in the round. Pu then called a halt, ending the contest before its halfway point. The unusual handling of the towel drew attention in a bout that otherwise followed the expected pattern of a young prospect overpowering a veteran opponent. Olaniyan has now finished all five of his professional fights inside the distance.

Two-time Olympic gold medalist Bakhodir Jalolov (18-0) cruised to a one-sided ten-round unanimous decision over Solomon Dacres (10-2) in a heavyweight contest short on action. The scores were 99-91, 99-90 and 99-90.

The 6’7” Jalolov was content to box from the outside, using his height and reach to keep Dacres at a distance. There was little urgency from the unbeaten southpaw to press for a stoppage, even with Dacres struggling to get close enough to land.

The fifth round provided the fight’s biggest moment. Dacres recklessly lunged forward and ran into a straight left that sent him to the canvas. His attempt to force the action left him exposed to precisely the punch he needed to avoid.

After that knockdown, Dacres appeared less willing to take chances. That made an already quiet fight even easier for Jalolov, who could continue picking his shots without having to deal with sustained pressure.

Dacres had spoken confidently beforehand about stopping Jalolov, but he offered little to support that prediction once the fight began. He needed to get inside and make the taller man work, yet rarely managed to turn the contest into anything beyond an outside boxing match.

Jalolov won comfortably, although the performance did little to answer questions about how aggressively he intends to pursue his professional career. His ability was clear; the desire to force a finish was harder to find.

Nelson Birchall (13-0, 10 KOs) stopped Levi Giles (17-4-1) in the seventh round of their scheduled ten-round super featherweight bout. Birchall used his speed and accuracy to control the action, gradually wearing Giles down.

Giles kept working but struggled to match the unbeaten prospect’s cleaner punching. Birchall scored the first knockdown in the fifth round. He put Giles down again in the sixth as his power began deciding the fight. A third knockdown in the seventh brought the stoppage. It was the first time Giles had been stopped in his professional career.

Super flyweight Tony Curtis (15-1, 4 KOs) stopped Kerim Agius (4-2, 2 KOs) in the fourth round to win the vacant Commonwealth International title.

Curtis scored knockdowns in rounds two and four before referee Sean McAvoy halted the scheduled eight-round bout at 2:57 of the fourth.

Featherweight Leighton Birchall (6-0, 3 KOs) defeated Alejandro Morales Chazaro (9-10-2, 5 KOs) by a six-round points decision. Birchall took every round on the 60-54 scorecard to remain unbeaten.

Super bantamweight Manny Safari (1-0, 1 KO) won his professional debut with a fifth-round TKO over Jake Pollard (1-122, 1 KO). The prospect finished inside the distance against the experienced journeyman.

Lightweight Fawas Aborode (3-0, 3 KOs) defeated Rashid Omar (8-10, 1 KO) by fourth-round TKO. Aborode controlled the action before forcing the stoppage, turning the expected one-sided contest into another early finish.

Aaron Noriega (3-0) defeated Leonardo Baez by fourth-round TKO, securing his third professional victory in a super featherweight bout. The stoppage brought an early finish to the bout, with Noriega celebrating afterward in a Mexican-flag cap.

Middleweight Issiah Hamilton-Allen (4-0) defeated Jensen Irving (6-41-2, 1 KO) by decision over four rounds. Hamilton-Allen won every round on the 40-36 scorecard.

Sports.title: Bakhodir Jalolov Drops Solomon Dacres In Wide Win
Sports.content:
Bakhodir Jalolov (18-0) had little trouble beating Solomon Dacres (10-2), but his ten-round unanimous decision offered more evidence of his boxing ability than his willingness to chase a finish.

The two-time Olympic gold medalist scored a fifth-round knockdown and won by scores of 99-91, 99-90 and 99-90 on Saturday at London’s O2 Arena.

The 6’7” southpaw controlled the distance with his height and reach, leaving Dacres struggling to get close enough to mount an attack. Jalolov could win from the outside without putting himself in danger, and he appeared comfortable keeping the fight there.

Dacres needed to disrupt that rhythm. Allowing the taller fighter to pick his shots at long range gave him little chance of winning rounds, yet getting inside required risks he struggled to judge.

That problem caught up with Dacres in the fifth. He lunged forward and was nailed by a straight left, sending him to the canvas. Jalolov punished the reckless entry with a clean counter rather than having to hunt for an opening himself.

The knockdown seemed to discourage Dacres from making further attempts to force the action. He continued through the remaining rounds, but his reluctance to commit made Jalolov’s job easier. There was little sustained pressure to make the Uzbek uncomfortable or force him to change his approach.

Jalolov deserves credit for making the contest look so straightforward. Dacres had talked about stopping him beforehand, only to find himself unable to solve the distance or avoid the left hand when he rushed forward.

Still, this was a quiet performance from a heavyweight with Jalolov’s power and amateur pedigree. Once Dacres became more cautious, Jalolov largely accepted the decision that was already within reach.

He left with a clear victory, but without the emphatic finish that might have made this feel like a bigger step forward.

Sports.title: Brandon Figueroa Illness Forces Tomoki Kameda Cancellation
Sports.content:
Brandon Figueroa’s disastrous weekend has now cost Tomoki Kameda his chance to fight for the vacant WBA featherweight title. Their bout on tonight’s Sebastian Fundora–Ermal Hadribeaj card in Las Vegas has been canceled, according to Dan Rafael.

Figueroa reportedly became ill Friday night following the weight cut that had already cost him his belt. He came in at 127.4 pounds, missing the featherweight limit by 1.4 pounds and being stripped before entering the ring.

“Per source, tonight’s Figueroa vs. Kameda fight has been canceled after Figueroa became ill Friday night after his weight cut that caused him to miss weight and be stripped of the WBA featherweight title,” said Rafael on X.

For Kameda, the situation has gone from frustrating to considerably worse. After making weight, he remained eligible to win the vacant championship by beating Figueroa. Now he leaves without the opportunity to settle anything in the ring.

The Japanese former champion had already expressed his frustration Friday, pointing out that he had completed his own preparations and made the required weight. The cancellation means that work will produce no fight tonight. Whether he receives compensation or another title opportunity remains unconfirmed.

Figueroa’s preparations had also included a hamstring injury, which he disclosed to Chris Mannix. There is no confirmed diagnosis in Rafael’s report explaining the illness, and the injury should not automatically be treated as its cause.

Losing Figueroa removes one of the strongest action attractions from the Fundora–Hadribeaj undercard. His pressure and willingness to fight at close range had made the Kameda bout a significant part of the evening’s appeal.

The consequences extend beyond one canceled contest. Figueroa has lost the championship he won from Nick Ball in February, while Kameda’s route to the vacant belt is unresolved. The WBA must now determine what happens next.

A weekend intended to begin Figueroa’s title defense campaign has instead ended with him without a belt, without a fight, and with questions over when he can return.

Sports.title: Denis Boytsov Dies at 40: Father Reveals Cause of Former Heavyweight Contender’s Death
Sports.content:
Former Russian heavyweight contender Denis Boytsov has died at the age of 40 in his hometown of Oryol, Russia. His father, Nikolai Boytsov, told Russian news agency TASS that his son died from a detached blood clot and that his death was sudden.

According to his father, Boytsov was at home with his wife when he suddenly became seriously ill. Emergency medical personnel were unable to save him.

Born in Oryol in 1986, Boytsov was once considered a promising heavyweight contender. He captured the WBC youth heavyweight title in 2006 and later won WBA and WBO regional titles.

He finished his professional boxing career with a record of 36 wins and one defeat, including 27 knockouts.

Boytsov’s death at just 40 brings a sad end to the life of a fighter whose promising career was cut short by devastating injuries.

David Price’s Sad Reminder of Denis Boytsov’s Lost Power: “He Only Hit the Top of My Head”

David Price didn’t post it for likes. He didn’t shove it into a promo reel. He just quietly reminded the boxing world of something brutal: the scariest puncher he ever stood in front of is now barely remembered, and barely alive.

“I sparred a Russian called Denis Boytsov in Germany once,” Price told Daily Star Sport. “He only hit the top of my head, but he was a powerful puncher.”

That’s all it took. Not a looping right. Not a clean uppercut. Just a glancing shot to the crown and Price, who’s taken punches from the division’s heaviest hitters, still can’t forget it. That says everything.

Let’s not sugar-coat it. Price’s career turned into a highlight reel for other people’s rise. He got flattened by names plastered across belts, posters, and DAZN deals. But the man who left the deepest mark wasn’t any of them.

It was Boytsov.

And you barely hear his name anymore.

He was 36-1. He had the momentum. He had the hands. He was lined up for a world title shot. Then he vanished. In May 2015, he was found unconscious between two Berlin train stations. Skull fractured. Brain swollen. Medically induced coma. Seven weeks.

They said it was an “accident.”

Berlin police had the gall to call it an “accident.” Meanwhile, Boytsov’s own website said it was linked to years of threats. His wife called it mob revenge.

Price didn’t mince words: “He got absolutely battered by a gang of Russian fellas and left for dead. He couldn’t fight again.”

And he never did.

Boytsov dropped over 30 kilos in hospital. Couldn’t speak. Couldn’t walk. Initially treated in Berlin, he was later transferred to a rehabilitation clinic in Hamburg. In August 2021, Boytsov was moved back to his native Russia for continued care. . He’s still under 24-hour care, unable to speak, and continues to require assistance for daily activities.

All while the sport moved on, pretending he never existed.

The hype went to safer hands. The belts went to ticket sellers. The world never saw what Boytsov could’ve been. He was buried under a system that never wanted him near a title.

No comeback story. No redemption arc. No one crying into a mic about how he “overcame adversity.” He just disappeared.

And next time someone starts listing who punched the hardest…Tyson this, Wilder that, remember who David Price named.

It wasn’t the poster boys. It was the one who never got his shot.

And we’ll never know what he could’ve done.

What a sad, sorry waste.

Sports.title: Jacob Bank Blueprint: Drowning Janibek In A War Of Attrition
Sports.content:
Jacob Bank’s best chance against Janibek Alimkhanuly may come from making the former middleweight champion fight harder and longer than he wants. Denzel Bentley succeeded at that against a younger Janibek. Bank needs to start sooner and take it further.

Their January 23 fight in Horsens, Denmark, will be contested for the vacant WBO super middleweight title. For Bank, the task is to turn a technical fight into a war of attrition without getting picked apart on the way inside.

Bentley came up short against Janibek in November 2022, yet sustained activity forced the champion to expend energy following a cautious start. Janibek looked vulnerable once Bentley grouped punches, taking away the room Janibek needed to set the pace. That bout provides Bank a clear blueprint. It highlights the danger of patience.

Bank cannot waste early rounds studying Janibek from outside, handing him distance and banking rounds while fresh. The younger fighter needs continuous volume, targeting the ribs and beltline whenever he safely steps inside. Forcing Janibek to pivot, defend, and reset takes a deeper toll than hunting for a single clean punch.

The goal must be to drain his gas tank before the second half begins. Bank showed strong finishing ability when halting William Scull in the twelfth round in January. Scull offered minimal return fire.

Janibek is moving up to 168 pounds, coming off inactivity, and will likely carry his pop early. If Bank charges in without a tight guard, feints, and head movement, he walks onto counters before Janibek’s tank even begins to drain. Bank has the size, the engine, and the home crowd in Denmark, but toughness alone won’t knock out guys with elite amateur pedigree.

If Bank commits to a high guard, cuts off the ring, digs to the ribs, and makes Janibek carry his weight in the clinch, the wear and tear will tell by round seven or eight. It comes down to whether Bank can absorb the initial fire to cash in on that size and stamina down the stretch.

Sports.title: Solomon Dacres Picks Himself to Stop Bakhodir Jalolov
Sports.content:
Solomon Dacres expects to stop Bakhodir Jalolov tonight, but his record offers little support for that prediction against the 6’7″ two-time Olympic gold medalist.

Jalolov has looked sluggish enough lately to give critics room for skepticism. The dominant puncher seen in the amateur ranks rarely appears in his prize ring outings, prompting a few observers to sniff an upset. Regardless, Jalolov looking flat does not suddenly transform Dacres into a top threat.

“Got to get him out of there, man,” Dacres told SecondsOut. “Mid to late rounds.”

That would be a considerable leap for a fighter whose most revealing professional result remains his first-round stoppage defeat to David Adeleye in December 2024.

Dacres describes that loss as a “blip,” but it came against the most notable opponent he had faced. Across five years as a professional, he hasn’t built a record of beating contenders that would make a Jalolov knockout seem likely.

His points win against Vladyslav Sirenko also requires context. Sirenko amassed numbers without testing himself against true threats, meaning that victory hardly proves Dacres can deal with Jalolov’s height, reach, and southpaw boxing skills.

“This fight here is beyond English title level, man,” Dacres said. “This is like world level.”

Jalolov deserves criticism for how slowly his professional career has moved and for performances that haven’t matched expectations. His Olympic medals don’t excuse that, and Dacres has an opportunity to make him work.

Expecting Dacres to win because Jalolov underwhelms ignores his own modest punch output. Managing just three stoppages across ten victories, he lacks the firepower to back up big talk.

For Dacres to land the kinds of sustained combinations required to stop someone Jalolov’s size, he has to pin him down. Jalolov does not fight like a traditional, stationary heavyweight slugger. Even when he looks uninspired, he uses lateral footwork, maintains long range with his southpaw lead hand, and angles off before opponents can set their feet.

Dacres lacks both the foot speed to cut off the ring effectively and the explosive one-punch power to make Jalolov cautious. If Dacres tries to force the issue, he’ll put himself at risk of getting caught. Pressing aggressively against a 6’7″ southpaw who excels at firing straight left hands down the pipe is asking for trouble.

Unless Jalolov completely checks out mentally and stands against the ropes to trade, Dacres will be eating long jabs and counters all night, with a Jalolov stoppage being the far more probable outcome.

Ghana News.title: Ghana must protect national interest in pursuit of BRICS membership – Hassan Ayariga
Ghana News.content:
The Founder and Leader of the All People’s Congress (APC), Hassan Ayariga, has cautioned Ghana against exchanging one form of economic dependency for another as the government pursues membership of the BRICS economic bloc.

In a press statement issued on Saturday, October 17, 2026, Ayariga said he was not opposed to Ghana establishing strategic relationships with BRICS countries but insisted that such partnerships must protect the country’s national interests, constitutional governance and democratic accountability.

He argued that any move to join the bloc must deliver tangible benefits for Ghanaian citizens and businesses rather than create new forms of economic dependence.

“For decades, African countries have struggled with economic dependency, foreign control of strategic resources, unequal trade relationships and limited industrial development. We must not repeat the mistakes of the past,” he said.

“If Ghana seeks to join BRICS to diversify its international relationships, that objective must translate into tangible benefits for Ghanaian citizens and businesses.”

Hassan Ayariga said Ghana’s gold, oil, minerals, agricultural resources and strategic infrastructure must be managed in ways that support national development.

He criticised the continued export of raw materials with limited local processing, arguing that Ghana must strengthen its industrial capacity and retain more value from its natural resources.

“We cannot continue exporting our raw materials cheaply, importing finished products at enormous costs and allowing foreign interests to dominate strategic sectors of our economy,” he stated.

He said Ghana’s approach to international partnerships should be guided by the same principles, regardless of whether potential partners come from Europe, America, Asia or the Middle East.

“Whether our partners come from Europe, America, Asia, the Middle East or elsewhere, the guiding principle must remain the same: Ghana first. Ghanaians first. National interest first,” he said.

“International cooperation must strengthen our sovereignty, not weaken it.”

The APC leader also called for clarity on the terms and implications of Ghana’s proposed BRICS membership.

He questioned the economic and diplomatic obligations the country might assume, the level of influence it could exercise within the grouping and the practical benefits for ordinary Ghanaians.

“What exactly does Ghana stand to gain? What obligations will Ghana assume? What are the potential economic, political and diplomatic consequences? Will Ghana become a full member or merely a partner country?” he asked.

He further questioned whether Ghana would have meaningful influence in decision-making or become a participant in a grouping dominated by larger economies.

Hassan Ayariga said the government must also explain how the proposed partnership would benefit farmers, traders, manufacturers, entrepreneurs and other businesses.

He maintained that such questions should be treated as matters of national interest rather than dismissed as political opposition.

The government announced its intention to pursue BRICS membership on October 6, 2026, with Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa saying Cabinet had approved a decision to formally apply to join the bloc.

The government has said the move is intended to diversify Ghana’s international partnerships and create opportunities for trade, investment and economic cooperation.

Ghana News.title: Multimedia Group wins Media Organisation of the Year award at the 2025 CIMG Awards
Ghana News.content:
The Multimedia Group Limited has been named Marketing-Oriented Media Organisation of the Year for 2025 at the 37th Annual National Marketing Performance Awards organised by the Chartered Institute of Marketing, Ghana (CIMG).

The award was presented at the Labadi Beach Hotel in Accra on Saturday, October 17, 2026, in recognition of the Group’s use of radio, television and digital platforms to drive public engagement and audience participation.

In its citation, CIMG praised the Group for turning audience attention into public conversation and participation, highlighting its JoyNews Impact Maker Awards and other audience-focused initiatives.

“The Multimedia Group has used its radio, television and digital platforms to turn audience attention into public conversation and participation,” the citation read.

It added that the Group’s initiatives demonstrated “the value of strong editorial brands supported by coordinated marketing”.

The citation also highlighted the Group’s reported audience shares for 2025, putting television at 28 per cent, Accra radio at 46.9 per cent and Kumasi radio at 43.2 per cent.

CIMG further noted the reach of the 2026 JoyNews Impact Maker Awards, which attracted about 2,000 attendees and 34 corporate participants.

The institute said the Group’s marketing approach extended beyond broadcasting messages to creating platforms where audiences could gather, contribute and share experiences.

“The marketing achievement extends beyond broadcasting a message. By giving your audience a reason to gather, contribute and share stories, the Group turns its media properties into platforms for participation,” the citation stated.

It described the Impact Maker event as an example of how editorial trust could support experiences that deliver value to communities and partners.

In its concluding remarks, CIMG commended the Group’s performance and its position in Ghana’s media industry.

“Your continuous exploit in this arena sets you apart as media house of choice,” the citation stated.

The institute subsequently adjudged Multimedia Group Limited the Marketing-Oriented Media Organisation of the Year for 2025.

The Multimedia Group operates radio, television and digital platforms in Ghana. Its brands include Joy 99.7 FM, JoyNews, Adom FM, Hitz FM, Asempa FM, Luv FM, Nhyira FM and MyJoyOnline.com.

The award recognises the Group’s marketing performance and its use of established media brands and audience-focused initiatives to strengthen public engagement.

Ghana News.title: Multimedia Group’s #NoToGalamsey campaign wins CIMG New Media Campaign Award
Ghana News.content:
The Multimedia Group’s anti-galamsey campaign, Galamsey Fight (#NoToGalamsey), has won the New Media Campaign Award at the 37th Annual National Marketing Performance Awards.

CIMG recognised the campaign for its ability to communicate its message effectively, appeal to its audience and make a positive impact on society. The institute also commended the ethical execution of its informative and educational content.

The Multimedia Group has used its radio, television and digital platforms to raise awareness of the environmental, social and economic consequences of illegal mining.

The campaign forms part of the Group’s broader advocacy efforts to protect Ghana’s natural resources and encourage public engagement on issues of national importance.

The CIMG award adds to the campaign’s recognition of the role public-interest media initiatives can play in informing audiences and sustaining attention on pressing environmental challenges.

The Multimedia Group is expected to continue using its platforms to advocate for the protection of the country’s natural resources.

Ghana News.title: Hassan Ayariga challenges Mahama over BRICS move, demands parliamentary consultation
Ghana News.content:
The Founder and Leader of the All People’s Congress (APC), Hassan Ayariga, has challenged President John Dramani Mahama over the government’s plan to pursue Ghana’s membership of BRICS, demanding parliamentary scrutiny and public consultation on the decision.

In a statement issued on Saturday, October 17, 2026, Dr Ayariga questioned whether Cabinet could determine Ghana’s long-term international economic and geopolitical commitments without broader public and parliamentary engagement.

“Who gave Cabinet the authority to decide for over 34 million Ghanaians without parliamentary and public consultation?” he asked.

He argued that Ghana’s sovereignty rests with its citizens and that decisions with far-reaching implications for the country should be subjected to transparency, accountability and public participation.

Hassan Ayariga cited Article 1(1) of the 1992 Constitution, which establishes that sovereignty resides in the people of Ghana.

He said the President and Cabinet must exercise their authority in accordance with the Constitution and remain accountable to the people.

“My question to President John Dramani Mahama is simple: Who has the authority to determine Ghana's long-term international economic and geopolitical commitments? Can the President do so without the approval of Parliament and the Ghanaian people?” he asked.

The APC leader maintained that democratic governance should extend beyond periodic elections to include consultation and participation in decisions affecting the country’s future.

He said major political, economic, legal and social policies should reflect the will of the people and be implemented through the appropriate arms of government.

Hassan Ayariga also invoked Article 75 of the Constitution, which provides for the President to execute treaties, agreements and conventions on behalf of Ghana, subject to ratification by Parliament.

He urged President Mahama to present the BRICS matter to Parliament for deliberation and a decision on the way forward.

“Mr President, you must therefore place this matter before Parliament for the deliberations and decision of Parliament and the people,” he said.

He further called on the government to explain the proposed membership’s contents, implications and expected benefits before proceeding.

“The contents, implications and benefits must be made clear to Ghanaians before membership,” he added.

The government announced on October 6, 2026, that Cabinet had approved a decision to formally apply for Ghana to join BRICS, according to Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa.

BRICS is a grouping of major emerging economies that has expanded beyond its original members and seeks to strengthen cooperation among participating countries in areas including trade, investment and development.

The government has presented the proposed engagement as an opportunity to broaden Ghana’s international partnerships and deepen economic cooperation with developing economies.

The Minority in Parliament has also called for an urgent briefing on the decision, seeking disclosure of its geopolitical implications and potential effects on Ghana’s national interests.

Hassan Ayariga’s latest intervention adds to calls for greater parliamentary scrutiny and public discussion as the government pursues its plan.

Ghana News.title: Belgium-based ICGC pastor enstooled Amanonehene of Abotakyi
Ghana News.content:
A 44-year-old Reverend Minister of the International Central Gospel Church (ICGC), Rev. Richard Tagoe, has been enstooled Amanonehene of Abotakyi in the Akuapem Traditional Area of the Eastern Region, with a pledge to mobilise diaspora support and attract investment for the town’s development.

The businessman, who lives in Belgium, assumes the traditional title Nana Ohene Tagoe I.

The Amanonehene title is intended to promote the welfare of indigenes living abroad and mobilise their support for development projects in the town.

Following the traditional rites, Nana Ohene Tagoe I was carried shoulder-high and paraded through the principal streets of Abotakyi amid cheers, drumming and dancing.

At a ceremony at the Abotakyi chief’s palace on October 12, Nana Ohene Tagoe swore an oath of allegiance to the town’s chief, Nana Kwame Sakyi Ababio II.

The chief and elders said the traditional council introduced the Amanonehene title to strengthen relationships with indigenes and organisations outside Ghana and mobilise resources for local development.

The Abotakyihene said Nana Ohene Tagoe was selected because of his previous support for the town and his willingness to help raise funds from the diaspora.

“We decided to introduce such a title in the traditional area to help us mobilise the needed funds from the diaspora,” the chief said.

He added that the new Amanonehene had been recommended by someone familiar with his generosity and contributions to the community.

The chief also urged him to remain truthful in his efforts to solicit financial support for development initiatives.

“I believe that as a reverend minister, you will be truthful in all your undertakings when soliciting for financial support from the diaspora for the development of the town,” he said.

In an interview, Nana Ohene Tagoe I pledged to use his new position to promote infrastructure development and attract investors to Abotakyi.

He said he intended to connect the town with business-minded people willing to invest in projects that could create employment and improve livelihoods.

“I accept to be Amanonehene to bring in investors, business-minded people who will develop the town. I will help get the youth employed and reduce the unemployment and teenage pregnancy rate in town,” he said.

His appointment is expected to strengthen the town’s engagement with its diaspora as traditional leaders seek support for development and economic opportunities for residents.

Ghana's U17 side, the Black Starlets, will face Ivory Coast in the semi-finals of the 2026 WAFU Zone B U17 Championship after the Ivorians secured second place in Group B following a 1-1 draw against Nigeria on Saturday.

However, Ivory Coast will pose a stern test for the Black Starlets, with both teams aware that victory will guarantee their participation in the 2027 U17 AFCON, while the losing side will miss out on qualification through the tournament.

Ghana News.title: GMA donates 300 life jackets to boat operators, fishers in Dambai
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Maritime Authority (GMA) has handed over 300 life jackets to boat operators and fishers in Dambai to promote safety compliance and reduce fatalities on the Oti River.

The donation, made at the Dambai Ferry Station, benefited three groups: the Boat Owners and Operators Association-Dambai, A1 Boats and the Inland Canoe Fishers Association, with each organisation receiving 100 life jackets.

The intervention formed part of the Authority's Life Jackets for Safety and Livelihood Initiative, which allows inland waterway operators to acquire life jackets at subsidised prices and pay in monthly instalments to ease the financial burden of obtaining essential safety equipment.

The Deputy Director of the Technical Services Division and Head of Inland Waterways at the GMA, Captain Kodjo Adjarko Osei, said the high cost of life jackets had been a major challenge for some operators and contributed to non-compliance with water safety regulations.

He said the Authority was addressing the challenge by improving access to affordable life jackets, stressing that their use was critical to preventing avoidable deaths during water transport accidents.

Captain Osei noted that the intervention also supported the enforcement of the Authority's "No Life Jacket, No Sailing" directive, introduced earlier this year during the launch of its Safety Guards Programme.

He said making life jackets readily accessible was essential to ensuring that operators complied with safety regulations before embarking on journeys on inland waterways.

The Krachi East Municipal Chief Executive, Mr Safo Nketiah, who spoke on behalf of the community, commended the Authority for its efforts to safeguard the lives of people who relied on waterways for their livelihoods.

He noted that nearly 40 per cent of residents in Dambai engaged in lake-related activities, making the provision and use of life jackets crucial to protecting lives and sustaining economic activities in the area.

Mr Nketiah urged the Authority to sustain such interventions to improve water safety awareness and encourage greater compliance among boat operators and fishers.

Beneficiaries lauded the GMA for the intervention, describing it as a significant step towards improving safety on the Oti River.

They pledged to use the life jackets for their intended purpose and comply with established safety requirements to protect lives and promote safer inland water transport.

The initiative underscores the GMA's commitment to enhancing safety standards on inland waterways by addressing barriers to accessing life-saving equipment and reinforcing compliance with maritime safety regulations.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Photos: No Kings rallies in US urge midterm voters to cast ballots early
World.content:
Rallies organised by the No Kings network opposed to United States President Donald Trump were held Saturday in cities and communities across the US, with an aim of getting people out to vote early in the midterm elections.

No Kings has more than 3,000 events planned across the US. The planned events, this time dubbed “No Kings: Vote Early”, were billed as nonpartisan, though they sought to build on nearly two years’ worth of No Kings marches and demonstrations by people upset with Trump’s presidency.

“It’s a day of nonpartisan voter participation: we are bringing our community together to make a plan to vote early and ensuring every eligible voter understands their options for how to vote and has the opportunity to make their voice heard,” organisers said in a statement.

By advocating for voting early, the “No Kings” organisers hope to cut off the potential for any malfeasance once election day rolls around.

A band entertained what appeared to be a few hundred people in caps and coats at the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, DC. Despite the chilly weather, many in the crowd danced to the tunes. “VOTE EARLY” and “HANDS OFF MY VOTE!” were among the many signs held aloft.

At an Atlanta rally, City Councilman Michael Julian Bond told the crowd to urge others to vote ahead of the November 3 general election.

“The Constitution gives you one power, right? That is the power to vote. Are you gonna use that power?” he said.

“You don’t see Superman giving up his power,” Bond continued. “You don’t see Black Panther giving up his power. You don’t see Wonder Woman giving up her magic lasso. So why would you give up your right, your power, your obligation to vote? Be a superhero, use your power. Go to the polls and vote.”



Trump has long been suspicious of mail voting and has claimed without evidence that voting fraud cost him the 2020 presidential election.

His administration sued California election officials Thursday, asking a judge to bar the state from counting mail-in ballots for the midterm elections from people whom the federal government has identified as “likely” noncitizens until their immigration status can be confirmed.

On Friday, the Department of Justice warned that local officials who process and tabulate ballots submitted by suspected noncitizen voters are putting themselves at risk of criminal investigation and potential prosecution.

Earlier that day, Democratic Senators Alex Padilla of California, Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island and Dick Durbin of Illinois wrote to Attorney General Todd Blanche, demanding that the Justice Department commit to not seizing ballots or other election materials before the midterm elections are certified.

World.title: Cost of living protests hit Belgium, Italy, Portugal and France
World.content:
Hundreds of thousands of Europeans took to the streets for separate demonstrations putting pressure on governments across the EU.

Hundreds of thousands of Europeans have taken to the streets in separate, uncoordinated demonstrations to protest against the rising cost of living in their countries.

Saturday’s protests were in Belgium, France, Italy and Portugal in a wave of unrest that has put pressure on national governments across the European Union.

France experienced one of its most turbulent days of protests in decades, with over 550,000 people joining demonstrations and police facing off with protesters across the country – but it was not the only country to see significant demonstrations.

In Belgium’s capital Brussels – which has already seen weeks of protests by students against university registration fees – police fired tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters, who they accused of launching missiles at them and setting fires.

In Liege, a smaller city east of Brussels, police also deployed water cannon to break up demonstrations. Police did not say how many people attended.

An estimated tens of thousands of protesters marched in Lisbon, the Portuguese capital, against the cost of living crisis, low wages and an inability to access housing in major cities. House prices in Portugal have more than doubled ⁠⁠since 2017, while rents for new leases have increased nearly as much.

Portuguese Parliamentary Affairs Minister Carlos ‌‌Abreu ‌‌Amorim said on Friday that the “government will not yield to shouts from the street”.Protesters said their leaders are “out of touch” with the problem.

In Milan and Bologna, Italian police reported that, alongside peaceful cost of living rallies, protesters threw stones and clashed with officers.



Italian media reported several injuries and arrests.

French protests spill over

None of the protests reached the same scale as the nationwide rallies in France but they may be a sign of spilling over into other European nations, according to Alberto Alemanno, Professor of EU Law & Policy at HEC Paris business school.

“France is the epicentre of this movement … and there are signs now that this is spreading beyond France,” Alemanno told Al Jazeera.

He said Saturday’s protests may not be the last in many of these countries and new hotspots could emerge.

In Greece, Germany, and Austria, the “early stages” of a movement is emerging, with mobilisation expected “in the coming week”, he said.

They are not a single movement, he explained, but several protests happening at the same time, with some “shared grievances”: underfunded education, rising costs and, for students, uncertain prospects after graduation.

The unrest comes at a crucial time for Europe, as the continent prepares for what Alemanno called an “unprecedented super-cycle of national elections” in the coming 12 months, with votes scheduled in Spain, France, Italy and Poland.

“Inevitably, all these protests, all these mobilisations, are going to be at the centre of the political conversation,” Alemanno said.

World.title: At least 17 killed in stampede at religious gathering in India
World.content:
Incident took place at festival in north Kolkata in India’s West Bengal state amid big crowds and rainfall, police said.

Share At least 17 killed in stampede at religious gathering in India on social media

A “stampede” during a Hindu religious festival in eastern India has killed at least 17 people and injured 25, officials said.

A seven-year-old girl was among the fatalities in Saturday’s disaster in north Kolkata in West Bengal, the state’s Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari told reporters.

“Six bodies have so far been identified,” Adhikari said.

Police said the injured were taken to hospital from a Durga Puja pandal, a temporary pavilion housing idols of the goddess Durga at a festival which attracts thousands of ⁠⁠⁠⁠devotees.

A police statement said the stampede happened in the evening due to “heavy crowds of pandal hoppers amid rainfall”.

A senior police official at the scene told the AFP news agency that an announcement caused “commotion” after it started raining and the “crowd waiting outside the pandal [pavilion] was pushing, pulling and rushing forward and fell on the ground, leading to the stampede.”

Prime Minister Narendra Modi described the incident as “saddening.”

“Condolences to the bereaved families. Wishing the injured a speedy recovery. The West Bengal Government is providing all possible help to the affected families,” Modi wrote on X.

⁠Modi’s office announced a ⁠compensation payment of 200,000 rupees ($2,106) for the next of kin of those who died and ‌50,000 rupees ($527) each for the injured.

Interior Minister Amit Shah said the “administration is ensuring that all possible medical facilities are being provided to the injured.”

Deadly crowd incidents happen frequently at Indian mass events, such as religious festivals, often due to poor management and safety lapses.



Last year, a stampede at India’s Kumbh Mela religious fair killed 30 people and injured several others. In Bengaluru, 11 fans were crushed to death during celebrations for the local cricket team’s first Indian Premier League title.

In southern Tamil Nadu state, 36 people were killed in a stampede at a campaign rally for a popular actor-turned-politician

In 2024, 121 people were killed in northern Uttar Pradesh state during a Hindu religious gathering.

World.title: Albanian police fire rubber bullets as protests against Rama escalate
World.content:
Five days of clashes rock Tirana as students join a wider movement demanding Prime Minister Edi Rama’s resignation.

Share Albanian police fire rubber bullets as protests against Rama escalate on social media

Police in Albania have fired rubber bullets at antigovernment protesters in the capital, Tirana, as violent clashes intensify over demands for Prime Minister Edi Rama to resign.

The clashes continued on Saturday for a fifth consecutive day after high school and university students joined a broader movement against Rama, whose governing centre-left Socialist Party has held power since 2013.

The unrest has brought growing anger over education, unemployment and alleged corruption into a wider confrontation with the government.

Protesters threw stones, petrol bombs and fireworks at police near Rama’s office and elsewhere in central Tirana.

Some set cars and rubbish bins alight, creating burning barricades across streets.

Police responded with tear gas, water cannon and baton charges as demonstrators pushed against security lines.

The AFP news agency reported that officers used rubber bullets for the first time since the demonstrations began.

National police chief Skender Hita confirmed their use at a news conference on Saturday, saying they had been deployed “in a limited manner”.

The Ministry of Health and Social Welfare said nine protesters and four police officers received medical treatment on Saturday.

Hita said 167 people had been arrested over five days of unrest, while 132 officers had been injured.

Seven police officers were also suspended pending investigations into allegations that they had exceeded their authority.

Rama, who is serving his fourth term and has refused to resign, visited businesses damaged during the unrest on Saturday. He promised to listen to students and protect their right to demonstrate, while warning against further destruction.



He also accused his conservative political opponents of encouraging the violence.

Growing discontent

The students have complained about expensive university fees, poor educational facilities and limited employment opportunities, alongside allegations of government corruption.

At the start of Saturday’s demonstration, protesters set fire to a suitcase and threw it into the Ministry of Education’s courtyard. AFP reported that the gesture symbolised their determination not to leave Albania in search of better opportunities.

“We are demanding our rights, our future and a better country,” journalism student Sinan Billa told AFP.

The student demonstrations have added to months of antigovernment rallies organised by the Flamingo movement, which began as a campaign against a luxury tourism development on Albania’s southern coast.

The project is linked to an investment company founded by Jared Kushner, the son-in-law of US President Donald Trump.

The movement has since widened its demands to include Rama’s resignation amid allegations of corruption against his government.

The unrest has also spread beyond Tirana. Local media reported that protesters in the coastal city of Durres damaged a post office and blocked roads with burning barricades, extending the confrontations beyond the capital.

World.title: Violent clashes, looting and buildings ablaze in France as over 1,000 arrested after protests
World.content:
Violence broke out across France on Saturday during the latest day of demonstrations against education standards and the cost of living.

At least 1,200 people were arrested during what the French government described as an "escalation in violence" alongside an estimated 550,000 taking to the streets.

In Paris, there were significant clashes into the evening with riot police, who used tear gas and water cannon on crowds.

Buildings were set alight in the capital and other areas, including in Limoges where a large fire in the town hall caused the roof to partly collapse.

Looting broke out in several cities, with widespread vandalism targeted against city halls and businesses also reported.

World.title: Trump waives several Russia sanctions as row with Zelensky intensifies
World.content:
Many of these provisions have now been waived by Trump.

Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev called the waiver "an important and truly historic moment".

Posting on X, he said the sanctions would have inflicted "serious damage", primarily on the US and global market, and that economic cooperation benefits both nations.

Democrats including the Virginia Congressman Don Beyer criticised the move, accusing Trump of capitulating to Moscow and turning his back on Kyiv and Zelensky.

"Trump's latest surrender to Putin again betrays our Ukrainian partners and defies clear congressional intent of legislation designed to punish Russia for its illegal war of aggression," Beyer wrote on X.

A handful of Republicans, too, have come out against the move.

Senator Ted Cruz of Texas, a Trump ally, called waving sanctions against Russia a mistake, saying on Fox News: "I wish the president hadn't done it."

He added there were other ways to could address diesel prices and "the current path, unfortunately, just... benefits Putin and that's not a good idea."

Senator John Cornyn, also of Texas, said on X: "Helping Putin in Ukraine is reckless. He would not stop with Ukraine and our NATO allies would be next."

North Carolina Senator Thom Tillis called it "beyond irresponsible", noting the sanctions legislation passed the chamber with bipartisan support and a large majority - only 11 senators voted against it.

Trump could bring down energy prices "by solving the Iran problem, not by doing a solid for Vladimir Putin," he said.

Nebraska Representative Don Bacon said many lawmakers will resist funding the president's agenda "knowing he is propping up a dictator's invasion and throwing an ally under the bus".

The move is likely to draw further anger from Ukraine, where Zelensky has long stressed the need for stringent sanctions to limit funding Russia can use in its war effort.

Zelensky said on Saturday morning that the sanctions "could have helped enormously" and that the law was "supposed to impose truly effective pressure on Russia to bring this war to an end".

He pointed to Russian overnight attacks on 15 Ukrainian energy facilities that had caused power cuts in several regions and said: "Russia is trying to cause a blackout in Ukraine â right before winter."

Zelensky said it was "important that everyone in America also sees what is really happening" on the ground.

World.title: European diplomats attacked by Israeli settlers in West Bank
World.content:
A delegation of European diplomats has been attacked by masked Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank.

Belgium condemned the assault on its consul general and the other envoys and called for Israel to bring those responsible to justice.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) also condemned what they called "the severe act of violence" and said they were investigating.

But the office of the Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cast doubt on what happened and suggested it was part of a "coordinated campaign to smear Israel".

The attack came only a day after a number of Palestinians and Heidi Levine, a Washington Post photographer, were injured in a separate assault by settlers in another village in the West Bank.

The diplomats - from Belgium, France, Poland and the Catholic Church - had come to the largely Christian village of Taybeh near Ramallah.

They were there to assess the situation on the ground after almost near daily attacks by Israeli settlers on Palestinians trying to bring in their olive harvest.

Video footage from the scene showed masked settlers confronting the convoy. Reports suggest stones were thrown.

The Belgian authorities said a car from its consulate had a window smashed and a French mayor was assaulted. Video showed a man wearing a French tricolor sash slumped beside a vehicle.

Belgium's foreign minister Maxime Prevot condemned the attack and said Israel had a responsibility to bring those responsible to justice.

"Palestinians face this violence every day. Settlers also target journalists reporting on it and diplomats. Harvesting olives, reporting the news or carrying out diplomatic duties should never put anyone at risk of attack," he said.

"As the occupying power, Israeli authorities must protect Palestinians, ensure the safety of diplomats and journalists, and bring those responsible to justice.

"Impunity for violent settlers must end. Belgium will continue to press for EU sanctions against those responsible for this violence and those who support them."

Gideon Sa'ar, Israel's foreign minister, said he strongly condemned the violence by what he called "Israeli rioters". He said the foreign ministry was in contact with the ambassadors of the countries involved.

But he added: "Without detracting from the severity of the incident, it is unfortunate that the visit was not coordinated with the IDF in advance. Such coordination could have helped safeguard the visitors' security."

The IDF said they "strongly condemn the severe act of violence that took place in the area of Taybeh, during which diplomatic representatives were attacked by Israeli rioters."

"According to a preliminary inquiry, no IDF soldiers were present at the scene at the time of the attack," they added.

World.title: Anti-government protesters battle with police in Albania
World.content:
Demonstrators and riot police fought pitched battles in the centre of Tirana on Saturday for the fifth day in a row.

Masked protesters, many of them high school and university students, hurled rocks and petrol bombs at riot police trying to defend the education ministry, one of the focal points of the protests.

The police responded with water cannon and volleys of tear gas, sending the crowds scattering. There are also reports that rubber bullets were used for the first time.

Protests which began in the summer have grown into a wider anti-government movement, with calls for the prime minister to resign following corruption allegations linked to his administration.

Many of the protesters in central Tirana wore gas masks or face masks, while volunteers handed out syringes of saline eyewash to reduce the pain from the tear gas which billows down the street.

The constant boom of petrol bombs could be heard exploding on Saturday.

During the afternoon, the focus of the protests shifted to the office of Prime Minister Edi Rama on the city's main boulevard.

Here the crowds swelled to far larger numbers than on previous days.

Riot police faced a steady hail of cobble stones and fireworks, and responded with barrage after barrage of tear gas, some of the canisters landing far back in the crowds, causing panic.

Incensed by the gas, the crowds waited for it to clear, then renewed their attacks.

World.title: At least 17 dead in crush at Hindu festival event in India
World.content:
At least 17 people have been killed and many more injured in a crush at an event in the Indian city of Kolkata to mark the Hindu festival of Durga Puja, officials say.

The incident occurred during sudden rainfall, which witnesses say prompted a surge of people to try to seek shelter.

West Bengal's Chief Minister Suvendhu Adhikari said a seven-year-old girl was among the dead, and that 25 people were being treated for injuries.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi described it as a "tragic" incident and said the regional government was providing help to affected families.

Six of the dead have been identified, Adhikari said.

A senior police official told the AFP news agency that an announcement caused "commotion" after it started raining and the crowd started "pushing, pulling and rushing forward and fell on the ground, leading to the stampede.".

Deadly crowd incidents, including during religious festivals, are not uncommon in India due to poor management and lack of adequate safety precautions.

Two years ago, 121 people were killed in Uttar Pradesh during a Hindu religious gathering.

World.title: Photos show luxury boat with 50m pool and water slides near Kim Jong Un's summer retreat
World.content:
An 80m (263ft) luxury vessel has been repeatedly spotted in satellite images off North Korea's Wonsan coast from July to mid-October this year.

What stands out is the 50m swimming pool along the deck, with a cluster of waterslides at one end.

After sitting idle for months at a maintenance facility, it relocated in early July to waters off a strip of coastline known as the Kalma Peninsula.

This is close to Wonsan, a seaside resort with a sprawling villa used by North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and his family.

It was not the only large vessel on the move. A handful of others were also repeatedly seen near Kim's villa, in satellite images analysed by the BBC.

The vessels are widely believed to be used by Kim and his family. Former North Korean officials, defectors and experts say it would be difficult for anyone unconnected to the regime's leadership to own or freely use vessels of this size.

World.title: Teacher fought US school attacker before armed dad shot suspect 'multiple times'
World.content:
Some readers may find this article distressing.

A female teacher in the US state of Oregon tackled a teenage shooter who entered her classroom and tried to wrestle the gun from his grasp, police have said.

The teacher, who has not been named, threw her mobile phone before trying to disarm the 16-year-old on the floor of a classroom at Silver Rail Elementary in the city of Bend.

The attacker killed three children and a teacher after shooting his way into the building on Thursday.

He was shot dead by a father with two daughters at the school, who was driving past as the attack started to unfold and, armed with a pistol, ran in to confront the suspect.

Police said the attacker used to be a student at the school. His motive remains unclear.

He had been armed with about 44 more rounds of shotgun ammunition when he was stopped, police said. He fired as many as 15 rounds in the class.

"To the people who showed courage in the face of such violence and intervened to prevent this tragedy from being any worse, we owe you a debt of gratitude," Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said.

Police used a news conference on Friday to identify two of the four victims of the school shooting. They were five-year-old Rhoam Summer and 25-year-old teacher Meghan Lambert.

Lambert's family said in a statement shared by the police that her goal was to be a teacher in the district in which she grew up and that she was "compassionate and had a huge heart".

"She always fought for the underdog and those with special needs," they said.

Bryan Jolly, Summer's grandfather, said the family was devastated by his death.

"The whole thing is senseless, and a shock," he told the New York Times, saying his grandson was "was very bright and very mischievous and very fun-loving, and totally without fear".

The families of the two other students who were killed, an eight-year-old and 11-year-old, did not wish to have them publicly identified yet, police said.

Two others were injured in the attack. Another teacher, a 54-year-old, was still being treated at hospital, and a seven-year-old student, who was in serious but stable condition.

World.title: Three men jailed for 158 years each for murdering Australian and US surfers in Mexico
World.content:
