A Mexican judge has sentenced three men convicted of murdering Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and their US friend Carter Rhoad to 158 years and nine months in jail each.

The Robinsons and Rhoad were killed in an apparent botched robbery of their truck on a secluded beach in Baja California in 2024 while they were on a surfing trip, the court heard during the trial.

The murders sent shockwaves around the world, particularly in Australia, as the area is usually safe from the violence seen in other parts of Mexico.

The guilty verdict was handed down last week. Debra Robinson, the brothers' mother, told the courtroom that her sons' murders had taken "the future we had imagined with them".

The convicted killers' full names were not given for legal reasons, meaning they were only identified as JesÃºs Gerardo, Irineo Francisco and Ãngel JesÃºs.

In November last year, the girlfriend of the alleged ringleader, JesÃºs Gerardo (alias "El Kekas"), was sentenced in a separate trial to 20 years in prison. She had admitted to involvement in the robbery.

The court heard that the bodies of the victims were found dumped down a well with gunshot wounds to their heads.

At the time, the murders shocked locals and tourists in the beach town of Ensenada who were disturbed at the apparent ease and sheer pointlessness of the killings.

Ensenada has a reputation as a welcoming spot for surfers, but the chilling murders revealed how commonplace such extreme violence remains in Mexico.

The only explanation the authorities were able to give was that the surfers - all in their early 30s - had ultimately been murdered for being in the wrong place at the wrong time.

Their killings happened barely 36 hours after they crossed into Mexico from the US. Their bodies, however, were not found for another week, when their families were able to identify them.

Local surfers also called for greater security for residents and visiting tourists, citing other recent examples of violence in the state. Tourism is a key part of the regional economy in Baja California.

World.title: 2027: Keke riders endorse Mbah, Tinubu, as governor extends tricycle operation time to 10pm
World.content:
The Tricycle Riders Association of Enugu State has endorsed the state governor, Dr Peter Mbah, for a second term in office, citing improved security, road infrastructure, and social amenities in the state.

The association, popularly known as Keke Riders, also endorsed President Bola Tinubu, citing the Enugu–Onitsha Road, Enugu–Port Harcourt Expressway, New Artisan Bridge, Obinagu Flyover, and strategic appointments.

This was even as Governor Mbah scrapped the N750 daily payment by tricycle operators and also extended their operational time from 9pm to 10pm.

Mbah also said they would continue to operate at no cost at all the state’s modern transport terminals.

Leading the endorsement at Okpara Square, Enugu, during the conclusion of a “One Million March” event on Saturday, the state Chairman of the Tricycle Riders Association of Nigeria, Kingsley Edeh, said the endorsements were predicated on achievements, especially those that have impacted the lives and businesses of tricycle riders, their families, and the people of Enugu State in general.

“Which will we reel out and leave the other? Is it the security and good roads, which now enable us to ply our trade without any problems, the 267 Smart Green Schools, the completion of long-abandoned projects such as the International Conference Centre, Nigergas Limited, Sunrise Four Mills, Hotel Presidential, and many more?

“We can also see the infrastructure President Tinubu is building in the South East and the support he is giving to our governors.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“So, we will vote APC from top to bottom come 2027,” he declared.

Corroborating the position of the Tricycle Riders Association in Enugu, the body’s National Secretary, Sunday Enang, described Mbah as a ‘magician’ in the art of governance, stressing that no governor anywhere had done what he was able to accomplish in three years.

“Your ‘Tomorrow Is Here’ vision is evident in the construction of modern transport terminals, the establishment of Enugu Air, investment in an asphalt plant, intra- and inter-city road construction, and efforts to improve traffic flow and urban transportation.

“These initiatives are promoting safer, more organised, and more efficient movement across the state.

“We also commend the policy allowing tricycle operators to use designated terminals without paying toll fees. This support recognises their contribution to the economy and the livelihoods of thousands of families.

“These practical policies reflect disruptive innovation and demonstrate how effective leadership can turn vision into tangible opportunities,” he said.

In his response, Mbah described tricycle operators as critical players in the state’s economy, stressing that while his administration was focused on growth, it was equally determined to eradicate poverty, hence the various interventions to increase their disposable incomes.

“You are the powerhouse of our economy because you set out early in the morning, working long hours, navigating traffic, taking our workers to work, taking our students to school, moving our people from urban areas to rural communities, connecting businesses, and helping traders get to their businesses. A lot of people earn their living because of what you do.

“But we also see your struggles. So, I have started engaging with your executives on how we can make life better for you. As the Managing Director of the Transport Terminal just said, no more payment by our tricycle riders at any of the transport terminals.

“Let me also recognise something. Our government, as you know, is not just about growth. We are also interested in ending poverty and making sure that you have more money or disposable income to take care of your family. And so, the issue of tickets is sealed. No more tickets for you.

“Again, when we came into the office in 2023, we inherited a curfew on tricycle operators such that they could only operate from 6am to 9pm. There was a sit-at-home, but we have ended that with your support. Today, Enugu State is safe. So, we will be shifting your operational time limit from 9pm to 10pm,” he said.

While acknowledging their commendation for the rapid construction of roads, Mbah said this was part of the government’s deliberate steps to increase their disposable incomes by reducing their spending on repairs, assuring them that his administration would construct and reconstruct all the remaining 1,022 urban roads in the state.

“Because I understand how bad roads can be terrible, not only for your tricycles and the money you spend on repairs, but also for the time you spend at the mechanic, all the roads in Emene, Abakpa, Idaw River, Trans-Ekulu, Awkunanaw Area, Coal Camp, New Haven, Thinkers Corner, Uwani, among others, are paved or being paved.

“I can assure you that there will be no road in our city that will be unpaved. We are going to pave all the remaining 1,022 roads,” he emphasised.

Meanwhile, Mbah has vowed that his administration would take every step within the law to preserve the security and peace that the people of Enugu had worked to build in the state.

“You must treasure it. You must protect it. Enugu is on an upward trajectory. We will not allow those deceptive voices and politicians who campaign in poetry but only govern in prose. With our government, you have experienced real development and real growth.

“Let me also warn that we have worked extremely hard to establish a safe state. Nobody, no matter their ambition, will take that away from us. And we will not stop at anything, deploying all means necessary within the law to bring to book any violator or anybody who tries to import thugs to disrupt the peace and public safety we enjoy in this city and this state. We have zero tolerance for violence.”

He enjoined the people to make good their endorsements by getting their PVCs ready for the 2027 elections and voting massively for him, all APC candidates, and President Bola Tinubu, whose policies, he said, ensured the availability of resources to execute the numerous projects they listed.

Other speakers at the event were the Enugu State Chairman of the APC, Martins Chukwunweike; Grand Patron of the Enugu State Traditional Rulers Council, HRH Igwe Greg Ugwu; and the Managing Director, Enugu East Zone Transport Terminals, John Egbo.

World.title: $7bn Deep Seaport: Ogun govt tackles PDP candidate over alleged ‘Broken Promise’ remark
World.content:
The Ogun State Government has strongly condemned the description of the proposed $7 billion Gateway Deep Seaport investment as “another broken promise” by the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) senatorial candidate for Ogun East, Abdul-Hameed Omotayo, describing the remark as a reckless distortion of facts, an attempt to politicise a landmark investment and evidence of disregard for the economic prospects of the state.

In a statement on Saturday, the government accused Omotayo of playing dirty politics with an investment initiative backed by formal agreements signed with global port operator DP World in Paris on 24 September 2026, insisting that the agreements, investment commitments and plans for the proposed Gateway Deep Seaport and Blue Marine Special Economic Zone were matters of public record that could be independently verified.

The government said it was particularly troubling that a candidate seeking to represent Ogun East in the Senate would dismiss an investment expected to transform the economic landscape of the host corridor, create employment opportunities and strengthen the state’s industrial and maritime capacity without adequately engaging with the facts surrounding the project.

The statement, signed by the Special Adviser on Media and Strategy to Governor Dapo Abiodun, Kayode Akinmade, said the agreements covering the proposed Gateway Deep Seaport and Blue Marine Special Economic Zone were signed in the presence of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority, Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, and DP World Group Chief Executive Officer, Yuvraj Narayan.

According to the government, the participation of senior Nigerian officials and the leadership of the international port operator underscored the significance of the agreements and the scale of the proposed investment, which is expected to strengthen Ogun State’s maritime infrastructure, expand industrial activities and create employment opportunities.

The government also cited a statement from the State House, signed by the President’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, which reported an initial investment exceeding $7 billion and projected the creation of 50,000 direct jobs.

It maintained that the project should be assessed on the basis of the agreements reached, the commitments made by the parties and verifiable milestones towards implementation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“How can you describe the deep seaport as another broken promise when concrete steps have been taken to advance the project?” the statement asked.

Akinmade said the multiplier effects of major infrastructure investments were too significant to be dismissed on partisan grounds, adding that the initiative had attracted commendation from residents who recognised its potential to expand economic opportunities, attract businesses and create jobs.

He accused Omotayo of being economical with the truth, insisting that responsible political discourse required an appreciation of the distinction between a project backed by formal investment agreements and one that existed only as an announcement.

He stressed that signing an investment agreement marked an important step in the development process, while acknowledging that financing arrangements, regulatory approvals and construction were among the subsequent stages required to bring the project to fruition.

The government also described as laughable Omotayo’s boast that he would defeat Abiodun before noon on election day, dismissing it as political bravado that failed to address the substantive development issues confronting Ogun East.

It characterised the PDP candidate as a political daydreamer, arguing that his focus on electoral boasts rather than the details of major investment initiatives raised questions about his understanding of governance and the processes involved in delivering large-scale infrastructure projects.

Akinmade further questioned the PDP’s political credibility and direction, citing the exclusion of its governorship candidate, Ladi Adebutu, and his running mate from the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) final list of candidates for the 2027 Ogun governorship election.

He said the development followed INEC’s enforcement of statutory requirements governing the submission of party membership registers, adding that the controversy raised questions about the PDP’s internal processes and compliance with electoral regulations.

According to him, the party should address its internal challenges rather than seek to discredit investment initiatives with far-reaching economic implications for Ogun State.

The government maintained that political criticism should be grounded in facts and substantive engagement with policy issues, rather than unsupported allegations or declarations about electoral victory.

On infrastructure development in Ogun East, Akinmade said the Abiodun administration had constructed and rehabilitated more than 243.3 kilometres of roads in the district since 2019, as part of a statewide total exceeding 1,600 kilometres across the 20 local government areas.

Among the projects he cited were the Ijebu-Ode–Mojoda–Epe Road, Sagamu–Iperu–Ode–Sapaade Road, Ejirin–Idowa–Ibefun–Itokin Road in Odogbolu, Tam Balogun Road in Ijebu-Ode and Imodi–Imosan Road.

He also referenced the approval of the J4–Gao Road in Ogun Waterside, alongside the administration’s reported delivery of more than 150 blocks of classrooms, primary healthcare interventions across the district and the Gateway International Agro-Cargo Airport at Iperu-Remo.

The government said the projects formed part of its broader development agenda aimed at improving connectivity, expanding access to essential services and creating an environment conducive to economic growth across the state.

“These are tangible development interventions whose details can be examined and verified. The debate should be about facts, project delivery and the future of Ogun East, not unsupported allegations,” Akinmade said.

The administration maintained that its infrastructure programme and investment initiatives provided a basis for assessing its development record, urging political stakeholders to subject their claims to scrutiny against available evidence.

It also called on residents to distinguish between project announcements, the agreements underpinning them and the subsequent stages required for implementation, stressing that the progress of the proposed Gateway Deep Seaport should be assessed against verifiable developments.

The Gateway Deep Seaport and Blue Marine Special Economic Zone are expected to expand Ogun State’s maritime and industrial capacity, attract domestic and international investment, strengthen logistics and trade, and generate employment opportunities, subject to the successful implementation of the agreements.

The government reiterated its commitment to pursuing investments and infrastructure projects that would broaden the state’s economic base, stimulate private-sector growth and support long-term development.

World.title: Police arrest 67 suspected Vikings cultists at anniversary celebration
World.content:
The Police Command in Delta State has arrested 95 suspected cultists and recovered five firearms and 12 live cartridges during coordinated operations across four local government areas of the state.

The operations, conducted on Thursday, also led to the recovery of seven expended cartridges, suspected cult insignia, branded jackets and charms, according to a statement sent to PREMIUM TIMES on Friday by the police spokesperson, Bright Edafe.

The statement said the arrests followed intelligence-led operations by the Department of Operations, Rapid Response Squad (RRS) and Command Anti-Cultism Unit in Asaba, Ika South, Ughelli South and Okpe local government areas.

The Commissioner of Police, Samuel Erale, directed operatives to intensify the crackdown on cultism and related violent crimes, the statement said.

67 suspects arrested at alleged cult anniversary

The largest operation occurred at a hotel along Abraka Road in Asaba, where police said suspected members of the Supreme Vikings Confraternity, also known as Aro Bagger, had assembled for an alleged cult anniversary celebration, Mr Edafe said.

“A combined team of police operatives raided the premises and arrested 67 suspects, comprising 55 males and 12 females,” Mr Edafe added.

The police said they recovered two pump-action guns, a locally fabricated cut-to-size gun, 10 live cartridges, five expended cartridges, 11 caps bearing suspected cult insignia and two branded cult jackets.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In a related operation in Agbor, Ika South Local Government Area, operatives arrested 15 additional suspects, comprising 14 males and one female, with items suspected to be linked to the same confraternity.

Three arrested in Ughelli South, 10 in Okpe

In another operation, police operatives raided a suspected criminal hideout at Jeremy Community in Ughelli South Local Government Area following intelligence about a gathering of suspected members of the same cult group.

The operation, conducted by the Command Anti-Cultism Unit’s Ovwian-Aladja Sector in collaboration with a civilian anti-cult group, resulted in the arrest of three suspects identified as John Pius, 32; Oghene Ochuko, 28; and Akinbule Godstime, 24.

The police said other suspects fled the scene.

Two locally made pistols, two live cartridges, two expended cartridges, two caps bearing suspected cult insignia, and suspected charms were recovered, according to the statement.

At Jeddo Community in Okpe Local Government Area, operatives arrested 10 additional male suspects over alleged involvement in cult activities.

The police said the suspects and recovered exhibits were in custody, while investigations continued.

Police warn cult groups

Mr Erale commended the operatives for the arrests and directed area commanders, divisional police officers and tactical commanders to intensify operations against cult groups across Delta State.

He warned that the command would not tolerate cult-related activities capable of threatening public peace and urged residents to provide credible information to support security operations.

The arrests come amid renewed attention to the activities of suspected cult groups in the South-south region.

On Friday, the police in Rivers announced that it had queried and relieved the divisional police officer in charge of Abuloma Division and the officer overseeing its police outpost after allegations that suspected cultists renovated the facility.

The police also ordered an investigation into the renovation and the possible involvement of police personnel after a video circulated on social media showing young men identified by a Facebook user as members of Aro Bagger at the outpost during what appeared to be a handover ceremony. Police officers were also seen taking photographs with them.

The police command in the state said legitimate community contributions towards improving police facilities were permissible, but warned that such support must not compromise police independence or confer legitimacy on suspected criminal groups.

The separate incidents have drawn attention to concerns about suspected cult groups and their activities in the region.

World.title: World Food Day: Gov Mbah had created safe environment for large-scale agriculture – Nnaji
World.content:
The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Ugwuanama Farms Ltd, Sani Friday Nnaji, has commended Enugu State Governor, Dr Peter Mbah, for creating a secure and investment-friendly environment that is accelerating agricultural transformation, boosting food production and encouraging large-scale farming across the state.

Nnaji, who gave the commendation to mark the third World Food Day celebration under the Mbah administration, attributed the growing confidence of farmers and agricultural investors in Enugu State to the governor’s deliberate policies, security interventions and commitment to modernising the agricultural sector.

He said the administration had made significant progress in repositioning Enugu among Nigeria’s leading states in agricultural transformation through strategic investments, improved access to farmland, technological innovation and policies designed to attract private-sector participation.

According to him, the transformation of previously insecurity-prone forests and hinterlands into viable agricultural production zones represents one of the administration’s most consequential achievements, particularly for farmers who depend on safe access to their farmlands.

Nnaji praised the governor’s sustained efforts to dislodge criminal elements from forests and rural communities, noting that improved security has strengthened farmers’ confidence and created opportunities for commercial agriculture to thrive.

He highlighted the deployment of Forest Guards, community policing structures, a Command-and-Control Centre, security drones, AI-enabled surveillance cameras and other modern security infrastructure as critical components of the state government’s strategy to protect lives, secure rural investments and restore confidence across farming communities.

He noted that effective security remained indispensable to agricultural development, stressing that farmers could not achieve optimal productivity if they were exposed to harassment, attacks or threats while accessing their farmlands.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Ugwuanama Farms chief executive also applauded the administration’s land reforms and investment-friendly policies, which he said had simplified access to land and strengthened the conditions necessary for commercial farming and agricultural expansion.

“We, the farmers in Enugu State, particularly Ugwuanama Farms Ltd, are successfully operating in the state today because of the governor’s deliberate policies designed to encourage investment, especially in land tenure, which makes commercial farming possible, as well as the flexibility in accessing land and other facilities,” he said.

Nnaji further commended Governor Mbah for promoting agricultural mechanisation, innovation and technology while encouraging young people to embrace farming as a viable source of wealth creation and employment.

He cited the Smart Green Schools initiative, which integrates agricultural activities into the learning environment, as a forward-looking strategy for introducing schoolchildren to modern farming practices and developing the next generation of agricultural entrepreneurs.

According to him, the growing emphasis on agricultural production is already contributing to increased food availability and easing food prices, while strengthening the connection between security, economic prosperity and food security.

He maintained that the administration’s approach demonstrated that securing rural communities and supporting farmers were essential to achieving sustainable food production and economic growth.

Nnaji congratulated Governor Mbah, farmers, agricultural investors and other stakeholders on World Food Day, expressing optimism that the state’s agricultural sector would continue to expand under the administration’s policies.

He urged sustained collaboration between government and private investors to consolidate the gains recorded, attract further investments and position Enugu State as a major agricultural hub capable of creating jobs, improving livelihoods and contributing significantly to Nigeria’s food security.

World.title: WAFU-B U-17 Championship: Nigeria’s Golden Eaglets crash out, to miss AFCON, World Cup again
World.content:
Nigeria’s Golden Eaglets have been eliminated from the 2026 WAFU-B U-17 Championship after drawing 1-1 with Côte d’Ivoire on Saturday in Burkina Faso, ending their hopes of qualifying for the 2027 U-17 Africa Cup of Nations.

The result condemned the team, coached by Eboboritse Uwejamomere, to an early exit after their opening defeat to Niger Republic left them needing a victory to keep their campaign alive.

Nigeria’s failure to beat the Ivorians means the five-time FIFA U-17 World Cup champions will miss another edition of the continental tournament and remain absent from the global competition, which they last featured in 2019.

The Golden Eaglets scored in the 80th minute against Côte d’Ivoire, but the late goal was insufficient to secure the victory they needed. The draw left Nigeria unable to advance to the semi-finals, while Niger and Côte d’Ivoire progressed.

The elimination represents another setback for Nigeria’s youth football programme, given the country’s historic success at U-17 level.

The result is particularly disappointing given Nigeria’s record at the competition and the expectations surrounding Uwejamomere’s team.

Nigeria entered the tournament seeking a return to the U-17 Africa Cup of Nations after missing the previous two editions. The latest failure means the country will miss a third consecutive edition of the continental championship, according to reports on the team’s elimination.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Golden Eaglets will also miss the 2027 FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar, extending their absence from the global tournament to four consecutive editions. FIFA records show that Nigeria last competed at the 2019 edition in Brazil, where they reached the round of 16.

Uwejamomere’s confidence proves misplaced

Ahead of Saturday’s decisive encounter, Uwejamomere had expressed confidence that his players could recover from their opening defeat to Niger.

“We had a setback in the game against Niger Republic, but we are in great spirit to overcome it as we play Côte d’Ivoire on Saturday,” he said before the match.

The coach acknowledged the pressure on his team, describing the fixture as a must-win game, while urging his players to remain composed and believe in their ability to secure the required result.

However, Nigeria could not turn that confidence into the victory needed to keep their qualification hopes alive.

The early exit raises questions about the preparation and development of Nigeria’s youth teams, particularly as the country seeks to rebuild its reputation in age-grade football.

Nigeria remain the most successful nation in FIFA U-17 World Cup history, having won the title five times, in 1985, 1993, 2007, 2013 and 2015.

That pedigree makes the latest failure particularly concerning, with the Golden Eaglets now facing another lengthy wait for a return to the continental and global stages.

World.title: NUJ FCT mourns death of Tribune photojournalist
World.content:
The Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), FCT Council, has expressed deep sorrow over the death of Felix Onigbinde, a photojournalist with the Nigerian Tribune newspaper.

Mr Onigbinde, who reportedly fell into a coma last week and was admitted to the Garki General Hospital, Abuja, before his death, was a dedicated and award winning photojournalist whose career reflected his commitment to the gathering and dissemination of information in the service of society.

He began his journalism career with Daily Trust newspaper before joining the Nigerian Tribune, where he worked until his demise.

As a photojournalist, Mr Onigbinde played a role in documenting events and telling stories through images, contributing to the work of the media in informing the public.

The NUJ FCT Council said his death was particularly heartbreaking, noting that his passing had created a painful void among colleagues and friends, as well as in the wider journalism community.

The Council in a statement issued on Saturday by the the Secretary, Jide Oyekunle, extended its heartfelt condolences to the management and staff of the Nigerian Tribune, Photojournalists Association of Nigeria ( PJAN ) his colleagues, friends and professional associates, praying that God grants them the strength to bear the irreparable loss.

The Council also commiserated with his immediate family, particularly his wife and two children, who are left to cope with the loss of their husband and father.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Onigbinde, who hailed from Ife Modakeke, in Ife East Local Government Area of Osun State, will be remembered by those who knew him for his contribution to journalism and his service to the public through his profession.

The Council prayed for the peaceful repose of his soul and for God to comfort his wife, children, extended family, colleagues and all those mourning his passing.

World.title: Venezia, Fulham win as Adams, Iwobi deliver decisive goals
World.content:
Super Eagles forwards Akor Adams and Alex Iwobi scored decisive goals for their respective clubs on Saturday, helping Venezia and Fulham secure important victories in the Italian Serie A and English Premier League.

Adams scored the winner as Venezia defeated former Italian champions Napoli 1-0, while Iwobi’s first-half strike earned Fulham a 1-0 home victory over Hull City, giving the London club their first Premier League win of the season.

The goals provided a timely boost for the Nigerian internationals, whose contributions proved decisive in closely contested encounters.

Adams sinks Napoli

Adams was the difference between Venezia and Napoli, finding the net in the 49th minute to secure all three points for his side.

The Nigerian forward delivered at a crucial moment in the contest, breaking the deadlock shortly after the restart and giving Venezia the advantage against one of Italy’s leading clubs.

Napoli pushed for an equaliser but could not find a way past the hosts, who held on to protect their lead and claim a significant victory.

The result offers Venezia encouragement as they seek to build momentum in the league, while Adams will hope to maintain his influence in attack as the season progresses.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

For the Super Eagles forward, the match-winning contribution further strengthens his growing importance to his club.

Iwobi ends Fulham’s winless run

In England, Iwobi scored the only goal as Fulham defeated Hull City 1-0 at home to register their first Premier League victory of the season.

The midfielder struck in the 33rd minute, providing the breakthrough Fulham needed after a difficult opening to their campaign.

Before Saturday’s encounter, Fulham had failed to win any of their six league matches, drawing two and losing four. Iwobi’s goal ended that run and earned the team three valuable points.

The victory lifted Fulham to 16th place on five points, offering some relief to the club after their disappointing start.

Nigerian international Calvin Bassey captained Fulham, while Super Eagles defender Semi Ajayi featured for Hull City.

Iwobi’s decisive contribution will also be encouraging for Nigeria as the midfielder continues to combine his creative responsibilities with an increasing ability to influence matches through goals.

Other results

Elsewhere in the Premier League, Manchester City edged Brentford 3-2 at the Etihad Stadium, bouncing back from their UEFA Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain.

The victory moved City to 21 points, temporarily opening a six-point lead over reigning champions Arsenal, who were scheduled to visit Nottingham Forest on Sunday.

Liverpool also secured an important away win, coming from behind to defeat nine-man Brentford 2-1. The result lifted the Reds to fifth place on 12 points.

Chelsea, meanwhile, recorded back-to-back league victories with a 2-0 win over Everton, following their 5-1 triumph over Bournemouth.

World.title: Enugu govt rescues banished teenager allegedly impregnated by father
World.content:
The Enugu State Ministry of Children, Gender Affairs and Social Development has rescued a 16-year-old girl who was banished from her Nenwe Community in Enugu State over allegations that the father impregnated her.

Nenwe is a community in Aninri Local Government Area of Enugu State.

The teenager (name withheld) was banished from the community alongside her father on Thursday.

The banishment

PREMIUM TIMES obtained video clips circulating on Facebook showing some angry community residents warning the teenager and her father never to return to the community.

The crowd led the duo to the exit point of the town.

Residents were heard raining curses on the duo, who were draped in palm fronds, a traditional symbol of abomination in Igbo land.

An elderly resident was heard in one of the clips telling the daughter and the father that the community members were banishing them because what they allegedly did was a taboo in the land.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Nenwe did not offend you. You were the ones who offended yourselves and defiled our land.

“We are not happy that we are banishing you people from Nenwe. We’re banishing you people because you have defiled the land with the abomination you committed,” the resident said in Igbo language.

The incident has elicited reactions in Enugu State since Thursday.

Many Nigerians say while incest remains a taboo in most African societies, banishment is an ancient practice that should be discouraged.

Rescue

The Commissioner for Children, Gender Affairs and Social Development in Enugu State, Ngozi Enih, said her ministry has now rescued the teenager and taken her into safe shelter.

READ ALSO: Enugu approves N32 billion to clear gratuity arrears

Mrs Enih, in a statement posted on her Facebook page on Saturday, explained that the ministry’s intervention followed public outcry against her banishment.

The commissioner said the girl was allegedly raped by the father.

“Under the purposeful leadership of Peter Ndubuisi Mbah, the Enugu State Government remains committed to protecting vulnerable children, upholding their rights and ensuring that survivors of abuse receive the care and support they deserve,” she said.

The commissioner assured Nigerians the survivor’s physical health, emotional well-being and overall welfare would be prioritised.

She further assured that the girl would receive appropriate psychosocial support to help her navigate the trauma she had experienced in order to begin her healing and recovery journey.

Mrs Enih emphasised that no child should ever be blamed, rejected or punished for being a victim of sexual abuse.

“Every child deserves protection, dignity, compassion and justice,” she stated.

Manhunt for the father

Mrs Enih said efforts to arrest the father, said to be on the run, were ongoing.

The commissioner said the ministry remains committed to working with the relevant authorities to ensure that the suspect was prosecuted.

She praised members of the public who raised the alarm and brought the matter to the attention of the government.

“Your voices matter, and together, we can build a society where every child is safe, valued and protected,” she said.

“The Enugu State Government, under the leadership of Peter Ndubuisi Mbah, will continue to strengthen child protection systems and ensure that no vulnerable child is left behind,” she assured.

World.title: Sahel states restart dialogue with ECOWAS
World.content:
Mali, Niiger and Burkina Faso junta leaders

Three junta-ruled Sahel states on Saturday resumed dialogue with the ECOWAS regional bloc which they quit over 18 months ago, agreeing to work together towards a cooperation “framework agreement”.

Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso, led by juntas that came to power between 2020 and 2023, left the Economic Community of West African States in January 2025, after teaming up to create their own group, the Alliance of Sahel States (AES).

Talks between ECOWAS and the AES had been under way since January 2025 but Saturday was their first official ministerial meeting.

In a joint statement issued Saturday evening, the two sides “welcomed the spirit of fraternity, mutual respect and openness” of the talks, and stressed the importance of maintaining relations of “good neighbourliness” particularly with “respect for sovereignty”.

They agreed to “set up joint thematic working groups (…) to reach a framework cooperation agreement”.

The AES delegation was led by Karamoko Jean-Marie Traore, Burkina Faso’s foreign minister, and the Ecowas delegation by Cheikh Niang, his Senegalese counterpart.

The AES juntas have all turned their backs on France, the former colonial power, and by extension on several countries in the region such as Cete d’Ivoire and Benin, which they consider too close to Paris.

The trio have moved closer politically to Moscow, claiming an anti-imperialist and pro-sovereignty vision, and they have bitterly criticised west African coastal countries which have remained close to France.

World.title: Dubois destroys Wardley in round two to retain WBO heavyweight crown
World.content:
Daniel Dubois scored a crushing second-round knockout victory over fellow Briton Fabio Wardley to retain his World Boxing Organization heavyweight crown on Saturday.

In a much-anticipated rematch of their bruising 11-round classic earlier this year, Dubois dominated Wardley from the opening bell to batter his rival into submission in the second round.

Dubois dropped Wardley after 17 seconds of the contest at the O2 Arena in London, catching the challenger flush on the chin with a huge overhand right.

The 29-year-old Dubois continued to land punches at will throughout the first round, which finished with Wardley clinging on desperately under a barrage a punches on the ropes.

The second round started as the first had ended, with the 6ft 5in Dubois uncorking an array of punches that left Wardley in desperate trouble.

With Dubois unloading on a defenceless Wardley, the towel came in after two minutes and 21 seconds of the round.

Dubois improved to 24-3-0 with 23 knockouts while the 31-year-old Wardley fell to 20-2-1.

AFP

World.title: Ambassador Dele Cole devoted his life to national service — Tinubu
World.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

President Bola Tinubu has expressed sadness over the death of the veteran journalist and diplomat, Ambassador Patrick Dele Cole, saying that the late statesman devoted his life to national service.

Ambassador Cole died at the age of 86.

President Tinubu, in his tribute titled “Farewell to Ambassador Dele Cole, distinguished diplomat, journalist and public servant,” said the late veteran journalist brought distinction to his work in diplomacy, journalism and politics.

The tribute read: “I received with profound sadness the news of the passing of Ambassador Patrick Dele Cole, a distinguished diplomat, journalist, politician, and public servant, who died at 86.

“Ambassador Cole devoted his life to national service, bringing distinction to his work in diplomacy, journalism and politics.

“His career reflected the enduring value of dialogue, tact, mutual respect and the pursuit of shared interests in advancing national development and international cooperation.

“His contributions to Nigeria’s media landscape were particularly notable. As Managing Director of the Daily Times, he upheld the vital role of the press in holding public officials accountable, speaking truth to power, and strengthening democratic governance. His legacy in journalism and public life remains an enduring part of our national story.

“At 86, Ambassador Dele Cole witnessed defining moments in Nigeria’s history and contributed to the nation’s development through his work in the media, diplomacy and public service. His life stands as a testament to the value of experience, principled engagement and commitment to the public good.

“As we mourn his passing, I extend my heartfelt condolences to his family, friends, professional associates and all whose lives he touched. I pray that memories of his remarkable life will bring them comfort and strength at this difficult time.

“May Almighty God grant Ambassador Cole eternal rest and give his family and all who mourn him the fortitude to bear this profound loss.”

World.title: Nigeria’s economy needs continuation of Tinubu’s reforms – Wike
World.content:
Photo: NAN

The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, says Nigeria’s full economic recovery depends entirely on sustaining the bold reform policies initiated by President Bola Tinubu.

Wike said this on Saturday, at the Rainbow Coalition’s stakeholders’ consultation in Ogba-Egbema-Ndoni Local Government Area of Rivers.

He said that only the continuation of the current administration’s economic direction could permanently pull the country back from the brink of collapse.

He noted that the hard economic choices being implemented presently were necessary remedies to salvage a system that was virtually “dead” when Tinubu took office.

“Only the continuation of the economic reforms initiated by the Tinubu government can bring this country back from the economic comatose it was in before this present administration took over,” he said.

He said that the presidential candidate of the Africa Democratic Congress (ADC), Alhaji Abubakar Atiku and his vice, Rotimi Amaechi, had nothing to offer to Nigerians.

The minister urged residents of the state not to surrender the country’s progress to “career politicians” and “political opportunists” whom he likened to “chronic pool betters” who repeatedly gamble with public trust.

According to him, supporting politicians who have made decades-long pursuits for power would mean diverting national funds to recoup lost campaign expenses rather than consolidating economic gains.

Wike further said that the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, would not make any meaningful difference if elected, stressing that Tinubu was the person who had shown true commitment.

Reaffirming that leadership must be judged by past governance records, the former Rivers governor challenged his predecessor to account for major capital allocations in Rivers.

Explaining the political strategy behind the cross-party Rainbow Coalition movement, he said that delivering economic recovery required total alignment between the executive and the national assembly.

He urged voters to support Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates vying for the Senate and House of Representatives seats in the area to ensure legislative cooperation for the president’s economic policy agenda.

He also called on party leaders and community mobilisers to prepare for an overwhelming turnout on election day.

“I want total mobilisation on Jan. 16, 2027. Everybody must be mobilised. Make sure we vote and win decisively to protect our collective future,” he said.

In his remarks, the Executive Chairman of the council, Dr Chukwu Shedrack, commended Wike for his historic development projects in the council, including road construction, hospital upgrades, and human capital investments.

Shedrack highlighted several local governance achievements which he said aligned with the FCT minister’s leadership model.

Reaffirming the council’s political commitment to the Tinubu administration’s economic recovery drive, he pledged a complete block vote for the APC across all elective positions come 2027.

“We are fully mobilised, ward by ward and unit by unit. Come the 2027 general elections, our people will deliver 100 per cent. From president to national assembly and house of assembly, no vote will drop,” Shedrack assured. (NAN)

World.title: Hunters kill two suspected bandits, recover ₦10m ransom in Kano
World.content:
By Hadiza Yusuf

Two suspected bandits have been killed by local hunters, while ₦10 million paid as ransom for a kidnapped man has been recovered in Falgore Forest, Doguwa Local Government Area of Kano State.

This was contained in a statement signed by CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, Police Public Relations Officer, on Saturday.

According to the statement, the kidnapped victim, identified as 45-year-old Kabiru Aliyu of Falgore Village, was released unharmed after the suspects collected the ransom

The incident occurred at about midnight on Saturday, when three suspected bandits allegedly emerged from Falgore Forest to collect the money demanded for Aliyu’s release.

According to the statement, the victim was kidnapped on September 11, 2026, and had spent several days in captivity before his release.

The police said that shortly after collecting the ₦10 million ransom and releasing the victim, the suspects were ambushed by local hunters known as Yan Bula while returning to their hideout in Falgore Forest.

“During the ambush, two of the suspected bandits were neutralised, while the third suspect escaped with injuries. The entire ransom sum of ₦10 million was recovered intact from the neutralised suspects,” the statement said.

The command said preliminary investigations had identified one of the suspects killed as Dogo Isah, a commercial motorcycle rider from Maigwanda Village in Kubau Local Government Area of Kaduna State.

The police said the suspects were believed to have come from Maigwanda Village before the incident.

The Commissioner of Police in Kano State, CP Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, commended the Yan Bula hunters for their efforts in supporting security operations in the area.

Bakori said the hunters’ activities continued to complement the police operation against kidnapping, banditry and other violent crimes in the state under Operation Kukan Kura.

Following the incident, the commissioner directed the Area Commander, Divisional Police Officers and tactical teams operating in the area to immediately search the forest and surrounding communities for the fleeing suspect.

He also directed the teams to intensify efforts to arrest the suspect and recover any weapons used by the group.

The police further disclosed that the rescued victim had been debriefed, medically examined and reunited with his family.

The command assured residents of its commitment to protecting lives and property.

World.title: Benue 2027: Ex-Otukpo council chair, APC, ADC, ZLP chieftains defect to PDP
World.content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi

A former Caretaker Chairman of Otukpo Local Government Area of Benue state, Mr. Inalegwu Adakonye, has defected from the All Progressives Congress (APC) to the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), alongside other political stakeholders and their supporters from the APC, African Democratic Congress (ADC) and Zenith Labour Party (ZLP).

The defection featured several prominent political figures from Adoka and Ugboju communities in Otukpo council.

Among prominent politicians who weekend in Otukpo joined the PDP with the former chairman of Otukpo were Adoga Edache, popularly known as Ebo, from the ADC; Emmanuel Akoche of the ZLP; Garuba Sule of the APC; and Mr. John Ojonye, ADC Chairman of Ugboju Ehaji Ward, alongside other party members and supporters.

Explaining his decision to return to the PDP, Adakonye said the party’s ideology of inclusiveness and collective participation informed his choice, arguing that its approach to politics differed from that of the APC.

He said “the PDP treats its members as one family and offer a platform where everyone can participate. And I am confident that the party is best positioned to rescue Benue state from bad governance.”

Adakonye, who led APC members from Adoka and Ugboju into the PDP, also cited the emergence of Dr. Oyije Ogbenjuwa as the party’s deputy governorship candidate as a factor behind their decision.

He said they could not afford to remain outside the political movement of their brother and friend, who he expressed confidence would soon become the deputy governor of the state.

The defectors also cited the PDP’s people-oriented ideology, leadership and prospects in forthcoming elections as reasons for abandoning their former parties for the opposition platform.

Receiving the new members were the PDP deputy governorship candidate, Dr. Ogbenjuwa; the Otukpo Local Government PDP Chairman, Godwin Ochapa; the party’s House of Assembly candidate for Otukpo/Akpa, Johnson Egli; its candidate for Adoka/Ugboju, Gabriel Olofu; and the Senior Legislative Aide to the Senate President, Chief George Alli.

Speaking on behalf of the party, Ogbenjuwa welcomed the defectors and assured them of “equal opportunities and full integration into the party’s activities.”

He described their decision to join the PDP “as evidence of the party’s growing acceptability across Benue South Senatorial District, and your support will further strengthen our political base ahead of future elections.”

The new members, in turn, pledged their loyalty and commitment to working for the success of the PDP at all levels.

World.title: How my mother was kidnapped over $2.4bn subsidy fraud — Okonjo-Iweala
World.content:
Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala

Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, the Director-General of the World Trade Organisation, WTO, has recalled how her investigation into an alleged $2.4bn fuel subsidy fraud in Nigeria led her mother’s kidnapping.

Read Also: Okonjo-Iweala’s mother, 82, kidnapped

Okonjo-Iweala narrated her experience in an interview with Bloomberg’s Francine Lacqua. She said the kidnappers’ demands were that she resigns as the Minister of Finance and leave the country.

On how the ordeal began, she said her office noticed a sharp increase in subsidy claims, so she began to probe.

Her words: “So I went to the president and said, look, something is going on here. Could we audit the accounts? And he said, yes, go ahead.

“And we found about $2.4 billion worth of fraud. So we refused to pay.”

That was when they took her mother. Okonjo-Iweala said the five-day ordeal was among the most painful periods of her life.

“I was told (by the kidnappers) that for her to be released, I should resign and leave the country.

“She was held in the middle of a forest, and one night she escaped. She’s still alive. She’s 96 now.”

“It was a terrible, terrible five-day ordeal. I think the worst in my life,” she said.

Okonjo-Iweala said initially she felt paralysed by fear and considered resigning. She added that that the experience left her with a sense of guilt that she still carries.

“I never dreamt my parents could ever be touched in this way, that people would be that evil,” she said.

On her father’s reaction at the time, she said: “He said, ‘We don’t give in to blackmail’. And he said, ‘You’ve got to carry on. You’ve got to go to work’.”

Okonjo-Iweala served as Minister of Finance under President Goodluck Jonathan. Her mother, Kamene Okonjo, was kidnapped from her home in Ogwashi-Uku, Delta State, in December 2012. Read the kidnap story HERE.

Vanguard News

World.title: Zulum calls for coordinated military offensive in the Lake Chad
World.content:
Borno State governor, Babagana Zulum

…Zulum’s support instrumental to military success – COAS

By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri

Borno State Governor, Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, has called on the military to immediately commence a coordinated offensive operation, Operation Lake Sanity, to dislodge insurgents from the shores and islands of Lake Chad.

Governor Zulum made the call on Saturday when he received the Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shuaibu, on a courtesy visit at the new Council Chamber, Government House, Maiduguri.

The governor commended the Nigerian Army for improvements in the security situation in the state and also requested stronger military deployments in strategic locations, including Kareto, Baga, and the Sabon Gari–Wajiroko axis, to protect communities, secure waterways, and support the reopening of the Damboa–Biu road.

“The recent attacks on some communities in northern Borno are a result of the presence of insurgents along the shores of Lake Chad. We cannot achieve complete peace without undertaking major military operations in that area,” Zulum said.

The governor acknowledged President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s support for the proposed operation and the coordination among the service chiefs; however, he urged the military authorities to accelerate preparations.

“I understand that the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, has provided the necessary support for the operation. I urge you to hasten the process so that the insurgents threatening northern Borno can be dislodged,” he stated.

He called for strengthening the amphibious command in Baga to clear waterways, stressing that holding those positions would be essential to sustaining the operation’s gains.

On the Gubio–Damasak corridor, Zulum appealed for the speedy establishment of a military formation in Kareto, and around Sabon Gari and Wajiroko in Damboa Local Government Area to support the restoration of vehicular movement between Damboa and Biu.

Governor Babagana Zulum thanked the Chief of Army Staff for training about 1,000 forest guards, who he said had completed their training and were deployed to the state.

Zulum emphasised the need to consolidate military successes through reconstruction, rehabilitation and resettlement, commending the Army’s support for re-establishing the Mairari community and preparing for military formations and community resettlement in Maiwa, Koshobe and Ala.

“Military operations must be followed by stabilisation measures, including reconstruction, rehabilitation and resettlement. Borno State Government will provide the support required by the Nigerian Army to fortify these locations,” he pledged.

He also expressed appreciation for additional battalions deployed across the two sectors, noting that the reinforcements were helping to strengthen security and stabilise affected areas.

“Notwithstanding the recent attacks in some parts of Borno State, there has been tremendous improvement in our security situation. I commend the officers and men of Operation Hadin Kai and urge them to sustain this momentum,” Zulum announced.

The Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shuaibu, commended Governor Babagana Umara Zulum for his sustained support to the Nigerian Army, describing it as instrumental to the successes recorded against insurgency.

“I must put on record that the support of the Executive Governor of Borno State has been phenomenal in the successes we have recorded here in Borno State. For that, we say a very big thank you, sir,” the COAS said.

The Army Chief explained that his visit to troops of Operation Hadin Kai was part of a routine assessment of their operations, to encourage commanders, and to appreciate the resilience of personnel confronting insurgency in the Northeast.

He reaffirmed their mandate to restore normalcy and create an enabling environment for socio-economic activities, assuring that challenges presented by commanders would receive prompt attention.

The courtesy visit was attended by the Senate Chief Whip, Senator Mohammed Tahir Monguno, member representing Marte, Monguno, Nganzai federal constituency, Hon. Bukar Talba, Secretary to the State Government, Commissioners, Special Advisers and other senior military and heads of security establishment in the state. End

World.title: TETFund Budget Jumps From N320bn To N1.6trn, Says Masari
World.content:
Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) budget has risen sharply from N320.3 billion in 2023 to N1.6 trillion in 2025, reflecting increased federal government investment in tertiary education.

Chairman of TETFund Board of Trustees, Aminu Bello Masari, disclosed this at the 2026 National Town Hall Meeting of the Fund held in Abuja yesterday.

Masari said the figure rose from N320.3 billion in 2023 to N683.4 billion in 2024 before hitting N1.6 trillion in 2025, about five times the 2023 allocation, demonstrating President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to human capital development.

He however stressed that the increased funding must translate to tangible results in academic performance, research output and graduate employability.

Masari disclosed that 271 institutions are covered under the 2026 annual direct intervention, with about N2.526 billion for each university, N1.871 billion for each polytechnic and N2.057 billion for each college of education.

He said the Fund committed N10 billion in 2026 to skills acquisition centres in polytechnics, supported innovation and entrepreneurship facilities in 12 universities, and approved N48 billion for upgrading engineering and technology facilities.

He added that about N6.09 billion was approved for 174 successful research proposals under the 2025 National Research Fund grant cycle, while presidential approval has been secured for six additional Centres of Excellence in robotics, coding, Artificial Intelligence, machine learning and cybersecurity, bringing the total to 36 centres.

Masari urged beneficiary institutions to ensure transparency, prudent management and proper maintenance of facilities, warning that funding alone cannot fix all challenges.

Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, said government is pushing curriculum reforms to produce graduates with practical, industry-relevant skills, commending TETFund for supporting infrastructure, research and specialised equipment.

Alausa said reforms include a proposed 80 percent practical and 20 percent theoretical curriculum model, with 36 new and reviewed National Diplomas, 10 additional ND programmes, 30 National Certificates in Education and 21 National Occupational Standards already produced 27 new and four reviewed.

He said programmes will continue to be aligned with labour market demands, and that initiatives like NELFUND will expand access so that financial hardship, disability or location does not block qualified Nigerians from completing education.

Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, described education as critical to human capital development and national productivity, calling for effective monitoring and transparent reporting to ensure investments deliver impact.

Executive Secretary of TETFund, Sonny Echono, disclosed that over 418 projects are ready for commissioning across beneficiary institutions, with 14 projects at one institution alone.

He said the Fund is expanding investments in infrastructure, research, student welfare, innovation and digital learning, supporting student innovation from idea development to intellectual property protection and industry linkage.

Echono added that student transportation initiatives cover 42 institutions, with about 98 schools provided electric-powered vehicles for affordable student transport, while the Fund is working with the Ministry of Labour to align skills development with manpower needs.

World.title: Over 1,000 Participate In Pinknaija Walk 2026, Puts Port Harcourt At Centre Of Breast Advocacy
World.content:
Sylvester Idowu in Warri

‎

More than 1,000 participants converged on Captain Elechi Amadi Polytechnic, Rumuola, Port Harcourt, on Saturday, October 10, for PinkNaija Walk 2026, in a major show of support for breast cancer awareness, early detection and improved access to cancer care.

‎

‎Organised by Engraced Life Foundation (ELF), the annual eight-kilometre walk brought together representatives of the Rivers State Government, health institutions, cancer organisations, survivors, students, corps members, business owners, influencers and members of the public under the theme, ‘United By Unique—Every Story Matters. Every Life Counts.’

‎

‎Recognised by the state, as the leading statewide breast cancer awareness mobilisation since 2021, and the biggest of its kind in the South-south region, the event transformed the Rumuola venue into a meeting point for organisations and individuals working to improve cancer awareness and patient support.

‎

‎The morning opened with an energetic warm-up session, before the Rivers State Government delegation and WHO led participants on the walk. The eight-kilometre route began and ended at Captain Elechi Amadi Polytechnic, taking participants through Rumuola and surrounding parts of Port Harcourt.

‎

‎The walk was followed by an interactive health and community engagement featuring medical information stands, breast health demonstrations, health talks, games, vendors and free screening services.

‎

‎Representing the Permanent Secretary of the Rivers State Ministry of Health, Dr Hope Avundaa, in an opening remarks, highlighted the importance of public awareness, early detection and collaboration in improving health outcomes.

‎

‎The Nigerian Medical Association (NMA), the Medical Women’s Association of Nigeria (MWAN), Peter Odili Cancer and Cardiovascular Hospital (POCCH) and the World Health Organization (WHO) community were among the medical and institutional stakeholders represented at the event.

‎

‎More than 400 women and men received health screening services, including breast and cervical cancer screening, prostate screening, blood pressure and blood sugar checks, alongside access to medical consultations assisted by Power Oil.

‎

‎The screening activities reinforced the foundation’s message that awareness must translate into practical access to health information, medical assessment and appropriate referrals.

‎

‎One of the event’s major highlights was a special parade by the Engraced Life Foundation medical team, led by Dr. Stella Jerry Chukwu that showcased the foundation’s achievements and recognitions over the years, culminating in the presentation of its latest international honour.

‎

‎In September 2026, the Union for International Cancer Control (UICC) announced Engraced Life Foundation as the winner of the World Cancer Day Campaign Award for its PinkRoom Schools Outreach initiative.

The award was presented at the World Cancer Congress in Hong Kong, recognising the foundation’s work in advancing the global United by Unique campaign through education, community engagement and people-centred cancer care.

‎

‎The recognition places a Nigerian community-based cancer advocacy organisation among the international initiatives celebrated by UICC and highlights the contribution of locally driven programmes to global cancer control.

‎

‎For founder Ethel Olumo, the recognition represents both an achievement and a call to greater responsibility.

‎

‎“Receiving this recognition on an international platform means a great deal to us. It affirms that the work we are doing in our communities matters, and that solutions developed in Nigeria can contribute meaningfully to the global fight against cancer. For us, the award is not the end of the journey. It is a call to reach more people, especially young girls and underserved women who may otherwise be left out of essential health information and care,” Olumo said.

‎

‎The foundation’s achievement comes amid growing international attention to Nigeria’s role in cancer advocacy and the country’s contribution to global cancer-control efforts.

‎The walk provided a platform for cancer survivors to share their experiences and encourage others to seek care without shame or fear.

‎

‎Among them was Benita Egone, a six-year thriver who travelled from Warri, Delta State, to participate. Her account of survival offered encouragement to women navigating diagnosis, treatment and recovery, while underscoring the importance of emotional support and a community that treats survivors with dignity.

‎

‎Dr Ngozi Welle, breast cancer survivor and New York-based founder of VictoriousNG, also joined the engagement, addressing women and celebrating survivors. She was one of many guests who travelled from different locations, including the United States, to participate in the campaign and show solidarity with the cancer advocacy community.

‎

‎For many participants, the gathering was an opportunity to see breast cancer awareness beyond the usual October campaign: as a continuing responsibility that involves listening to survivors, supporting patients and ensuring that women can access timely information and appropriate care.

‎

‎Another important feature of the engagement was the official introduction of FT3, From Testing to Targeted Treatments, by Barbara Ariolu from the ELF medical unit.

‎

‎The international initiative provides patient-centred resources designed to help people affected by cancer and their representatives understand targeted therapies, biomarker testing and the questions they can ask healthcare professionals when considering treatment options. Its inclusion at PinkNaija Walk 2026 extended the campaign beyond prevention and early detection to address the importance of treatment knowledge and informed conversations between patients and medical teams.

‎

‎Survivors and advocates were engaged on how improved understanding of treatment options can support more meaningful participation in healthcare decisions and help patients navigate their care pathways. National Coordinator of Engraced Life Foundation, Tamunotonye Pamela Daniel, thanked the Rivers State Ministry of Health, the office of the Permanent Secretary – Dr. Vincent Wachukwu, WHO Rivers State coordinator and team, medical associations, institutional partners, volunteers, supporters and individuals whose contributions helped make the walk possible.

‎

‎She said the foundation would continue to use every available resource and communication channel to advance breast cancer awareness, encourage early detection and improve access to screening, particularly among underserved communities.

‎

‎“PinkNaija Walk opens our October campaign, but our work continues long after the walk. We are taking the message into communities where women and men may have limited access to screening, reliable information and medical guidance. Our goal is to make early detection and informed health decisions accessible, regardless of where people live or their financial circumstances,” Daniel said.

‎

‎Following the Port Harcourt event, the foundation plans further awareness and screening activities across Ekiti, Lagos and Abia States, alongside additional outreaches in Rivers State and other communities. The national campaign will offer free breast screening, health education and other available health checks, connecting participants to medical professionals and appropriate referrals where necessary.

‎

‎Although the Niger Delta and the wider South-south remain core areas of focus, the foundation says its mission extends across Nigeria, particularly to communities where access to cancer information and early detection services remains limited. As the foundation builds towards World Cancer Day on February 4, 2027, attention is turning to its next phase of school-based advocacy through the PinkRoom Schools Outreach, which targets 20 schools.

‎

‎The initiative provides age-appropriate breast and cervical health education, personal hygiene information, guidance on recognising changes in the body and information on when to seek help from a trusted adult or qualified health professional. It also aims to equip girls with practical self-care resources and dignity kits, helping to make health education accessible and relevant to their daily lives.

‎

‎The urgency of reaching young people is underscored by the need to ensure that girls understand their bodies, can discuss health concerns without stigma and know where to seek reliable guidance. While breast changes and lumps do not automatically indicate cancer, any unusual or persistent change should be assessed by a qualified health professional.

‎

‎The foundation is therefore calling on schools, government agencies, healthcare providers, corporate organisations, development partners and individual supporters to collaborate in reaching the 20 targeted schools and expanding the programme’s impact. With PinkNaija Walk 2026 setting the pace for another season of advocacy, Engraced Life Foundation is urging Nigerians to support the campaign towards World Cancer Day 2027 and help ensure that awareness leads to practical action.

‎

‎For the foundation, the message remains clear: every story matters, every life counts, and access to cancer awareness and early detection must extend beyond the event ground into the communities where it is needed most.

World.title: Navy Intensifies Crackdown on Oil Thieves, Uncovers Three Underground Reservoirs Containing 75,000 Litres of Crude Oil
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Nigerian Navy has intensified its crackdown on oil thieves, as troops of Operation Delta Sentinel uncovered three dugout reservoirs containing a total of 75,000 litres of crude oil in the Oteghele general area of Delta State. The discoveries followed two separate operations conducted on 12 and 14 October 2026.

The Service said the operations, carried out by Nigerian Navy Ship (NNS) Delta, led to the discovery of approximately 30,000 litres of suspected crude oil in one reservoir on 12 October and a further 45,000 litres in two large reservoirs on 14 October.

According to a statement by the Director of Naval Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, the reservoirs and their contents were handled in accordance with established procedures.

“The successive discoveries highlight the presence of concealed storage points that could facilitate the accumulation and onward movement of suspected stolen crude oil.

“Uncovering these stockpiles disrupts a key link in the illicit petroleum trade and reduces opportunities for the unlawful exploitation of the nation’s oil resources.

“Through Operation Delta Sentinel, the Nigerian Navy has continued to uncover concealed petroleum stockpiles and disrupt infrastructure suspected of supporting crude oil theft,” Captain Folorunsho said.

He stressed that the Navy would sustain intelligence-led operations to identify and dismantle such facilities, constrain the activities of oil thieves and illegal refiners, and protect critical national assets. The ultimate aim, he added, was to curb oil-related economic sabotage and safeguard Nigeria’s petroleum revenue.

World.title: AI Will Transform Healthcare, Says Prof. Okeji
World.content:
.Urge medical professionals to embrace technology

.As PAMO University inducts 28 health professionals

Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

A professor of Radiography and Radiological Sciences at the University of Nigeria Nsukka, Prof. Mark Okeji, has noted that Artificial intelligence (AI) is set to revolutionise healthcare delivery by accelerating diagnosis, improving patient monitoring and supporting clinical decisions.

Prof. Okeji however, urged medical professionals to embrace emerging technologies to remain relevant in a rapidly changing health sector.

Okeji, made the assertion as the induction lecturer at the joint induction and oath-taking ceremony for graduates of the Departments of Medical Laboratory Science, Nursing Science, and Radiography and Radiation Science at PAMO University of Medical Sciences, Iriebe, Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State, yesterday.

He said AI would enhance the efficiency and accuracy of healthcare services rather than simply replace human professionals.

Okeji, warned that practitioners who failed to acquire the skills required to work with the technology risked being left behind.

“AI has not come to replace you. It has come to help you. It makes the job simpler and makes our patients feel better. So, don’t be afraid of it. But if you’re not there to understand AI, AI will take over from you,” he said.

Okeji explained that AI-powered diagnostic systems could analyse medical samples, interpret images and process large volumes of patient information within seconds, significantly reducing the time required for investigations and improving the speed of clinical decisions.

According to him, AI is already being deployed in medical diagnostics, telemedicine, hospital administration, clinical decision-making and remote patient monitoring.

He said wearable devices, including smart watches, could help monitor vital health indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen levels and sleep patterns, providing clinicians with information that could support early intervention.

The professor also highlighted AI’s potential to strengthen public health surveillance by analysing disease patterns, predicting outbreaks and helping authorities deploy medical personnel and resources to areas with urgent healthcare needs.

He identified data fragmentation, privacy concerns, algorithmic bias and inadequate trust among some healthcare professionals as challenges requiring urgent attention.

While advocating stronger ethical safeguards and regulation, Okeji urged medical practitioners and healthcare institutions to develop the competence needed to harness AI responsibly.

“AI is transforming healthcare today. Tomorrow, it will redefine it. The future is intelligent, connected and very human-centred,” he said.

Earlier in his welcome address, the Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Smith Jaja, said the 28 inductees had undergone rigorous academic and clinical training, expressing confidence in their preparedness to serve the healthcare sector.

“We are proud to inform everyone that these graduates have gone through the best training anybody in their respective professions can receive,” Jaja said.

He charged the graduates to uphold professional ethics and honour the oaths they had taken, describing the occasion as a significant milestone for the university, the graduates and their families.

Representing the Pro-Chancellor, Dr. Peter Odili, former Rivers State Commissioner for Health, Prof. Adaeze Oreh, congratulated the inductees and emphasised the importance of collaboration among nurses, medical laboratory scientists and radiographers in delivering safe, effective and patient-centred care.

She described medical laboratory scientists as the “detectives of medicine,” nurses as the “heart and backbone of patient care,” and radiographers as the “eyes of medicine,” stressing that each profession played a critical role in improving patient outcomes.

Oreh also announced that the university’s governing board had approved automatic employment after internship for the best graduating students from the three departments.

She urged the inductees to take their internship seriously, noting that the period was essential to their transition into fully credentialed and licensed professionals.

The Acting Dean of the Faculty of Allied Health Sciences, Dr. Clement Nyenke, said the induction represented more than the completion of academic programmes, describing it as the beginning of a lifelong commitment to patients, professional colleagues and society.

He urged the graduates to demonstrate sound judgement, accuracy and respect for human life in their practice.

World.title: 2027: Kwara ADC Promises to Tackle Insecurity, Food Security If Formed Govt
World.content:
Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

The opposition African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Kwara State has said that it would embark on intensive intelligence gathering, deployment of technology and improved support for conventional security among the residents of the state so as to return the state into her original status of ‘State of Harmony’ if it forms government of the state come 2027.



The party also said that the administration would develop agricultural potential of the state so as to ensure affordable food for all and sundry.



The governorship candidate of the ADC in the state, Hon. Zakari Mohammed, made the promises in Ilorin yesterday while addressing journalists on the sidelines of his governorship ambition in the state.

Mohammed, a former member of the House of Representatives representing Baruten/Kaiama Federal Constituency from 2011 to 2019, stressed that security remained fundamental to development, warning that the rising insecurity in parts of the state could undermine farming activities, economic growth and residents’ livelihoods.

“No meaningful development takes place without security,” he said, outlining his proposed approach to tackling insecurity in the state.

According to him, his administration would prioritise community-based intelligence gathering, the deployment of technology and improved support for conventional security agencies to strengthen the protection of lives and property.

He also called for greater collaboration between residents and security agencies, urging members of the public to report suspicious activities to relevant authorities.

Mohammed, who served in the National Assembly for eight years, said Kwara needed a comprehensive development strategy that would address the peculiar challenges facing its northern, central and southern senatorial districts.

He identified agriculture as a critical sector requiring urgent attention, noting that several communities in the state depended on farming for their livelihoods.

The ADC candidate argued that improving agricultural productivity and supporting farmers would help address food insecurity and reduce the cost of living.

He criticised the economic policies of the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led governments at the federal and state levels, accusing them of placing additional financial burdens on households through taxation and other economic measures.

Mohammed maintained that government should adopt policies that would make food more affordable, citing agricultural subsidies in some countries as examples of interventions that could help reduce production costs and improve food availability.

He also highlighted education and healthcare as important areas that required sustained investment, stressing the need to expand opportunities for residents and improve access to essential services.

On political leadership, the former lawmaker urged voters to assess candidates based on their programmes, competence and capacity to deliver, rather than sentiments or political affiliations.

He challenged political parties and their candidates to explain how they intended to address the challenges confronting the people instead of relying solely on campaign promises.

Mohammed further said the ADC was committed to implementing its manifesto, insisting that candidates elected on the party’s platform would be expected to operate within its policy framework.

He expressed confidence that a government focused on security, agriculture, education, healthcare and economic relief could improve the living conditions of residents across the State.

World.title: Defence Minister Urges Graduating Officers to Adapt Faster Than Those Seeking to Undermine National Security
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (rtd.), has urged graduating military officers to strengthen their ability to anticipate risks, identify vulnerabilities and adapt more quickly than those seeking to undermine national security. He stressed that their task is not simply to respond to threats after they emerge.

He also urged the officers to combine professional competence with intellectual curiosity and the courage to make difficult decisions under pressure.

Speaking at the graduation ceremony of Army War College Nigeria Course 10/2026 yesterday in Abuja, the Defence Minister stressed that Nigeria was making efforts to develop indigenous defence capabilities in various areas while strengthening cooperation with reliable international partners.
