World.title: Reform Party unveils campaign slogan as PM touts economic growth
World.content:
Prime Minister and Reform Party chair Kristen Michal says Estonia's economy is growing twice as fast as the EU average, as Reform pledges a clear course in the 2027 elections.

Speaking at the party's council meeting in Tartu on Saturday, Michal said the largest income tax cut in Estonia's history had doubled economic growth.

"Estonia's economy is growing twice as fast as the EU average," he said, also citing rising wages, consumption, exports and manufacturing, alongside lower unemployment and easing inflation.

"The Reform Party can say with confidence: our plan is working," the prime minister emphasized. "Estonia has been led through a major test and is now on a solid growth path, moving forward even in the face of headwinds."

He noted that wages are rising, with consumer confidence up and people taking home an average of 10 percent more money this year. Defense spending of 5 percent GDP, he added, is also strengthening security and giving families and businesses confidence to plan for the future.

Even the opposition is starting to see that the Reform Party's plan is working, Michal said, accusing Isamaa and the Center Party of already making plans to form a coalition — potentially joined by the Conservative People's Party of Estonia (EKRE).

"The Reform Party is their main enemy for a reason: they can only steal Estonia's prosperity and growth if we're out of the picture," the party chair said, emphasizing that the key issue in the March 2027 elections will be whether this prosperity will continue to grow or be taken away from them.

Michal said that incomes must rise faster than prices, as a wealthier Estonia can invest more in education, healthcare, a cleaner environment and a better quality of life.

"No other party in Estonia stands as firmly for the economy, national defense, liberal principles, Estonian-language education and culture, and European values," he said. "These are the foundations of Estonia's future."

'A clear course for the future'

The Reform Party also unveiled its campaign slogan: "A clear course for the future."

Tartu mayor and party council chair Urmas Klaas said it reflects the party's focus on security, economic growth and opportunities for families and businesses.

He recalled that Reform's "Blue, black and white plan" for Estonia, unveiled in March, centers on building a stronger middle class, bolstering security and making greater use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the economy and government.



"We're running for election to ensure that robust security can give families confidence, people's work and knowledge can create prosperity and technology can help businesses grow and the state operate more efficiently," Klaas said.

MP and Reform Party secretary general Kristo Enn Vaga said the slogan emphasizes that Estonia's future is up to its own choices.

"We in the Reform Party want Estonia to be secure and the economy to grow, because that gives people and businesses more opportunities to carry out their plans," Vaga said. "This is the future we want to build."

World.title: Gallery: Public bomb shelter in Tallinn hidden behind woodland mural
World.content:
A street-level public civil defense shelter in the heart of downtown Tallinn has been transformed with a mural featuring Estonian trees and wildlife.

Located next to Kalev Sports Hall in Tiigiveski Park, the modular concrete shelter cannot withstand a direct missile hit, but it can protect around 20 people from blast waves, shrapnel and debris from an explosion as close as 50 meters away.

Similar shelters are already widely used in Ukraine, including in Kramatorsk.

The concrete module, donated by security company Citysec, is also now fully wrapped in a woodland mural by Colorees Art's Helena Hanni and Vahur Agar, featuring a wild hare, a bear family, an owl in flight and a wolf.

While usually kept closed in peacetime, the shelter was open to visitors on Friday, when officials were on hand to explain its features to the public.

Tallinn unveiled a new street-level civil defense shelter on Juhkentali tänav. October 2026. Source: Ellen Rudi/Tallinn Strategic Management Office

City weighs dozens more shelters

Citysec CEO Eduard Rikkas said the module was developed on a 50-50 basis with partners in Ukraine, where the design has already been in use for years.

Deputy Mayor Tiit Terik (Center) said the shelter door can be opened remotely during an emergency, and will unlock automatically if power or communications fail.

The shelter door, he added, will be kept locked in peacetime.

Tallinn has mapped 40 to 50 potential sites for similar shelters, with public procurement to follow if the city decides to order more.

According to the manufacturer, the shelter model installed on Juhkentali tänav costs up to €70,000.

World.title: Nearly third of teachers at schools transitioning to Estonian unqualified
World.content:
Nearly a third of teachers at schools transitioning to Estonian lack the required qualifications, as heavy workloads and limited pay make recruitment and retention harder.

When Tallinn's Ehte High School of Humanities switched to Estonian-language instruction in 2024, it hired 17 new teachers. One in three has since left, and the school continues to hire 10–15 more a year to replace both retiring teachers and those who leave due to burnout.

Principal Marika Kranisver said teaching students whose first language is Russian can require more work, as teachers have to adapt materials and bridge students' language gaps. Some end up leaving for schools with more native Estonian-speaking kids.

"I have tremendous respect for the teachers who have taken on this challenge and come to a transitioning school," Kranisver said, acknowledging how much more work it involves than teaching at schools where Estonian is already the main language.

Higher pay has helped attract teachers, but increasing funding constraints are making this harder for schools.

Tartu Jogentaga School principal Alina Braziulene said their school has had to cut the bonus pay for qualified teachers from 20 percent to just 3 percent as state support for Ukrainian students has ended and enrollment is down.

"A third of our students came from Ukraine, and the state used to provide substantial funding to support them," Braziulene explained. "That support is gone now."

Empty classroom in an Estonian school. Photo is illustrative. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

When schools could no longer offer higher pay, some teachers quit. Meanwhile, the number of teachers required to teach in Estonian has grown, but funding has not, further squeezing budgets for bonus pay.

'The workload is killing them'

At Tallinn's Läänemere High School, principal Deniss Presnetsov said bonus pay is important, but the school can't offer it to everyone, especially as some applicants lack the required qualifications.

He said workloads are also taking a toll on teaching staff, who juggle heavy administrative demands, lesson planning and consultations on top of the teaching itself.

"That kind of constant workload is killing them," Presnetsov stressed, adding that it quickly drives young teachers away. "They end up leaving the school after a couple of years. Some leave after just one."

The Ministry of Education and Research recommends training to help teachers work with students with non-Estonian language backgrounds, adding that with the right methods, teaching Russian-speaking students isn't necessarily harder.

World.title: Estonia's Eneli Jefimova sweeps skins event, snags MVP at college swim meet
World.content:
Estonian swim star Eneli Jefimova swept the breaststroke skins event at California college meet Friday, snagging MVP honors, a personal best and a win for alma mater NC State.

Estonian swim star Eneli Jefimova swept the breaststroke skins event at California college meet Friday, snagging MVP honors, a personal best and a win for alma mater NC State.

Jefimova clocked 2:06.19 in the 200-yard breaststroke at the College Swimming League (CSL) meet in Walnut, California, pulling away in the second half to beat Stanford University's Addie Robillard by 2.12 seconds — and shave 0.14 seconds off her previous personal best from February.

Robillard finished in 2:08.31, with teammate Lucy Thomas third in 2:09.67.

NC State's relay win gave the team the right to choose the stroke for the women's knockout skins competition, in which eight swimmers start and the two slowest are eliminated after each round until two remain.

The team picked breaststroke, and Jefimova won every 50-yard round despite having less than two minutes to complete all four, leaving little time to recover.



Jefimova swam the first three rounds in 26.71, 26.89 and 26.68 seconds before clocking her fastest time of 26.65 in the final. Italy's Anita Bottazzo, swimming for Indiana University, finished 0.42 seconds behind.

About 15 minutes later, the Estonian also took second in the 100-yard breaststroke, finishing 0.49 seconds behind Bottazzo with 58.74.

Another 15 minutes on, she helped NC State reach the final of the 4x50-yard medley relay skins event, where the team narrowly lost to Indiana, 1:36.95 to 1:36.18.

'It was so hard, I teared up'

"That was an insane meet!" acknowledged Jefimova, a two-time Olympian and four-time European champion. "I even teared up during the last 50 yards of the relay because it was so hard."

She was pleased with her new 200-yard personal best, saying it showed her endurance was improving. "I showed good speed in the skins," Jefimova said. "And the 100 breastroke? That was just hard!"

North Carolina State University (NC State) won the meet with 544.83 points, well ahead of Indiana's 469.83. Fellow Estonian swimmer Egle Salu's University of California, Berkeley (UC Berkeley) team placed third with 394.33, followed by Stanford with 311.

The season's main event for both Estonians is the short-course world championships in Beijing on December 1–6. Jefimova won bronze in the 100-meter breaststroke at the previous championships.

Estonian swimmers Egle Salu (UC Berkeley) and Eneli Jefimova (NC State) at the College Swimming League (CSL) meet in Walnut, California. October 2026. Source: Estonian Aquatics

World.title: Gallery: Central Estonia's upgraded Mäo junction reopens to traffic
World.content:
Mäo's upgraded highway junction has reopened with five bus stops, two roundabouts and a 30-space parking lot, improving long-distance bus connections in Central Estonia.

A Lux Express bus made the symbolic first stop at Mäo on Friday, marking the completion of construction and the launch of bus service at the junction.

"By Monday morning, ten Lux Express routes en route to Tallinn and another ten en route to Tartu will be stopping here," said Urmas Kupp, executive director of the Järva County Public Transport Center (JÜTK).

Other bus operators are also interested and could begin stopping there as early as November 2.

One key amenity, however, is still missing. Despite assurances at the opening that the upgraded junction is safer and ready to accommodate long-distance buses, passengers have no proper public bathroom at Mäo, with only a temporary portable toilet installed next to one of the bus shelters.

The Transport Administration says building a passenger terminal is not its responsibility.

A portable toilet next to one of the bus stops at the updated Mäo junction in Central Estonia. October 2026. Source: Olev Kenk/ERR

"Our job is to maintain and develop national roads," said Transport Administration director general Priit Sauk, adding that it's up to public transport centers and local governments to build stops and passenger terminals.

JÜTK plans to sell an unused terminal and use the proceeds to build a new one at Mäo, which would also solve the bathroom problem. Infrastructure Minister Kuldar Leis (Reform) said the project should be a joint effort with the state.

"I think the most logical approach for projects like this is for the state and local governments to work together," Leis said.

Next stretch of Tallinn–Tartu Highway roadwork begins

Friday also marked the start of reconstruction on an eight-kilometer stretch of Tallinn–Tartu Highway between Käsukonna and Imavere. The work, expected to take about two years, includes a multilevel interchange at Imavere that will connect traffic from Viljandi to the highway.

Sauk said another 15 to 16 kilometers between Mäo and Käsukonna also need rebuilding.

"It's included in our road maintenance plan and long-term plans," he noted. "If the next funding period allows, we'd like to get started on it within the next couple of years."

The updated Mäo junction in Central Estonia. October 2026. Source: Karli Saul/Transport Administration

World.title: Estonia, Latvia at odds over cross-border wind farm
World.content:
A hybrid wind farm under construction in northern Latvia is stirring tensions across the border, where nearby Estonian villages are facing the greater impact.

Utilitas Wind is building Lode Hybrid Park just across the border in Latvia, with 18 wind turbines and battery storage, and company executives say the site was chosen largely for its connection to the third electricity interconnection between Estonia and Latvia.

The Lode project is the first wind farm to be built directly on the border.

Earthworks are underway near Arakste, where the first foundations have been poured and equipment ordered. The park is expected to start generating electricity in about a year, with full completion planned for the first half of 2028.

The €200 million project also includes battery storage, and Utilitas hopes to build four additional turbines on the Estonian side as well.

"We have 18 wind turbines, along with battery storage capable of delivering 60 megawatts (MW) of power for four hours," said Utilitas Group CEO Priit Koit.

He said the entire complex is connected to the third Estonian-Latvian power link, "so electricity can flow in either direction depending on where demand is higher."

100 trucks a day

Latvia's Ministry of Climate and Energy says the project will bring local economic benefits.

"Up to €300,000 a year will go to the municipality and local residents," said ministry parliamentary secretary Einars Cilinskis, emphasizing that people will see economic benefits and regional development spurred by the wind farm.

But construction has also brought disruption to nearby Estonian villages. For the next six months, around 100 big trucks a day are expected to pass through the usually quiet village of Penuja, hauling sand and gravel from Estonia.

New speed limit signs have been installed and truck drivers are being careful, but a road originally intended to support tourism in the area is now carrying mainly construction traffic.

"We have a very good working relationship with the developer," said Penuja resident Reet Paju. "Some residents do object, of course, but since we had no say in the decision to build the wind farm, we have to accept it."

Mulgi Municipality tried to challenge the project in a Latvian court but lost, as Estonian local governments have no legal standing to appeal decisions made by Latvian ones.

'Too many wind farms'

Local leaders, however, say the concern extends beyond Lode, with several other wind farm projects planned in the wider area.

"This isn't just about the Lode wind farm, but wind farms more broadly," said Mulgi Municipal Mayor Imre Jagomäe.

He pointed to eight potential turbine sites in his municipality, two projects in neighboring Saarde Municipality and a planned development on the Latvian side in Ipiķi.

"Clearly, that's just too many wind farms for this area," he stressed.

With the municipality's support, the nonprofit Looduse ja Inimeste Eest is conducting environmental studies in the area.

"Underway and also partially completed are environmental studies of birdlife, bats and ecological coherence," said board member Urmas Maranik.

Lode Hybrid Park is expected to produce enough electricity to meet the annual needs of 110,000 households.

World.title: Canceled school trips abroad leave dozens of families chasing refunds
World.content:
Dozens of families in Estonia say they are out thousands of euros for canceled school language-learning trips abroad, with one organizer still owing about €50,000 in refunds.

Twelve students from Jüri School were due to travel to Spain this fall through organizer Gerri Vihman and his company Keeleõppereisid OÜ. Each family paid €1,260 for flights, host-family accommodation, language classes in Madrid and insurance.

According to one parent, everything seemed fine until their latest meeting with Vihman, where concerns were raised about his previous issues organizing trips, including a canceled trip to England for Lagedi School.

Asked whether the same thing could happen to them, Vihman replied that he had learned from his mistakes. Concerns grew, however, when Vihman failed to send the families their plane tickets and then canceled the trip.

When teachers inquired whether parents could book the kids' flights themselves, Vihman reportedly said he could not refund them because the money was gone. The parents later learned that he had made no payments in Spain either.

"We realized he had probably planned from the start to steal our money, or that this was fraud," one parent told ERR.

In all, Vihman had collected €15,120 from the Jüri School students' families.

Organizer: All but last two trips paid back

Vihman told ERR that he has organized language trips for nearly 20 years and has never deliberately canceled a trip to keep customers' money.

Every business, he said, has its ups and downs, and most trips have gone smoothly. Over the years, he has canceled seven organized trips for various reasons.

"Sometimes people have canceled by choice, sometimes I've had to cancel myself," Vihman said, admitting that there have certainly also been shortcomings in financial management involved.

Even so, he said he has refunded all but the two most recent canceled trips.

"I am working on the refund process, but everything takes time," the organizer said, adding that he has already been in touch with the Consumer Protection and Technical Regulatory Authority (TTJA).

About 40 students' families are still waiting for refunds totaling roughly €50,000.

Vihman also confirmed "in the interest of honesty and transparency" that a Tartu school's trip had been canceled under similar circumstances.

"Lessons learned, and we need to address the situation and work with the parties involved, whether that's the TTJA or the police," he said.

No stranger to consumer regulator

The TTJA's Consumer Disputes Committee has received four complaints this year involving Keeleõppereisid OÜ, said Margot Leen, a consumer rights adviser at the authority. Two consumers received refunds, one withdrew their complaint and one case remains under review.

In 2024, the committee received 10 complaints involving another Vihman-owned company, Keelereisid Eesti OÜ. Five consumers received refunds, four withdrew their complaints and one case was closed because the consumer did not provide the information missing from their complaint.

"Consumers are entitled to a refund if they have paid for a trip and then the organizer confirms it has been canceled," Leen said.

Consumers should first submit a written complaint clearly stating what they want. If the company fails to respond within 15 days or the consumer is dissatisfied with the response, they can turn to the Consumer Disputes Committee.

In contractual disputes, final decisions can be made either by the committee or in court.

Two troubled companies

Before buying anything or signing a contract, consumers can check whether a company is listed as noncompliant with the Consumer Disputes Committee.

Business register records show that Vihman owns both Keeleõppereisid OÜ, registered in 2013, and Keelereisid Eesti OÜ, registered in 2024. Neither company has submitted all required annual reports, and Keelereisid Eesti OÜ's latest filed report showed no sales revenue and a loss of €124,022 in 2023.

Under the Tourism Act, travel companies must not only register their activity with the register of economic activities but also maintain sufficient financial security to cover obligations such as customer refunds if they become insolvent, said Diana Lints, head of the TTJA's Services Supervision Office.

The authority launched supervisory proceedings against Keeleõppereisid OÜ on April 30, issued a precept over its failure to meet the financial security requirement and issued the company a penalty fine.

Schools say earlier trips went smoothly

Jüri School principal Triinu Luiga said the school had acted only as an intermediary for the planned Spain trip, with teachers recommending the organizer to parents who paid the company directly.

"The school had previously taken five successful language trips with companies run by the same person," she said, adding that the teacher involved had also run a background check on the organizer and found no obvious warning signs.

Luiga said the teacher eventually contacted the Madrid school directly to confirm whether the arrangements were still in place, only to learn that Vihman had not been in touch with them at all.

She said the company sent parents a letter on October 14 promising refunds within 14 days.

he school is seeking help from a municipal lawyer but has not filed a police report; because parents paid the company directly, they must file any reports themselves.

Lagedi School principal Oliver Hoole said his school had taken six trips with Vihman without any issues, however a trip planned for this spring was canceled about a week before departure. Vihman told the school that the host language school could no longer accommodate the students.

"Sixteen students were supposed to go, and so far, half of them have gotten their money back," Hoole said, adding that one parent had paid more than €1,000 for the trip.

World.title: Estonia's Soviet-era summer cottage culture to become museum exhibit
World.content:
Built to strict Soviet rules, they stand apart from what came before and after, embodying both state leisure and private dreams.

Nearly 50,000 were built between 1950 and 1980. Now art historians from the Estonian Academy of Arts and ethnologists from the University of Tartu have joined forces to understand this heritage — what people built, and how they spent their time there.

The classic Soviet-era suvila design followed very strict dimensions. Source: ERR

"The privately owned summer cottage is a type of building constructed en masse during the Soviet era that shows how the state sought to create opportunities for working citizens to enjoy leisure time," said Epp Lankots, dean of EKA, on "Tähelepanu! Tegemist on teadusega."

Dagmar Ingi, head of rural architecture at the Estonian Open Air Museum, stressed the human-centered approach. "For me as an ethnologist, it is extremely important that we study the person and their relationship with their summer cottage," she said.

Another standard suvila design was this A-frame variety. Source: ERR

The researchers spend their summers across Estonia, talking to owners and documenting history. Interviews are free-form, closer to conversation than survey. They examine the whole property — garden beds, small structures, interiors — and spatial specialists measure and draw up plans. "We photograph them if people allow us to, inspect the interiors and draw up site plans so that, at some point, if someone wants to study this subject, all this material will have been properly preserved," Ingi said.

They also dig into archives for rare types, like terraced summer cottages. Owners bring out old photo albums, receipts and construction plans kept for decades — insight into everyday building practices and people's ingenuity.

A more idiosyncratic design of suvila. Source: ERR

The researchers approach every participant without prejudice. "For us, it does not matter what work they do or what kind of life they have lived. Every person's story is important, significant and interesting precisely as they have lived it," Ingi said.

The work is limited by time and the subjectivity of memory. Decades-old events arrive filtered through nostalgia, lending emotional color but diminishing factual accuracy.

The knowledge won't gather dust. "The aim of this project is actually to find a Soviet-era summer cottage that can be relocated to the Open Air Museum, where we can tell the story of a summer cottage built in the 1960s or 1970s, together with the story of the person who owned it, what they dreamed of and what they needed the summer cottage for," Ingi concluded.

World.title: 52nd OIC Council of Foreign Ministers convenes in Baghdad with 55 nations
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The 52nd session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) officially opened in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, on Saturday, October 17, 2026. Convening under the banner of advancing regional solidarity, peace, and sustainable development, the two-day summit brings together diplomatic delegations representing 55 member states and observer nations.

The spokesperson for the 52nd ministerial session, Ambassador Hassanein Kamil, announced in a formal statement that proceedings commenced following the arrival of all participating international delegations in Baghdad.

The commencement follows an announcement by the Iraqi Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Friday confirming the completion of all logistical, technical, and security arrangements required to host the high-profile multilateral convention, which runs through October 17–18.

Baghdad’s stewardship of the OIC foreign ministers’ summit reinforces Iraq’s proactive diplomatic posture aimed at bridging regional divides and serving as a neutral convening hub for dialogue.

Ministerial agendas across the two-day meetings are set to address collective security frameworks, cross-border economic integration, humanitarian response mechanisms, and coordinated diplomatic strategies to de-escalate ongoing conflicts across the wider Islamic world.

World.title: AI is coming for every company, Nvidia boss says
World.content:
Stockholm – Artificial intelligence will ultimately become a key aspect of all companies, the head of AI chip giant Nvidia said during a visit to Stockholm, where he urged Europe to ramp up its AI industry.

“Every single company will be an AI company eventually. Every single industry will be impacted by AI,” Jensen Huang told an event late Thursday, part of a European tour that includes a Nvidia-hosted conference in Berlin next week.

“The important thing for us is to recognise that Europe needs to build out the entire stack,” he said, referring to the AI technology chain from data centres to chatbots and other apps.

Speaking later to AFP, Huang said his company had invested $8 billion in Europe over the past year.

“We’ve strategically invested in different parts of that ecosystem, really high quality companies that we believe could help lift it, the whole ecosystem in Europe,” he said, citing the British data centre and AI cloud provider Nscale and the Dutch cloud provider Nebius as examples.

“In the last one year, we’ve invested $8 billion already. We have another couple of billion dollars in the pipeline,” he added. “We’re helping Europe create the AI ecosystem.”

Huang was in Stockholm for the launch of Sferical One, a Swedish supercomputer using Nvidia chips that will keep sensitive Swedish data and expertise in the country.

During his visit, Volvo Cars also announced it was expanding its partnership with Nvidia to improve safety technology in its planned self-driving vehicles.

World.title: Chelsea captain James has knee surgery
World.content:
London – Chelsea captain Reece James has undergone successful knee surgery, the Premier League club announced on Friday.

The England international has missed Chelsea’s past two league games — a 3-0 defeat by Brentford and a 5-1 win over Bournemouth.

“The 26-year-old was absent from Saturday’s 5-1 victory over Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge while medical assessments took place following the injury suffered in training,” the club said in a statement.

“Those assessments confirmed surgery would be the required course of action.

“Reece has already begun his road to recovery and will be supported by the club’s medical department at Cobham during this rehabilitation phase.”

Chelsea are sixth in the Premier League ahead of Saturday’s visit to Everton.

World.title: Asian stocks rise as tech bounces from rout, Warsh upbeat on AI
World.content:
Hong Kong – Most Asian markets bounced Friday after the previous day’s tech rout fuelled by concerns over the AI boom, which Federal Reserve boss Kevin Warsh said offered huge benefits to the global economy.

Seoul and Tokyo enjoyed healthy gains in early exchanges boosted by chipmakers SK hynix and Kioxia, after having been pummelled Thursday as investors bailed out of the once-dominant AI sector.

The selling had been fuelled by forecast-beating US inflation data that ramped up bets on Fed interest rate hikes, as well as concerns about the financial health of data centre operator CoreWeave owing to its huge debt pile.

The New Jersey firm — which has borrowed heavily to finance hefty purchases of pricey semiconductor chips from Nvidia — tanked 15.5 percent Wednesday in the US as yields on some of its bonds soared, reflecting heightened angst over its future.

That added to concerns about the whole AI-tech complex, but Nvidia chief Jensen Huang on Thursday lifted spirits by defending the company and its health.

“CoreWeave’s strength is improving every day,” he told Bloomberg. “I’m optimistic. Their cost of capital is actually decreasing.”

CoreWeave’s shares climbed almost six percent.

Huang’s “defence of CoreWeave’s financial position was enough to pull the NeoCloud complex off the floor, drag AI equities higher and give the broader market something resembling a pulse”, wrote SPI Asset Management’s Stephen Innes.

“One moment the market was pricing the possibility that the AI financing machine had started eating its own tail, the next it was listening to the high priest of the boom explain that the patient was getting stronger.

“AI Jesus had entered the trading room and, for a while at least, the machines found religion again.”

Seoul jumped more than two percent and Tokyo around 1.8 percent, though they slumped 7.6 percent and 4.9 percent respectively Thursday.

Hong Kong, Shanghai, Singapore, Taipei, Mumbai, Bangkok and Manila were also up.

Paris and Frankfurt opened higher but London fell.

Fed chief Warsh said Friday that AI was the “most consequential change” to the global economy in his lifetime, predicting its effects would be positive but the path forward “bumpy”.

At an event at the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok he said the AI investment boom would drive prices up in the short term, but “there really is, I think, a huge benefit to the global economy, to the US economy over the horizon”.

He also reiterated his previously stated belief that the technology would “make economies and countries that put it to good use more productive”.

But he added: “The path from where we are to there is likely to be a very bumpy one, bumpy in our understanding of the technology, bumpy because we really don’t know what the market structure is going to be of these new technologies.”

Shares in Jakarta tanked more than 11 percent — its heaviest loss since 1998 — after index compiler MSCI said it was “no longer appropriate” to maintain Indonesia’s emerging-market status, fuelling fears of an exodus of foreign investment.

The US firm said earlier this year that investors had raised concerns about “ongoing opacity in shareholding structures” as well as co-ordinated trading behaviour that affected price information.

Authorities said they had carried out changes but MSCI said Friday that investors had indicated the “sufficient progress has not been observed consistently across the Indonesian equity market”, adding “it considers Indonesia’s continued classification as an Emerging Market no longer appropriate”.

World.title: Trump’s new press secretary says China lacked ‘proper’ toilets
World.content:
Washington – White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia, who was appointed less than a week ago, said China lacked “proper toilets” in an interview that aired on Thursday.

Zacharia, 41, is already under scrutiny over her legal credentials, after giving an inconclusive answer about where she had passed the bar exam, a prerequisite for practicing law in the United States.

The press secretary, who previously lived in China, recalled in an interview that the perception in 2016 was that China would soon overtake the United States.

“We were all being told Hillary (Clinton) was going to win. The golden days or the glory days of America were over. That China was on the horizon,” Zacharia told right-wing influencer Jack Posobiec.

“I remember this very distinctly, having just come from China, thinking, ‘How is China the next country on the horizon? They don’t even have proper toilets,” she added.

There was no immediate comment from Chinese authorities.

Trump has boasted about his “great relationship” with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

During a Washington summit in September, the two leaders discussed topics ranging from AI and trade to the stalled war in Iran, and confirmed that they would meet for a third and fourth time this year.

Zacharia held her first White House press briefing on Tuesday and only answered questions from three journalists.

She succeeded Karoline Leavitt, a loyal Trump supporter and often combative spokesperson, who stepped down in August to care for her young children.

Zacharia has described herself as a lawyer and listed herself as general counsel of a California-based conservative nonprofit. She also said she had worked at a law firm in Beijing.

Asked about her legal background on Thursday, Zacharia said she had registered to take the bar exam but was then “distracted and overwhelmed” by plans to move with her husband to China.

Zacharia said that she did not retake the bar exam upon returning to the United States due to the birth of her first child.

World.title: Indonesian stocks dive 11% as MSCI weighs market reclassification
World.content:
Jakarta – Indonesian stocks plunged more than 11 percent Friday as index compiler MSCI said it was “no longer appropriate” to maintain the country’s emerging-market status, fuelling fears of an exodus of foreign investment.

The US firm said earlier this year that investors had raised concerns about “ongoing opacity in shareholding structures” as well as co-ordinated trading behaviour that affected price information.

Authorities in Jakarta said in April they had completed reforms, hoping to avoid the downgrade, which could deal a blow to government efforts to kickstart Southeast Asia’s biggest economy, and have a significant impact on investment decisions.

But on Friday MSCI said investors had indicated the “sufficient progress has not been observed consistently across the Indonesian equity market”.

“Despite the announced reforms, significant concerns remain around market dysfunction, including continued suspected coordinated trading behaviour and lack of evidence of meaningful enforcement.

“Accordingly, MSCI considers Indonesia’s continued classification as an Emerging Market no longer appropriate and is launching a consultation on a proposal to reclassify Indonesia as a Standalone Market.”

“A reclassification to Frontier Markets would not properly recognise the depth of the market problems,” it said.

A standalone classification could force investment funds tracking the MSCI’s emerging market indexes to sell Indonesian holdings.

Argentina, Lebanon and Palestine are among the markets with the designation, with none in Asia, according to Bloomberg.

The Jakarta Composite Index collapsed eight percent at the open, sparking a trading halt. When trading resumed it was down 11.1 percent, its heaviest fall since early 1998 and sitting at its lowest level since 2020.

The index has now fallen more than 40 percent since the start of the year.

– Rupiah weakens –

In reaction to the news, the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) said it “respects MSCI’s independence in assessing and determining market classification based on its proprietary methodology”.

“However, considering the various progress and reform measures that have been taken, the IDX will request further clarification from MSCI regarding the basis for the considerations and assessments behind this announcement.

“We also need to emphasise that this MSCI announcement is still part of the consultation process, with input being accepted until April 30, 2027, and does not constitute a final decision.”

The rupiah dropped about 0.8 percent against the dollar to sit at around around 18,060, having hit 18,209 in June, its weakest level on record.

Erwin Gunawan Hutapea, the Indonesian central bank’s head of monetary management and securities, said the bank would take action to ensure stability of the rupiah, which had already tumbled around eight percent this year to a record low.

“Amid rising global risk-off sentiment, which has driven US dollar strengthening and put pressure on domestic financial markets, capital outflows from domestic portfolio assets are expected to continue.

“Bank Indonesia is committed to maintaining a presence in the market to uphold Rupiah exchange rate stability in line with its fundamentals and to ensure that market mechanisms function properly.”

The central bank had carried out several rate hikes earlier in the year to shore up the rupiah, after it came under pressure over the state of Southeast Asia’s biggest economy.

The bank is due to hold its next monetary policy meeting on Wednesday.

New York-based MSCI produces international indexes used by investors as a benchmark to balance their portfolios.

It has a significant impact on investment decisions through its flagship emerging markets index, which contains 1,200 companies with a market capitalisation more than $10 trillion.

Fund managers worldwide keep a close eye on what countries are included or excluded in MSCI’s indexes as that can trigger adjustments to their portfolios.

World.title: Iraq’s parliament approves new cabinet ministers
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — On Thursday, Iraq’s parliament confirmed 11 cabinet nominees and three deputy prime ministers, including Laith al-Khazali, a key member in Iran-backed Asaib Ahl al-Haq who faces US terrorist sanctions.

The nomination is a politically risky decision for Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi, whose administration is dealing with strained regional ties and severe economic challenges as a result of the continuing US-Israeli war against Iran.

Al-Khazali is the brother of Qais al-Khazali, the commander of Asaib Ahl al-Haq, which Washington listed as a foreign terrorist organization in 2020.

Both brothers were classified as specially designated global terrorists, and the US Treasury sanctioned them individually in 2019 for suspected participation in violence against Iraqi demonstrators.

Their US designations also included references to assaults on American troops, such as a 2007 operation that killed five US soldiers.

The parliamentary decision raises concerns about al-Khazali’s nomination and its ramifications for Baghdad’s relationship with Washington, especially as al-Zaidi wants to reinforce Iraq’s sovereignty and manage ties with neighboring nations.

Al-Zaidi has declared a significant depreciation of the Iraqi dinar, warning that the government confronts unprecedented economic and security problems.

The presence of a US-sanctioned militia member in the government’s high leadership may hamper Baghdad’s attempts to preserve fruitful relations with Washington.

World.title: ‘Mixed feelings’: AI cracks centuries-old ciphers
World.content:
Tokyo – Napoleon Bonaparte ordered the wartime missive written in code, creating a puzzle that went unsolved for more than 200 years — until AI cracked it in a matter of hours.

Artificial intelligence is helping non-specialists unlock the secrets of historical sources, a trend described as a “turning point” in a field previously the preserve of scholars and dedicated hobbyists.

One new sleuth is Carter Church, a 27-year-old AI engineer who decrypted a 19th-century letter to one of Napoleon’s generals.

Without digital tools, the task could have taken weeks, but the latest model from ChatGPT-maker OpenAI broke the cipher in just six hours.

“What AI mostly brings is persistence,” Church told AFP, saying he felt “an unbelievable sense of satisfaction and excitement when I saw the result”.

The message from 1809 — detailing French and allied troops’ positions in two dozen lines of symbols, numbers and letters — had lain ignored in an online academic archive.

Because traditional, low-tech methods to crack ciphers are effective but time- and labour-intensive, historians “have more important problems to solve, so many ciphers like this often sit unattended”, said Church.

To find the solution, Church, who works at US cybersecurity firm SentinelOne, needed to learn “very little” about code-breaking techniques or the historical period.

He spent some evenings going over it, then consulted Japanese patent engineer Satoshi Tomokiyo, who maintains an online list of unsolved ciphers, to verify it.

“2026 will be remembered as a turning point for codebreaking of historical ciphers,” Tomokiyo wrote on his website Cryptiana, a go-to resource for the small but enthusiastic global community of amateur cryptographers.

– ‘Mixed feelings’ –

Researchers were already developing AI models to break ciphers, but the public release of state-of-the-art generalist tools has unleashed dozens of new solutions.

Although Church used OpenAI’s most powerful model, GPT-6 Astra, other people have used top offerings from rival US lab Anthropic instead.

Tomokiyo said that since mid-September, most of the ciphers on his list have been cracked using AI.

“There remain some tough problems” which could stay an enigma for years to come, because there is less relevant data available to help AI figure them out, the 58-year-old told AFP.

“I’m excited long-time problems are now solved, but on the other hand, I have mixed feelings, because AI seems to have solved these difficult problems so easily,” he said.

With technology draining the satisfaction of being first to crack a cipher, a fellow code-breaker told Tomokiyo: “I feel useless.”

AI is surpassing human abilities in pursuits from mathematics to computer programming, while threatening to alter or even eradicate many jobs.

The technology is transforming the work of historians not only by decoding documents, but also by analysing millions of medieval manuscripts or helping read ancient scrolls.

Too fragile to be unrolled without risking destruction, the Herculaneum Papyri — hundreds of papyrus scrolls carbonised in the eruption of Vesuvius in 79 AD — are now being X-rayed and analysed by AI to reveal the hidden writing inside.

Researchers in Italy announced in June the first complete virtual unrolling of a scroll, which turned out to be a treatise on ethics.

– ‘Facebook of the past’ –

AI is also being used to build a huge, searchable collection of previously inaccessible sources on Jewish history and culture by transcribing 10 million pages of Hebrew manuscripts.

“It’s gigantic. No human being could process such a quantity” of data, said project leader Daniel Stoekl Ben Ezra, of the Ecole Pratique des Hautes Etudes in Paris.

Researchers hope the databases created using the digitised text — which he likens to a kind of “huge Facebook of the past” — could help bring to light links between people, places and ideas.

And at the French capital’s Notre Dame Cathedral, an AI system has been trained to transcribe 14,600 Latin pages from the church’s medieval archives — a task not dissimilar to code-breaking.

“These are minutes drawn up by notaries who abbreviate their decisions. The script is highly administrative, very pragmatic… with rather technical vocabulary,” said historian Julie Claustre, who leads the e-NDP project.

With character recognition rates ranging between 88 and 94 percent, the project has revealed information about the cathedral’s daily life, its building work, its staff and the care of abandoned children.

Doing the same by hand would take “several decades”, said Claustre, but “it’s not just a time-saver”.

Automation enables “inquiries that were not previously possible; it transforms the conditions of research.”

World.title: Prices of 137 cancer drugs to fall by up to 70% from November 9
World.content:
In good news for cancer patients, prices of 137 drugs are set to be reduced by up to 70% from Nov 9, with govt capping trade margins by 30%. Drug prices regulator National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) Saturday notified the 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs to address the issue of excessive trade margins, invoking Paragraph 19 of DPCO, 2013.

Significantly, patented drugs are also included in the list.

The trade margin rationalisation at 30% of MRP, excluding GST, corresponds to a mark-up of 42.9% on price to stockist/price to distributor (PTS/PTD), according to the minutes of the NPPA meeting accessed by TOI. Simply put, PTS/PTD is the first point of sale of the drug.

This follows a nudge by Supreme Court, flagging the huge gap between price to retailer and MRP of medicines billed to patients, in certain cases of 10 times.

The MRPs of certain drugs â including pertuzumab + trastuzumab, atezolizumab, teclistamab, inotuzumab ozogamicin and daratumumab â are up to Rs 5 lakh per vial/pack.

All manufacturers will be required to inform NPPA of their revised prices within seven days of publication of the gazette notification. Manufacturers will be req-uired to display the price lists on their website and widely disseminate them to all retailers and hospitals, with the latter also required to display the revised prices on their websites prominently.





The authority approved the calculation of the revised MRP based on PTS/PTD for March 2026 as the reference month.

NPPA said patient assistance programme quantities may be excluded from the calculation of PTS/PTD and MRP for trade-margin capping only. These programmes, where drugs are supplied free of cost, are typically run by MNCs.

As a substantial supply of anti-cancer drugs is directly made to hospitals and medical institutions, they shall be responsible for ensuring revised prices of such drugs from the date of implementation, NPPA said.

State drug controllers will take necessary steps to ensure compliance by manufacturers, dealers including retailers, hospitals and medical institutions, it added.

In a bid to tighten rules further, NPPA said uninterrupted availability of the covered formulations needed to be ensured. Any manufacturer intending to reduce monthly production levels would have to obtain permission.

Consumers can use the Pharma Sahi Daam app and NPPA website to check revised prices of drugs, an official release said.

In 2019, the MRP of 526 brands of non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines was reduced by up to 90%, NPPA said. The present exercise extends this approach to a larger set of drugs, based on the list recommended by an expert committee under Directorate General of Health Services.

World.title: Internet is fundamental right of all, even children: Supreme Court
World.content:
It said the efficacy of such restrictive measures remains far from established in countries which have imposed them.

SC: Internetâs value priceless, efficacy of curbs not proved

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Raising citizensâ right to access and use of internet to the level of fundamental right, Supreme Court has held that even children are entitled to that right and said it does not endorse imposing in the name of safety a blanket ban on children accessing internet. At the same time, it favoured restricting access to content that is inherently harmful to kids.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Chandran said that right to access and use of the internet is part of Article 21 (right to life and liberty) and Article 19(1)(a) (freedom of speech and expression). The internet is âpricelessâ as it provides access to information and education to all in even remote areas, where it is often the only source of learning for many children. Noting that the SC had earlier refrained from expressing a definitive view on whether the right to access the internet is, by itself, a fundamental right, the bench said, â. ..we have no hesitation in saying that the right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right of every individual under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution.âSC said, âOur children, irrespective of their age enjoy the same rights, and to deny the same altogether would be as absurd as saying children below a certain age do not have a conscience worth protecting or freedom of speech worth expressing.âThe order was passed on a public interest litigationfiled by NGO âJust Rights for Children Allianceâ, which highlights continued lapses by intermediaries in tackling child sexual exploitation and abuse material (CSEAM) despite SCâs 2024 judgment in this regard.Agreeing with its plea, SC said there has been âno progress worth the nameâ in the last two years.Acknowledging that there has been âa growing yet short-lived tendency across the globe in the recent past to limit the access of children below a certain age to the internet, more particularly to social media platforms,â SC said, âwe too gave this our anxious consideration, and only thereafter, we decided consciously not to endorse the sameâ.It said the efficacy of such restrictive measures remains far from established in countries which have imposed them.â... Children do not cease to use the internet merely because the law prohibits them from doing so ... They move to other platforms and websites that are unregulated and even more unsafe,â SC said.âAll that we are trying to say is that any blanket restriction on access to internet by children is nothing more than unproven measures of proven disproportionality. No jurisdiction has, so far, been able to demonstrate that children are any safer on account of such measures,â it said.It said some age-based restrictions and safeguards should exist for the safety of children online.

World.title: SC panel opens web portal for complaints on July NEET protests
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The high-powered enquiry committee (HPEC) set up by SC to examine all aspects of the violent incidents that broke out during the anti-NEET paper leak protests in Delhi and beyond in July, has launched a dedicated portal for people affected by the violence, including the police personnel deployed at the protest sites, to upload their complaints and representations.

The identity of the complainants/informants shall be kept confidential if they so wish.

The panel shall examine all issues enumerated by SC in its orders dated August 18 and Sept 10. is designed in such a manner as to enable due protection to vulnerable witnesses and also to keep the identities confidential and undisclosed, if so wished by the affected persons. Two months after students opposed CJI Surya Kantâs presence at the campus, he attended the convocation along with Karnataka CM D K Shivakumar in Bengaluru

NEW DELHI: Two months after students of National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru, opposed his presence on the campus, CJI Surya Kant addressed them at the convocation ceremony and said the legal profession is not for the faint-hearted as it demands intellectual independence coupled with fairness and hearing a person before judging.Delivering the âPresidential address of the Chancellorâ on Saturday at the convocation, which was postponed after students and alumni of NLSIU opposed his presence, CJI Kant said the university, regarded as âHarvard of the Eastâ, has âwitnessed its fair share of quad parties and impromptu flash mobs in the courtyard!â Shifting to the serious task, he said the legal profession demands not only the mastery of statutes but also the courage to defend what is just, and the humility to listen to the voices that get drowned in cacophony.CJI Surya Kant at NLSIU said legal profession demands humility to listen to the voices that get drowned in cacophony.âThis intellectual independence also calls for fairness: hearing before judging, distinguishing a person from a position and disagreeing without denying another personâs dignity,â he said.He said the purpose of legal education is to enable law graduates to explore the situations beyond criminal and constitutional laws and gain experience from myriad real-life situations where many comprehend the world very differently than ourselves.âLaw will challenge your patience, test your ethics, and call upon the deepest reserves of your courage. But it will also reward you with the singular joy of service â the serene satisfaction of righting a wrong, the pride of defending liberty, and the honour of upholding the Constitution,â he said.Advising the students on the challenges that lie ahead of them in the challenging legal profession, the CJI said, âAs you leave this campus, you step not only into a profession but into a calling.â

World.title: 19 killed in Kolkata stampede; CM Suvendu announces jobs, Rs 25 lakh for kin
World.content:
Adhikari added that a fact-finding committee would be constituted to investigate the incident

'Appropriate measures against those who failed to manage crowd'

'Some attempting to politicise this, but it will be to no avail'

'An announcement by the organisers' led to the rush

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday announced a compensation of Rs 25 lakh and a government job for the family of each person killed in a stampede at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata.The state government will also bear the entire cost of medical treatment for the injured and provide Rs 5 lakh to each of them, Adhikari said, adding that a fact-finding committee would be constituted to investigate the incident."This is a tragic incident. 19 people have lost their lives, 17 of whom died on the spot... 25 people have been injured; 24 of them are out of danger, while one remains in critical condition," the chief minister said. He added that the government was making every possible effort to assist the affected families and that he had personally met relatives of the deceased.Adhikari said the state government would seek the intervention of the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court to constitute a fact-finding committee, which would include special task force (STF) and forensic teams. The investigation would examine the circumstances leading to the stampede and identify those responsible for the crowd management arrangements.Kolkata Police's Anti-Rowdy Section (ARS) has collected CCTV footage from the site, which will be examined as part of the investigation."We will check the footage and take appropriate measures against those who failed to manage the crowd. That could be a member of the puja committee, a homeguard, a temporary worker, a policeman, or a private company security guard. Nobody will be spared," Adhikari said.He said the state government was making arrangements for postmortems in accordance with the law and that six of the deceased had been identified so far. Officials were also coordinating with the families of the victims.The chief minister said the families who had met him had expressed faith in the state government. He added that the Prime Minister's Office had sought a report from the chief secretary, which had been submitted, and that the Centre and the state were working together to provide assistance.Adhikari also criticised the previous state government over its handling of past tragedies, accusing some people of attempting to politicise the current incident."Everyone is well aware of the role of the previous government in similar incidents that occurred in the past. Some are attempting to politicize this, but it will be to no avail. I have met with the families of the deceased, and they have explicitly stated that they have full faith in the Chief Minister and the government... The PMO also requested a report from the Chief Secretary, which we have submitted. The Prime Minister has announced relief and compensation. The central and state governments are working together on this..." he said.Referring to other incidents, Adhikari said 13 people had died due to electrocution during the 2025 Puja season amid heavy rain. He also referred to a devastating flood in north Bengal that killed 100 people, questioning the previous chief minister's response to those tragedies.The stampede occurred on Saturday evening, on Maha Saptami, at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata. At least 19 people died and 25 were injured after a crowd surge amid rain, according to officials.A police officer said people waiting outside the pandal rushed forward as it began raining, causing some to fall on the road and triggering the stampede. Adhikari said an announcement made by the organisers of the community Durga Puja had led to a rush among revellers, resulting in what he described as a "painful incident".Officials of the organising club, private security guards and personnel on duty were detained for questioning, he said. The administration also advised several crowded theme-based puja pandals to temporarily close following the tragedy.Union home minister Amit Shah, who had arrived in Kolkata and was scheduled to visit pandals on Sunday, cancelled his programmes following the incident. President Droupadi Murmu, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Shah and former chief minister Mamata Banerjee expressed condolences over the deaths.PM Modi announced an ex gratia payment of Rs 2 lakh for the next of kin of each deceased person and Rs 50,000 for each injured person. The state government has also launched a toll-free helpline to provide information related to the stampede.

World.title: 'Do something. You can’t die like this': flydubai pilot Capt Smit Machchar recounts cockpit attack
World.content:
MUMBAI: Two hours into the flight from Dubai to Tel Avivi, flydubai commander, Capt Smit Machchar was checking landing time and fuel figures on the computer when something struck hard at the back of his head.

He thought part of his Boeing 737âs cockpit roof had broken loose. Seconds later, as more blows rained in, he turned and saw it was his co-pilot. Bleeding, his vision shrunk to a few inches, he drifted in and out of consciousness during those fateful minutes when the aircraft went into a rapid descent, while the attack continued. âThere was a moment I told myself, Smit, do something, you canât die like this,â said the flydubai pilot, recounting the Sept 30 terror attack on flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv, which was diverted and landed in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.

The pilot said his memory of what followed is fragmented, a gap he is still working through with doctors and psychologists. In his first extended account since the incident, given to Sky News Arabia on Sat evening, Machchar said an ordinary flight, with a co-pilot he was flying with for the first time, turned violent minutes after the man stood up to pray.

It was a route he had flown many times. An augmented crew was on board, and the relief captain was to take over operating duties after landing.





âNormal flight,â he told the channel. âIt went on like a normal day till it wasnât.â

About two hours in, the relief captain had dropped by the cockpit to chat about rosters and flying hours when the co-pilot, who had stepped out for a toilet break, returned. A few minutes into their conversation, he said he wished to pray and asked the relief captain to step out. Machchar said such requests are accepted in the region when the flight is stable.

The co-pilot asked the other Captain to step out, stood up behind him and began praying. âOut of respect, I did not look back. I was checking the landing time and fuel figures on the computer, the routine background tasks of the monitoring pilot. Suddenly there was a very hard hit at the back of my head,â he said. âIt was something very strong and hard. I didnât know at that point what had hit me.â He fell forward, and his mind reached for training.

âMy first thought was, okay, something has broken from the aircraft roof, and it has been a catastrophic damage. I was planning to regain my composure and check my systems.â

The blows kept coming. Within seconds his vision had narrowed to a few inches, he said. When he glanced back, he understood. âHe was saying something while hitting me, but I could not understand.â Machchar unbuckled and tried to shield himself, taking a blow on his hand.

âThatâs when something flipped,â he said. He screamed for the relief captain and, since the door switch was within reach, managed to open it. He lost consciousness for the first time soon after.

He recalled hearing shouting between the co-pilot and the other crew before the door shut again, with the co-pilot threatening to hit them too.

It was after this, he said, that he heard the engines spool down and felt the aircraft pitch into a dive.

âI donât have to see the instruments, I can have my eyes closed and still know the engines are spooling down and the aircraft is going down. Every pilot will tell you this.â

Drifting in and out of consciousness from blood loss, he said, he reached a point of decision. âI told myself, Smit, do something. You canât die like this. Iâm not saying I accepted my death. It was like, do something, otherwise...â The pilot added his memory of what followed is fragmentary, a gap he is still working through with doctors and psychologists.

He said he remembers locking his legs against something and pushing toward the door.

He said he remembers then lying face down between the cockpit and the galley, the door open, passengers panicking.

Machchar credited his colleague for taking the controls and recovering the aircraft, calling it something he will carry âtill I die.â Asked about the speculation over how the plane was saved, he declined to single anyone out.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âEveryone did the best in their capacity,â he said, including crew and passengers.

He said he knew he was out of danger only when the aircraft touched down. Until then a doctor on board and his crew kept him conscious. âAt that point, what I was more focused on was to not give up on life. You say you see flashes and stuff like that (speaking about death). You just remember the person who matters the most,â he said. The first call he made was to his 2-year old son. In the days that followed the incident, he continued to get flashes of the first blow.

The commander added that he has been getting better with each passing day and can now sit and have conversations.

World.title: 'He kept on hitting': Indian flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar reveals what happened mid-flight as he was stabbed
World.content:
Smit Machchhar is recovering in Abu Dhabi

âSmith, do something. You canât die like thisâ

Indian pilot Smit Machchhar who was attacked by his co-pilot aboard a Flydubai flight has recalled how a routine journey turned into a fight for survival, describing the repeated blows to his head, his attempts to call for help and the moments he lost consciousness as the aircraft went into a dive.after he was stabbed by his Omani copilot Hamam Al Hammami who was allegedly trying to crash the plane.In an exclusive 1st news interview after being stabbed, with Sky News Arabia, Captain Smith Machchhar said there had been nothing unusual about the flight until about two hours after take-off. He was carrying out routine checks in the cockpit when the attack began, initially mistaking the first blow to the back of his head for damage to the aircraft.Giving out details as he remembered he said, "when I was just in in the checking my computer for the timing and everything, uh suddenly there was a a very hard hit at the back of my head, right here. And uh it was quite hard and felt that it was something which was very strong."He said he initially thought something had broken off the aircraft's roof and hit him, causing catastrophic damage. Drawing on his training, he tried to regain his composure and check the aircraft's systems. âMy thought process went on that track, that oh, there is a big damage in the aircraft which has hit me at the back,â he said.But within seconds, he realised he was being attacked. âHe kept on hitting,â Machchhar said.He recalled turning around and realising what was happening, although the impact had severely restricted his field of vision.âImmediately, I would say in the next few seconds, my vision was restricted to like few inches,â he said, adding that he learnt about the extent of the impact from doctors later.His first response was to protect himself from further blows. He quickly unbuckled his seatbelt, turned around and tried to block the attack, sustaining an injury to his hand. âAt this point, it was very obvious what was going on,â he said.Machchhar said he immediately tried to get help from another captain who was on board and was expected to operate the return flight. âI was screaming his name and I was trying because the switch was very close to me to open the door. I was trying to just get help in,â he said.He lost consciousness amid the commotion but remembered managing to open the cockpit door. He could hear shouting as the other crew members confronted the co-pilot. âThe door shut immediately after that because he threatened to hit them as well,â Machchhar said.By then, he was struggling to stay conscious and could feel his strength fading because of blood loss. Soon afterwards, he heard the engine sounds change and felt the aircraft go into a dive. âSince Iâve been flying for such a long time, I donât have to see the instruments to figure out or hear the engine to know whatâs happening,â he said.Machchhar said he repeatedly drifted in and out of consciousness but realised he had to fight to survive. âThere was a moment where I realised and I told myself that, âSmith, do something. You canât die like this,ââ he said.His memories of what happened next remain fragmented. He recalled trying to reach the door, bracing his leg against something and pushing himself forward.âThe next memory that I have is the doorâs open and Iâm lying between the cockpit and the galley,â he said. He remembered being face down as panic and shouting continued around him.While Machchhar was fighting to survive, another captain took over the controls and helped save the aircraft. âThe other thing, how my other colleague who took over the controls and saved the day again is commendable. Itâs something that Iâll keep with me till I die,â he said.Asked what he wanted people to understand about the incident amid speculation over how the plane was saved, Machchhar said everyone on board had done what they could.âI think everyone in world everyone in world did the best in their capacity to save the day,â he said. The pilot said the first blow continued to haunt him in the days after the attack.âImmediately after the event, I used to get flashes of the first hit. And trust me, it shook me up for the first few days,â he said, describing how the memory would return suddenly and leave his heart racing.But what stayed with him most was the determination of those on board. âOne thing that I would take away from that day was the determination, the sheer determination of everyone to survive,â he said.Machchhar said he felt out of danger only when the aircraft touched down in Saudi Arabia. By then, a doctor was attending to him in the galley, while crew members worked to keep him conscious.Asked whom he thought of first, he replied: âMy son.â His two-year-old son, wife and daughter live with him in the UAE.Machchhar also expressed gratitude for the medical treatment he received in Saudi Arabia and after being brought back to the UAE. âFrom the first day onwards, the way I was taken care of, the way I was brought back to the UAE, even the care that I was given in Saudi is something I would never forget in my life,â he said.Still recovering from the traumatic incident, he said he felt grateful for the care and support he had received over the preceding two-and-a-half weeks.âGrateful is the word I would say right now,â he said.

World.title: 'Thoughts with those who have lost their loved ones': PM Modi on Kolkata stampede
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday expressed grief over the deaths of 17 people and injuries to 15 others in the Kolkata pandal incident, calling it âextremely distressingâ.

PM Modi also announced an ex-gratia of Rs 2 lakh from the Prime Ministerâs National Relief Fund (PMNRF) for the next of kin of each deceased person and Rs 50,000 for each injured person.

"The stampede in Kolkata is extremely distressing. My thoughts are with those who have lost their loved ones. May the injured recover at the earliest. The local administration is providing all possible assistance to those affected," PM Modi was quoted by PMO on X.

As rain began, people waiting outside the pandal rushed forward, causing some to fall on the road and triggering a stampede, a senior police officer told PTI.

An eyewitness told ANI, âMany people lost consciousness; some were being taken on motorcycles. I witnessed this happening all aroundâwhen people fainted, they were taken away on bikes. All of this took place, and there was a massive crowd as well...â

World.title: Jagan can’t escape from corruption cases, says TDP leader Varla Ramaiah
World.content:
TDP Polit Bureau member Varla Ramaiah said on Thursday that YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy got the investigation into the slew of corruption cases dragged on for 15 years, but he no longer had that luxury as the courts were set to conduct trial on a daily basis.

As a consequence, Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy appeared to be in deep trouble, while the Y.S. Vivekananda Reddy murder probe, as part of which Kadapa MP Y.S. Avinash Reddy was questioned by the Enforcement Directorate for two consecutive days, compounded his woes, he stated.

Addressing the media persons at the TDP central office near Mangalagiri, Mr. Ramaiah said it was the CBI that stated on the basis of concrete evidence that Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy amassed wealth amounting to nearly ₹43,000 crore when his father was the Chief Minister and, as the courts were turning the heat on him, the YSRCP chief was desperate to somehow wriggle out of the dire situation.

He observed that the noose was tightening around Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy’s neck in some other major scandals, and the investigating agencies were zeroing in on the conspirators in the sensational Vivekananda Reddy murder case. The YSRCP chief initially wanted it to be inquired by the CBI, but changed his stand later for reasons best known to him.

The YSRCP was trying its best to vitiate the conduct of the local body elections as it realised that it had little chance of winning the battle, Mr. Ramaiah said, adding that what it feared was bound to happen.

World.title: Ukraine resumes attacks on Russian oil refineries as U.S. relations teeter
World.content:
Ukrainian drones attacked a refinery in Russia's Ryazan region early Thursday, hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that a brief truce spurned by Moscow was over amid deepening tensions with Washington.

The drone strike started a fire at the refinery about 300 kilometres southeast of Moscow, Russia's Defence Ministry and Ryazan Governor Pavel Malkov said. Russia's Astra online news outlet posted what it said was a photograph of the blaze.

A senior Ukrainian official, who spoke on condition of anonymity because he wasn't authorised to speak publicly, confirmed that Ukraine had hit the refinery.

Zelenskyy complains about U.S. stance toward Ukraine

The strike could further complicate Kyiv's relations with US President Donald Trump, which have soured again in recent days.

Mr. Zelenskyy was outraged by Russia's continuing aerial bombardment of his country's energy infrastructure in apparent defiance of Trump's demand on Sunday for both sides to halt those attacks.

The Ukrainian government said that it was heeding the ceasefire, but Kremlin spokeperson Dmitry Peskov said that Ukraine never stopped its strikes on refineries that have hurt Russia. It wasn't possible to independently verify each side's claims.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov labelled Ukraine's strikes on oil facilities as a “direct and crude challenge to President Trump.”

Mr. Zelenskyy complained that, despite going along with Trump's demand for a truce, Ukraine in recent days was denied the usual Western intelligence on Russian ballistic missile strikes and limits were placed on its use of US-made Starlink communication terminals. Both are vital for Ukrainian defences and attack operations.

The Ukrainian leader said that his patience had run out. He said in an interview with the Financial Times published Thursday that Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries would resume. “We're done,” he was quoted as saying.

Mr. Trump made a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to import Russian diesel, despite international efforts to sanction Russia for its invasion and diplomatically isolate Putin.

Mr. Zelenskyy slammed the agreement, saying it would allow Russia to press on with its full-scale invasion of Ukraine that began more than 4.5 years ago. US efforts under Trump to end the war have made no progress.

Mr. Zelenskyy said in an interview late Wednesday (October 14, 2026) with Piers Morgan on the British journalist's YouTube show that he felt betrayed by Trump's deal with Putin, the energy ceasefire announcement and the Starlink operational issues.

“Really, yes, between us,” Mr. Zelenskyy said when asked if he felt betrayed by the American president. “Our country has to survive, and we count on our real partners, strategic partners, the United States and President Trump.”

He said that the U.S. behaviour “was really strange and what was not like between partners but that they switch off Starlink, so some actually crazy steps between us.”

Zelenskyy says U.S. position isn't on the right side of history

In the same interview, Mr. Zelenskyy said “we are losing a strong partner” in the United States. He said that “it's painful when President Trump chooses one side, not our side. But we are OK that he's in the middle.”

Mr. Zelenskyy said someone is pushing Mr. Trump into a stance that is “not the right side of history.”

The Starlink speed limits choked Ukrainian efforts to defend itself and hit back against Russia, Kyiv officials said.

The absence of Western intelligence leaves Ukraine more vulnerable to Russian ballistic missiles. Mr. Trump has said the U.S. hasn't stopped sharing intelligence with Ukraine.

World.title: New China-North Korea bridge opens after more than a decade of delay
World.content:
A new bridge linking China and North Korea opened on Thursday (October 15, 2026) after more than a decade of delay, signalling deeper ties between the two countries.

China's official Xinhua News Agency reported that a ceremony for the launch of the New Yalu River Bridge was held, and an on online video from state media outlet China News Service showed the bridge and trucks waiting on it adorned with the national flags of China and North Korea.

Beijing expected that the four-lane, 3-kilometre (1.8-mile) crossing, which connects the northeastern Chinese city of Dandong to the North Korean city of Sinuiju, would further promote economic, trade and “people-to-people" exchanges.

“The relations between China and North Korea have entered a new stage, embarking on a new chapter,” Chinese Premier Li Qiang said in a video address at the ceremony, Xinhua reported.

Mr. Li said that the crossing would become a new landmark symbolising the two nations' traditional friendship. He hoped both sides would seize the opportunity of the opening to continue to enhance connectivity and explore potential for cooperation in border areas, Xinhua said.

Bridge opens after a 12-year delay

The bridge initially was expected to enter use in 2014, when China had apparently completed construction on its side. But North Korea had not done corresponding work on its side at the time.

The absence of substantial work in Sinuiju fuelled speculation that Pyongyang was wary of becoming more economically dependent on China or displeased with Beijing voting for United Nations resolutions toughening international sanctions on the North over its nuclear program. Some observers suggested North Korea and China also differed over the bridge's location.

The setback over the bridge prompted an unusually sharp report in the Global Times, a newspaper affiliated with the ruling Chinese Communist Party, which quoted Dandong residents expressing frustration over delays in what they had hoped would be an economic boon for their border city.

New link opens a month after launch of Russia-North Korea bridge

Observers said the new bridge would likely boost bilateral trade and enhance logistical efficiency.

It is expected to lessen the burden on an aging bridge on the Dandong-Sinuiju route, which handles more than 70 per cent of official trade between the two countries.

That decades-old bridge carries a railway line as well as cars and trucks, but vehicle traffic can move only one way at a time.

“The new bridge could facilitate trade that violates UN sanctions, but traffic across it could be more transparent and subject to customs than cross-border smuggling,” said Leif-Eric Easley, a professor at Ewha University in Seoul.

The new bridge's launch came about a month after North Korea and Russia opened a road bridge as part of their efforts to cement relations.

Experts say Chinese officials likely felt uneasy about that opening

China has long been North Korea's biggest trading partner and economic pipeline. But in recent years North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has prioritised Moscow, sending thousands of troops and conventional weapons to support Russian President Vladimir Putin's war in Ukraine, apparently in exchange for military and economic assistance.
